CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with DCB for recurrent bulbar urethral stricture is a safe and easy minimally invasive treatment with good short-term results, however success rates are lower than the gold standard treatment of urethroplasty.

title: HIGH CONCENTRATIONS OF PENTOXIFYLLINE AFTER CAPACITATION IMPAIR BOVINE SPERM FUNCTION AND IN VITRO FERTILIZATION OUTCOMES
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Fabiana Mariani Wingert, Carolina Comissoli Fernandes, Sophia Abur Said Shugair, Elisa Weirich Braido, Marta Ribeiro Hentschke, Luciana Keiko Hatamoto Zaervoudakis, Claudio Teloken, Mariangela Badalotti
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In vitro embryo production (IVP) is an essential biotechnology for genetic dissemination and herd productivity. However, cryopreserved semen often compromises fertilization efficiency. Pentoxifylline (PTX), a phosphodiesterase inhibitor, enhances sperm motility in several species and may mitigate cryodamage. This study evaluated whether post-capacitation supplementation with 10 or 20 mm PTX affects sperm function and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes in cattle. METHODS: The study was conducted at a Brazilian Animal Biotechnology and Reproduction Laboratory using semen from four Nelore bulls. Samples were thawed, processed by Percoll gradient (45–90%), and divided into three groups: G1) control, G2) 10 mm PTX, and G3) 20 mm PTX. Sperm motility, vigor, mitochondrial activity, capacitation status, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were assessed. Data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test (p<0.05). RESULTS: Comparing G1 (control), G2 (10 mm PTX), and G3 (20 mm PTX), respectively, post-thaw motility was 51.56 ± 1.54, 51.56 ± 1.54, and 51.56 ± 1.54 (p=1.00), and vigor 2.68 ± 0.08, 2.68 ± 0.08, and 2.68 ± 0.08 (p=1.00). After capacitation, motility declined to 29.53 ± 2.90A, 20.18 ± 2.86B, and 14.62 ± 2.21B(p<0.0001), while vigor dropped to 2.25 ± 0.12A, 1.87 ± 0.12B, and 1.59 ± 0.11B(p=0.0002). PTX did not affect IVF rates (p=0.95) but reduced cleavage at 20 mm (p=0.01) and expanded blastocysts at 10 mm (p=0.04). Degenerative acrosomal reactions increased (p=0.0004), while mitochondrial activity and ROS levels showed no differences (p>0.05). Both PTX concentrations impaired sperm function and embryo development. CONCLUSIONS: PTX at 10 and 20 mm proved detrimental to bovine sperm function, reducing motility, vigor, and acrosomal integrity, and impairing cleavage and blastocyst formation. Although mitochondrial activity and oxidative stress were unchanged, the increased acrosomal degeneration suggests cytotoxicity at high doses. These findings indicate that PTX supplementation after capacitation does not enhance IVF outcomes and may impair sperm performance in a dose-dependent, species-specific manner. Further studies should determine safe concentrations that improve motility without compromising fertilization or embryonic development.

title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF SHEAR WAVE ELASTOGRAPHY FOR RISK STRATIFICATION OF PATIENTS WITH ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION—A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Manoj Kumar, Subranshu Sahu, Chandan J. Das
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is the most common male sexual dysfunction and its prevalence is increasing year after year. The best method to predict the severity of ED is histological assessment of the penile tissue through biopsy. However, its role is limited because of its complexity, invasiveness, and associated serious side effects. Elastography is a new and non-invasive imaging modality used for assessing the stiffness of tissues. Here we aim to find out the penile viscoelasticity(stiffness) of corpora cavernosa with the new and non-invasive diagnostic Shear wave elastography (SWE) and correlate it with the IIEF-5 score. METHODS: We included patients aged18-70 years with erectile dysfunction who are willing to participate in the study. The exclusion criteria are Peyronie's disease, penile trauma, spinal injury, h/o penile surgery, severe psychiatric disorder, patients not willing to undergo SWE, patients with hypogonadism, and carcinoma penis. All included patients were divided into 4 categories according to IIEF-5 scoring (Control-22-25, Mild ED-17-21, Moderate ED-8-16, and Severe ED-5-7). They underwent shear wave elastography of Bilateral corpora cavernosa in flaccid penis in proximal and distal parts separately. They were followed up after 3 months with being treated with PDE5i. The IIEF-5 scores were assessed after 3 months. RESULTS: We evaluated 41 patients (Severe ED-8, Moderate ED-8, Mild ED-9, Control-14) with penile SWE in bilateral corpora cavernosa both proximal and distal part in flaccid penis. From the initiation of the study, we found the mean SWE of patients with severe, moderate and mild ED were 29.14(Standard Deviation 4.0) KPa, 20.08(SD 4.0) KPa and 17.7(SD 4.1) KPa respectively. The mean SWE of normal/control patients without ED is 15.28(SD 3.9) KPa. Patients with mild and moderate with low mean SWE values responded well to PDE5i with 3 months follow up. CONCLUSIONS: This SWE will be a non-invasive objective method which could be highly beneficial from the clinical practice standpoint compared with other modalities like colour Doppler which require intra-cavernosal injection to assess the ED. Our method might have great potential to make a paradigm shift in both the diagnosis and prognosis of ED. This study will be the first of its kind to be undertaken among Indian population.

title: URBAN–RURAL DISPARITIES IN PROSTATE CANCER OUTCOMES: A NATIONWIDE POPULATION-BASED ANALYSIS
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Antonio Flavio Silva Rodrigues, Douglas Padua Rodrigues, Gustavo Santana Lima, Guilherme Miranda Andrade, Rafael Rosa Ergang, Joao Pedro Soares Nunes, Matheus Fagundes Azevedo, Gustavo Romeiro, Fernando Franco Leao, Joao Paulo Barbosa Oliveira
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most common malignancy among Brazilian men, but regional disparities in access to screening and treatment may influence disease burden. Understanding differences between urban and rural regions is crucial for planning equitable public health strategies. Objective: To analyze temporal trends and regional disparities in PCa incidence, mortality, and mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) in Brazil, comparing urbanized and less urbanized regions. METHODS: Population-based data from DATASUS and INCA (2013–2021) were analyzed for men aged≥50 years. Age-specific incidence (PCSIR) and mortality (PCSMR) rates per 10,000 inhabitants were calculated. Regions were classified by degree of urbanization and healthcare infrastructure. Non-parametric Wilcoxon tests compared regional medians, and Joinpoint regression identified temporal trends. Multivariate robust linear regression models assessed associations between MIR and healthcare accessibility indicators (number of treatment centers, GDP per capita, urbanization index, and PSA screening coverage). RESULTS: A total of 273,933 new cases and 135,336 deaths were recorded. Median PCSIR was highest in the Southeast (14.7/10,000) and lowest in the North (6.9/10,000), representing a 113% higher incidence in the most urbanized region. Conversely, MIR was twice as high in the North (0.88) compared to the Southeast (0.44). The Northeast showed the highest mortality (7.7/10,000), 28% higher than the South (6.0/10,000). Joinpoint analysis revealed an incidence rise until 2018 (β=+3.66, p<0.001) followed by a post-2020 decline (β=−2.15, p=0.002). In multivariate models, higher MIR was independently associated with lower urbanization (β=−0.43, p=0.01) and reduced access to radiotherapy and robotic surgery (β=−0.35, p=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Urban regions in Brazil exhibit higher PCa incidence due to greater screening coverage, while rural and less urbanized regions show higher mortality and MIR, reflecting delayed diagnosis and limited treatment access. Strengthening early detection and expanding oncologic infrastructure in rural areas are essential to reduce inequalities in PCa outcome

title: PENILE GIRTH ENHANCEMENT USING HYALURONIC ACID FILLER: A PROSPECTIVE EVALUATION OF 120 PATIENTS
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Leonardo De Souza Alves
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Penile girth enhancement has gained increasing attention among men seeking aesthetic and functional impromvement. Among available techniques hyaluronic acid (HA) filler injections have emerged as minimally invasive and reversible alternative to surgical augmentation. HA fillers are biocompative and absorbable, offering immediate results with favorable safety profile. However, objective data regarding the magnitude and durability of penile girth increase remain limited. Objective of this is evaluate the efficacy and short term persistence of penile girth enhancement using hyaluronic acid filler injections in men seeking penile augmentation. METHODS: A total of 120 men aged 25-55 years underwent penile augmentation with 8-12 ml of cross linked hyaluronic acid (HA). The product was injected subdermally along the penile shaft using a cannula technique. All procedures were perfomed by same urologist, under local anesthesia in a outpatient setting. Penile circumference was measured at the mid-shaft in the flaccid state at four time points: 15 minutes post-procedure, 15, 45, and 3 months. RESULTS: Immediate increase (15 minutes): mean gain of 2,0-3,0 cm in penile circumference. At 15 days: addiitonal mean increase of 0,5 cm. At 45 days and 3 months: the girth increase remained stable, with no significant reduction in circumference compared to the 15 day measurement. Adverse event with ecchymosis in 9% of patients, no cases of infection, no nodules, no vascular complications. CONCLUSIONS: Penile girth enhancement with hyaluronic acid filler resulted in a significant and durable increase in penile circumference, maintained up to 3 months post procedure at least. The techinque demostraded a high safety profile, minimal downtime, and high patient satisfaction. Hyaluronic Acid injection represents a safe effective and reversible option for penile augmentation in men seeking aeshtetic or confidence-related improvement.

title: AUTOMATING CLAVIEN-DINDO CLASSIFICATION WITH LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: A FASTER AND MORE RELIABLE WAY FOR DATA COLLECTION
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Gustavo Monteiro Perrone De Oliveira, Alexandre Danilovic, Lucas Dias, Giovanni Marchini, Fabio Torricelli, Carlos Batagello, Fabio Vicentini, Rodrigo Perrella, William C. Nahas, Eduardo Mazzucchi
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Interrater agreement of the Clavien-Dindo classification is only moderate, what questions the reliability of any conclusions that use it as a study endpoint. We aimed to validate the use of large language models (LLMs) for this task, benchmark them against physician performance, and compare the performance of different LLMs. METHODS: We evaluated the accuracy of ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, xAI Grok and Meta Llama through four steps: (1) defining Clavien-Dindo grades, (2) classifying complications, (3) classifying case summaries, and (4) classifying case summaries after machine learning. Vignettes were obtained from a categorization of percutaneous nephrolithotomy complications, used as an answer key. We measured agreement with Gwet’s AC2 coefficient and compared it with attending urologists and urology residents via electronic survey. RESULTS: All models accurately defined the Clavien-Dindo classification and accurately graded complication descriptions and case summaries before and after machine learning (accuracy values in Table 1). Six attending urologists and 15 residents classified the same vignettes, demonstrating lower accuracy than the LLMs (p<0.001). LLMs’ latency ranged from 1.04 (Copilot) to 3.02 minutes (DeepSeek), while the fastest physician required 17 minutes to complete the same tasks. LLMs’ intra-rater reliability was almost perfect: from 0.97 (Copilot) to 0.99 (Llama). Interrater reliability between LLMs (0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-0.98) was significantly higher than among physicians (0.93, 95% CI: 0.92-0.94). CONCLUSIONS: LLMs are faster, more accurate and more precise than physicians for Clavien-Dindo classification. We recommend its use to automate data collection, provided that it is implemented in compliance with applicable laws and ethical standards. We do not have evidence to endorse one specific LLM over another; this choice remains at the discretion of the user. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: PROFILE OF BRAZILIAN MEN SEEKING ONLINE HELP FOR EJACULATORY DISORDERS
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Marco Aurélio Lipay, Lucimar Venancio Secches, Bernardo Pires Saleme, Waldemar Braatz Krueger, Bruna Santana Sanglard, Fernando Gardin Caldano, Felipe Bulhões Ojeda, Natalia Dalsenter Avilez, Eduardo Lopez Mazzucato, Ubirajara Barroso, Jr
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: This study describes the profile of Brazilian men seeking online help for premature ejaculation. METHODS: An online application was used to evaluate men with ejaculatory disorders. The study analyzed data from 1,242 Brazilian men collected between October 20, 2024, and March 22, 2025. Participation was voluntary, and informed consent was obtained. Responses were collected via a questionnaire in the app and analyzed with the aid of artificial intelligence. The prevalence of ejaculatory disorders was determined using global questions derived from the definitions in validated instruments (IELT and PEDT). This was an uncontrolled retrospective study conducted in accordance with the guidelines of the Brazilian Ministry of Health, the Declaration of Helsink. RESULTS: From October 20, 2024, to March 22, 2025, 1,242 men voluntarily completed the questionnaire. Ages ranged from 18 to 72 years (median, 32 years). Most participants lived in the Southeast (31.6%) or Northeast (29.5%) regions. Of the respondents, 75.7% had a stable partner, 36.6% had hypertension, and 12.6% had diabetes. The app was discovered primarily through YouTube (42.4%), Google (22.5%), and Instagram (17.5%); overall, 87.7% of users learned about it via these platforms. Sixty-six percent of the men had never sought treatment for any sexual complaint, yet 88% expressed a genuine desire to improve their sex lives. Prevalence of dysfunctions was as follows: 41.2% had both premature ejaculation (PE) and erectile dysfunction (ED), 30.0% had PE only, and 13.0% had ED only. The primary concerns were improving ejaculation control (60.9%) and improving erections (22.1%). Men with PE were 1.65 times more likely to have ED than men without PE (odds ratio). CONCLUSIONS: The study underscores the need for an integrated assessment of male sexual function that includes both ejaculatory control and erectile quality, particularly when one dysfunction is present. A multidisciplinary approach involving physicians and psychotherapists is recommended. The app is a valuable tool but cannot replace in-person multidisciplinary care.

title: PREEMPTIVE ANALGESIA USING LIDOCAINE INFILTRATION BEFORE INCISION IN SUBINGUINAL VARICOCELECTOMY: INTERIM ANALYSIS OF A DOUBLE BLIND RANDOMIZED TRIAL
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Filipe T. Lira Neto, Josinaldo S. Costa, Geraldo T. Leite, Jr, Debora Antas Campello Souza, Alexandre B. Albuquerque, Igor P. Calado, Mirela B. A. Lima, Guilherme T. S. Maia, Luciana C. Lima
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Microsurgical varicocelectomy (MSV) is the most commonly performed operation for male infertility. Although MSV is minimally invasive, postoperative pain remains a key concern for many patients. This study aimed to determine whether pre-emptive analgesia via local infiltration of 0.5% lidocaine before skin and cremaster incision provides more effective early pain control than the current standard technique of lidocaine infiltration after wound closure. METHODS: We conducted a triple-blinded randomized controlled trial with men undergoing left subinguinal microsurgical varicocelectomy that were randomized to: Group A (pre-emptive)—lidocaine 0.5% infiltrated before incision at skin and cremaster; saline after closure; or Group B (post-closure)—saline before incision; lidocaine 0.5% after closure. Pain assessed by Visual Analog Scale (VAS) was recorded at 1, 6, and 24 postoperative hours in rest and cough. The following endpoits were compared between groups: each patient’s mean of the six VAS scores within 24h, presence of any pain (≥1 evaluation with VAS>0), and clinically relevant pain (≥1 evaluation with VAS>3), each assessed overall (rest+cough) and separately (rest only; cough only) at 1h, 6h, 24h; plus any rescue analgesic use. RESULTS: We enrolled and randomized 29 men, 14 in the preemptive group (PG) and 15 in the contreol group n=15 (CG). Early postoperative pain was generally low and comparable: mean 24 h VAS in PG 1.63 vs CG 2.27 (p=0.34). Any pain within 24 h occurred in PG 71% vs CG 93% (p=0.169), with no significant differences at 1 h, 6 h, or 24 h; rest only analyses were similar (p=1.00), and cough only patterns mirrored overall with not significant trends favoring preemptive at 6 h and 24 h. Clinically relevant pain was PG 43% vs CG 73% over 24 h (p=0.139) without time specific significance; rescue analgesic use did not differ, PG 29% vs CG 40% (p=0.700), and opioids were rarely required, PG 0% vs CG 6.7% (p=1.00). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, early postoperative pain after microsurgical varicocelectomy was low, with a low need for rescue analgesics across both study arms. In these preliminary data, the number of clinically relevant pain episodes (VAS>3) and the proportion requiring any rescue analgesic were numerically higher in the post-closure lidocaine group than in the pre-emptive group, but none of these differences reached statistical significance. Taken together with the primary non-inferiority finding, these results suggest that pre-emptive local infiltration is at least an equivalent strategy for early analgesia; however, larger, adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define the true clinical benefit of this anesthetic approach.

title: MINIMALLY INVASIVE SURGICAL THERAPIES COMPARED WITH PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR LOWER URINARY TRACT SYMPTOMS IN MEN WITH BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Thiago Iorio Tagliari, Henrique Cunha Vieira, Lucas G. C. R. De Amorim, Hibba Asim, Ogbeide Edwin Osamede, Luiza Mastrange Pugin, Rafael Tsutomu Martins Yadoya, Bruno Rodrigues Lebani
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive surgical therapies (MISTs) have emerged as alternatives to long-term pharmacological treatment in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Their comparative effectiveness versus standard drug therapy remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared outcomes of MISTs and pharmacotherapy in men with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) secondary to BPH. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing MISTs—water vapor thermal therapy (Rezum), prostatic artery embolization (PAE), and prostatic urethral lift (PUL)—with pharmacotherapy. Study selection followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Primary outcomes were the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax). Secondary outcomes included quality of life (QoL), sexual function, adverse events, and retreatment. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, with subgroup analyses by MIST type. RESULTS: 3 RCTs and 2 Cohort including 475 men treated with MISTs and 1,876 treated with pharmacotherapy were analyzed. For IPSS, the overall meta-analysis found no significant difference between MISTs and pharmacotherapy (mean difference \[MD\] 2.17, 95% confidence interval \[CI\] –1.19 to 5.53; P=0.15; I2=91%). Subgroup analyses showed no significant differences for Rezum (MD 0.30, 95% CI –0.48 to 1.08; P=0.99), PAE (MD 0.00, 95% CI –11.32 to 11.33; P=0.99), or PUL (MD 4.53, 95% CI –15.90 to 24.95; P=0.22). For Qmax, no difference was observed (MD 0.33 ml/s, 95% CI –0.17 to 0.83; P=0.14; I2=0%), with no significant subgroup interaction (P=0.74). Secondary outcomes were inconsistently reported, limiting further quantitative synthesis. CONCLUSIONS: MISTs did not demonstrate superior efficacy to pharmacotherapy in symptom relief or urinary flow improvement. High heterogeneity among trials likely reflects differences in patient selection, prostate size, and follow-up duration. Current evidence suggests that MISTs offer equivalent efficacy but may represent a suitable alternative when drug intolerance, side effects, or patient preference are decisive. Additional well-designed RCTs with standardized endpoints and longer follow-up are warranted.

title: OPTICAL VERSUS DIGITAL FLEXIBLE URETEROSCOPY: A PROSPECTIVE AND RANDOMIZED TRIAL
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Iso F. Kauffmann, Silvio Da Ressurreição Pires, Bruna Do Nascimento Santos, Tiago Guirro, Luis Gustavo Morato De Toledo
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In the past two decades, urolithiasis prevalence has risen, affecting about 7% of women and 10.3% of men in the U. S., with annual costs around $2 billion. Flexible ureteroscopy (FU) is widely used for renal stones larger than 1 cm. A key development in this field is the digital flexible ureteroscope (DFU), featuring high-resolution cameras that replace traditional optical fibers. This enhances durability, efficiency, and reduces weight, according to manufacturers. The objective of this study is to compare the efficacy and safety of digital ureteroscopes with those of traditional optical ureteroscopes. METHODS: This randomized clinical trial involved patients with renal or proximal ureteral stones measuring 1 to 2.5 cm. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group 1 underwent the procedure using a digital flexible ureteroscope, and Group 2 was treated using a fiber-optic flexible ureteroscope, both with similar diameters and working channel sizes. Each patient underwent a preoperative CT scan and a follow-up CT 30 days post-surgery. Outcomes were classified as Stone-Free, Stones < 4 mm, or Stones \> 4 mm, with success defined by patients achieving Stone-Free or Stones < 4 mm statuses. All procedures were conducted by a senior urology resident, under experienced supervision. RESULTS: The study was conducted prospectively from March 2019 to February 2022, involving 94 patients, 43 using a digital flexible ureteroscope and 51 an optical one. Most participants were female (64%), averaging 44 years, and 59% were classified as ASA II. Preoperatively, 54% had a double J stent, and 32% had lower calyx stones, mostly hard stones over 1000 Hounsfield units. Intraoperatively, mean surgical times were similar (63 minutes for digital, 61 minutes for optical), and fluoroscopy usage time, which was also comparable, averaged 64 seconds for the digital ureteroscope and 54 seconds for the optical ureteroscope. Conversely, the optical group used significantly less saline infusion (1447 ml vs. 1627 ml, p<0.01) and had significantly superior postoperative flexion and deflection (267 degrees vs. 257 degrees for flexion, 265 degrees vs. 255 degrees for deflection, p<0.01). Postoperative CT analysis revealed no statistically significant differences in failure rates between the two techniques. Digital ureteroscopes experienced a 27.3% failure rate, compared to a 33.3% failure rate with optical ureteroscopes (p=0.592). Complication rates were 9.8% for optical and 7.3% for digital ureteroscopes (p=0.906). All complications were Clavien-Dindo grade I, minor adverse events not requiring further surgical or therapeutic intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Digital ureteroscopes did not demonstrate superiority in stone-free rates or complications. Both technologies remain safe and effective options for the treatment of renal stones.

title: PREVALENCE OF LOWER URINARY TRACT SYMPTOMS IN PATIENTS WITH MYOTONIC DYSTROPHY TYPE 1
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Jose Antonio P. Prezotti, Victor Bruno Pereira Pinto, Claudia Rosemblatt Hacad, Davi Paraguassu Souza Martins, Jose De Bessa, Jr, Cristiano Mendes Gomes
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1, Steinert disease) is the most common hereditary muscular dystrophy in adults, with a prevalence of 4.7–15.2 per 100,000. This autosomal dominant, multisystem disorder causes myotonia, distal muscle atrophy, cataracts, endocrine dysfunction, infertility, cognitive impairment, and cardiac conduction defects. Despite DM1’s diverse manifestations, data on lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) remain scarce. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included consecutive DM1 patients aged≥18 years, evaluated at a specialized neuromuscular clinic. Muscular impairment was graded using the Muscular Impairment Rating Scale (grades 1–5), and functional status was measured with the Modified Barthel Index. LUTS were assessed in men with the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and in women using ICIQ-FLUTS. A symptomatic patient was defined as IPSS≥8 or similar cutoff for females. Overactive bladder (OAB) was evaluated via ICIQ-OAB, and urinary incontinence (UI) with the ICIQ-UI SF. Bowel function was examined using the Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction Score (NBDS), and quality of life (QoL) via WHOQOL-BREF. RESULTS: 36 patients (median age 43 years, IQR 21–73; 50% male) were included. Muscular impairment was moderate, with 38.9% with MIRS grade 2, 41.6% with grade 3, and 19.5% with grade 4\. As for functionality, 15 (41.7%) had moderate to complete dependence and only 10 (27.8%) were fully independent. The overall prevalence of LUTS was 75% (66.6% in men, 83.3% in women). Storage symptoms were most common (68.8%), with voiding symptoms in 22.2% and post-micturition in 13.9%. Moderate to severe LUTS occurred in 22.3% of men and 38.8% of women. OAB was diagnosed in 27.8% of men and 55.6% of women. UI affected 58.3% overall (50% of men, 66.7% of women). Moderate to severe bowel dysfunction was observed in 13.8%. Most patients (61%) reported being satisfied with their QoL. Higher Barthel Index scores correlated with lower prevalence of LUTS (p=0.025) and urinary incontinence (p=0.005), indicating that greater functional independence predicted fewer LUTS. CONCLUSIONS: LUTS, mainly storage-related and urgency urinary incontinence, are highly prevalent in DM1, affecting men and women similarly. Greater functional independence is associated with a reduced burden of LUTS and urinary incontinence in DM1 patients. | | | --- | | |

title: FINANCIAL LITERACY AMONG GRADUATING CANADIAN UROLOGY RESIDENTS COMPARED TO FACULTY
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Archit Jain, Naji J. Touma
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Personal financial literacy influences wellbeing, particularly during the transition from residency to independent practice when residents transform into small business owners. Despite growing emphasis on wellness, many residency programs provide little education on financial management. This study evaluated the financial literacy of graduating Canadian urology residents in comparison to staff urologists. It also examined perceptions of financial competence and the frequency of financial discussions between both groups. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey study at a national preparatory exam for graduating Canadian urology residents. The survey was administered to all residents and faculty attending the event and the response rate was 100% in both groups. We created a 40-item survey with demographic questions (11), Likert scale questions about comfort and perception of financial literacy (5), reimbursement-related questions to a urology practice (12), and validated financial literacy questions (9 true/false, 11 multiple choice). Descriptive statistics were generated and responses were analyzed using Welch’s t-test for group comparisons. RESULTS: A total of 38 residents and 13 staff completed the survey. Staff achieved higher objective financial literacy scores (77% vs. 63%; p=0.004). Staff also reported a greater perception in financial literacy skills (p<0.05). Both groups viewed financial literacy as highly important (p-0.765). Most respondents felt finances were discussed “not enough” during residency. Regarding reimbursement, both groups were equally likely to be wrong about true compensation with a delta varying from 0.4% to 44.1%. CONCLUSIONS: Staff urologists outperformed residents in both validated financial literacy questions and perceived self-competence in financial literacy. Despite these differences, both groups indicated a lack of adequate discussion of financial topics during residency. Discrepancies in perceived versus actual reimbursement underscores the importance of structured financial education within residency programs to ease the transition to practice.

title: TO CIRC OR NOT TO CIRC — THAT IS THE QUESTION FOR PATIENTS WITH POSTERIOR URETHRAL VALVES
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Hans Bae, Alyssa Wong, Falla Jin, Harry Chae, Qian Zhang, Abdullah Al Shalan, Douglas Matsell, Jeffrey Bone, Kourosh Afshar, Erik Skarsgard, Andrew Macneily, Soojin Kim
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Antibiotic prophylaxis (AP) and circumcision are commonly used to prevent urinary tract infections (UTIs) in children with posterior urethral valves (PUV), but there is insufficient research examining their efficacy when used together. This study compared the effectiveness of AP when used alone and in combination with circumcision in preventing UTIs in PUV patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed PUV patients managed at our institution from 2000-2019 with a 2-year follow-up period after initial presentation. Patients were classified as ‘AP-only’ if they received AP but not circumcision, or if circumcision occurred after AP initiation due to breakthrough UTIs. Patients were classified as ‘combined treatment’ if they received both AP and circumcision without intervening UTIs. UTIs were defined based on patient symptoms, microbiological confirmation, and/or clinical documentation. An inverse probability-weighted multivariable Poisson regression model was used to compare UTI incidence rates between treatment groups, while accounting for informative censoring due to treatment change and adjusting for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission status, distance to hospital, and socioeconomic deprivation. RESULTS: Out of 61 patients with PUV, 41 received AP only (67.2%), 12 received combined treatment (19.7%), 4 received circumcision only (6.6%), and 4 received none of the two interventions (6.6%). Median age at circumcision, AP initiation, and first UTI was 120 days (interquartile range (IQR) 32, 355), 11 days (IQR 2, 40), and 52 days (IQR 18, 132), respectively. The incidence rate of UTIs in the AP-only group was 0.17 per person-year (95% CI 0.14, 0.22), and 0.05 per-person year in the combined treatment group (95% CI 0.02, 0.11). Multivariable analysis showed that patients who received combined treatment had a 74% lower UTI incidence rate compared to those who received only AP (incidence rate ratio 0.26; 95% CI 0.10, 0.65; p=0.004). Greater patient distance from hospital (p=0.02) and greater socioeconomic deprivation (p=0.005) were each associated with higher UTI rates, whereas NICU admission was not significant (p=0.83). CONCLUSIONS: Combined treatment of circumcision with AP may be more effective than AP alone in preventing UTIs in PUV patients. In our cohort, geographical proximity to hospital and degree of socioeconomic deprivation were predictive of UTI occurrence. Further investigation through implementation of a national, multicenter PUV registry could inform future practices in the management of UTIs in PUV patients.

title: LEVERAGING MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS TO PREDICT THE RISK OF PATHOLOGICAL EXTRAPROSTATIC EXTENSION AFTER ROBOTIC-ASSISTED RADICAL PROSTATECTOMY
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Abbas Hammoud, Mohammad Ali Mazloum, Nadim Alame, Marwan Zein, Kayanne Toutounji, Noha Faour, Albert El Hajj
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Pathological extraprostatic extension (pEPE) is an important prognostic indicator that is linked to increased risk of prostate cancer recurrence after robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) and may influence decisions about adjuvant therapy. However, pEPE usually remains undiscovered until operative specimens are sent for pathology. While multi-parametric MRI has improved preoperative local staging, other preoperative variables may improve risk stratification for pEPE. Our study aimed to train machine learning models to use a comprehensive set of preoperative clinical, pathological, and MRI features to predict pathological pEPE after RARP. METHODS: Our database included 610 patients who underwent RARP. Preoperative variables that served as inputs to our models included age, BMI, PSA, clinical stage, PIRADS score, and biopsy features. Preoperative variables missing < 5% of their values were imputed with the mode or mean. The rest were imputed with multivariate imputation by chained equations (MICE). The database was split into training (80%, n=488) and testing (20%, n=122) sets. Multiple machine learning classifiers, including logistic regression, random forest (RF), xgboost, support vector machine, k-Nearest Neighbors, adaboost, and catboost were trained to predict pEPE status. Each model's hyperparameters were optimized using 5-fold cross validation on the training set. Final performance was evaluated on the test set using AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). An error analysis was conducted on the best-performing model. RESULTS: 30% of patients in our database had positive pEPE status. The tuned random forest (RF) was the winning predictor of pEPE, with the highest AUROC (0.83). RF’s main strengths were its high specificity (0.89) and NPV (0.83). It achieved modest sensitivity (0.57) and moderate PPV (0.7). Fraction of cores that were positive and maximum percent positivity were the top contributors to the RF. Error analysis revealed that most of RF's false negatives (12/13) and false positives (6/7) occurred in patients with high-risk PIRADs of 4 or 5. This highlighted the unreliability of a high PIRADS score in the database: our best model was unable to find strong-enough patterns in the other pre-op variables to robustly stratify risk within this subgroup. CONCLUSIONS: Our study shows that considering the full preoperative picture can allow machine learning algorithms to predict postoperative pathologic EPE with high specificity and NPV. This can enable robust identification of low-risk patients, which can improve patient counseling before RARP.

title: THE VALUE OF INTRAOPERATIVE POINT-OF-CARE URINALYSIS TO PREDICT POSITIVE URINE CULTURES AND SYMPTOMATIC POST-OPERATIVE INFECTIONS DURING CYSTOSCOPIC PROCEDURES FOR PEDIATRIC PATIENTS
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Michael E. Chua, Kay C. Rivera, Lai Nam E. Tse, Martin Koyle, Mariana E. Adam, Natalie E. Fox, Felicia E. Tanudjaja, Emily E. Miao, Sarah Hughes, Michael E. Vladimirsky, Darius E. Bagli, Armando E. Lorenzo, Mandy E. Rickard, Joana E. Dos Santos
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate intraoperative point-of-care urinalysis (UA) for predicting positive urine cultures and postoperative UTIs in children undergoing cystoscopy, and to assess its potential to reduce unnecessary cultures and antibiotics. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort at a tertiary pediatric urology center (Aug 2023–Apr 2024), 62 cystoscopy cases with paired dipstick UA and quantitative culture were analyzed after excluding recent antibiotic use or incomplete data. Dipstick markers—leukocyte esterase and nitrite—were evaluated alone and combined (“either-positive” vs. “both-positive”). Positive culture was defined as≥105CFU/mL; postoperative UTI required fever, clinical signs, and a positive culture within 7 days. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed by ROC curves andχ2tests. A multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, procedure, laterality, and clinical condition. A retrospective QI model estimated reductions in culture orders and empiric antibiotics. RESULTS: Thirty-nine patients (62.9%) were dipstick-negative by the ‘either-positive’ rule; one had a positive culture (NPV 97.4%; 95% CI 86.5–99.9%). Of 23 dipstick-positive patients, 13 (56.5%) had positive cultures. In multivariable analysis, “either-positive” dipstick was the sole predictor of culture positivity (OR 330.2; 95% CI 30.5–3 574.1; p=0.003). QI modeling indicated that restricting cultures to the 23 dipstick-positive specimens would have averted 39 of 62 cultures (62.9%), at the expense of missing one infection (2.6% of un-cultured cases). CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative dipstick UA reliably identifies pediatric cystoscopy patients at low risk for postoperative UTI, offering a rapid, cost-effective tool to enhance antimicrobial stewardship and reduce laboratory utilization. Prospective multicenter validation is recommended. | | | --- | | |

title: PHASE 1/2 STUDY OF AN ANTI-PD-L1/IL-15 VARIANT FUSION PROTEIN (SIM0237) IN BCG-UNRESPONSIVE HIGH-RISK NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER (NMIBC)
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Dingwei Ye, Hua Xu, Hailong Hu, Shusuan Jiang, Shudong Zhang, Zhixian Yu, Zhuowei Liu, Haitao Niu, Yu Cao, Benkang Shi, Tao Dai, Tao Wu, Jiajia Xu, Rong Sun, Nating Zhang, Haolin Sun
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Treatment options for BCG-unresponsive (UR) NMIBC are limited. Anti-PD-1 monotherapy and IL-15 agonist in combination with BCG have shown clinical efficacy in BCG-UR carcinoma in situ (CIS) NMIBC. It remains unclear whether targeting both PD-(L)1 and IL-15 has synergistic effect in NMIBC. SIM0237 is an anti-PD-L1/IL-15 variant fusion protein. The single agent showed good safety profile and promising efficacy signal in patients with BCG-UR NMIBC in the dose escalation part. This abstract reported data from the dose escalation and expansion parts of SIM0237 monotherapy from the ongoing Phase 1/2 study (NCT06186414). METHODS: Patients with BCG-UR high-risk NMIBC received intravesical SIM0237 following the standard induction/maintenance treatment schedule. A re-induction course was allowed if the patients had persistent CIS or high-grade Ta at Month 3. Key study endpoints included DLT, safety, tolerability, PK and efficacy \[complete response (CR) rate and duration\ of CR for CIS NMIBC, disease-free survival (DFS) and DFS rate at specific time points\ for papillary-only NMIBC\]. RESULTS: From January 10, 2024 to the data cutoff date of August 8, 2025, a total of 43 patients (10 CIS with or without Ta/T1, 33 papillary-only) have received SIM0237 monotherapy, with 3, 10 and 30 patients at the dose levels of 75 mg, 150 mg and 300 mg, respectively. The median age was 62 years, with 81% male. The median number of prior BCG doses was 13\. Of the 7 CIS patients who had at least 1 post-baseline tumor assessment, 6 achieved a best response of CR and 5 were maintaining the CR status. In the 33 papillary-only patients, the median follow-up duration was 4.57 months. The median DFS was immature, with a 12-month DFS rate of 75.4% (95% CI, 48.9%-89.4%). TEAEs occurred in 38 (88.4%) patients and 23 (53.5%) patients had TRAEs. The majority of TRAEs were Grade 1/2 and limited in the urinary system. Nine (20.9%) patients had Grade 3 TEAEs and 1 (2.3%) had Grade 3 TRAEs. No Grade 4 or 5 TEAEs were reported. Four (9.3%) patients had SAEs and 1 had TRSAEs of urinary bladder haemorrhage and prostatic haemorrhage. Ten (23.3%) patients had dose interruptions due to TEAEs, and 4 (9.3%) had dose interruptions due to TRAEs. No DLT, immune-related AE or AE leading to SIM0237 discontinuation. PK data showed undetectable systemic exposure of SIM0237 in all 29 patients with serum samples analyzed. CONCLUSIONS: Intravesical SIM0237 was safe and well tolerated with promising clinical efficacy in patients with BCG-UR high-risk NMIBC. The Phase 3 study of SIM0237 monotherapy in this patient population is under plan.

title: SODIUM-GLUCOSE COTRANSPORTER 2 INHIBITORS USE IN PROSTATE CANCER PATIENTS UNDERGOING HORMONE THERAPY: A SEQUENTIAL TARGET TRIAL EMULATION STUDY
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Rong Na, Ruofan Shi, Xiaohao Ruan
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Emerging evidence suggests that sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) may be inversely associated with the risk of prostate cancer (PCa). This target trial emulation (TTE) study is designed to evaluate the impact of SGLT2i use on clinical outcomes in PCa patients undergoing hormone therapy (HT). METHODS: This TTE utilized electronic health records of the Hong Kong population between March 2000 and March 2025. A sequential TTE design was applied with monthly intervals. The study outcomes were: time to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) failure, time to next-generation hormonal agent (NHA) failure, and overall survival (OS). Study outcomes were analyzed using marginal structural models fitted via weighted pooled logistic regression, with inverse probability weighting to address time-varying confounding and informative censoring. RESULTS: A total of 712 PCa patients who received both HT and SGLT2i for diabetes were identified, and 1167 non-diabetic PCa (non-SGLT2i) patients who underwent HT were included as the control group. SGLT2i use was significantly associated with improved time to ADT failure (hazard ratio, HR=0.65, 95% confidence interval, 95% CI: 0.43-0.97, p=0.036) and overall survival (HR=0.32, 95% CI: 0.21-0.50, p<0.001). However, a non-significant reduced risk was observed for NHA failure (HR=0.68, 95% CI: 0.38-1.21, p=0.188). Subgroup analysis comparing two SGLT2is (i. e., dapagliflozin and empagliflozin) indicated that dapagliflozin was associated with significantly greater protective effects on the overall survival compared to empagliflozin (HR=0.32, 95% CI: 0.12-0.85, p=0.022), whereas no significant differences were observed in terms of the other outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: The use of SGLT2i in PCa patients receiving HT was associated with a significantly reduced risk of disease progression and mortality.

title: CARDIOLOGIC AND ONCOLOGIC OUTCOMES WITH GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS IN MEN RECEIVING ANDROGEN DEPRIVATION THERAPY FOR PROSTATE CANCER
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Tamas Fazekas, Ádám Lénárt, Mihály Ruppert, Celia Blasszauer, Daniel Reibl, Ida Komka, János Szalontai, Marcin Miszczyk, Pawel Rajwa, Péter Hegyi, Tibor Szarvas, Shahrokh F. Shariat, Michael S. Leapman, Péter Nyirády
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is the backbone of treatment of advanced prostate cancer (PCa), however it is associated with adverse metabolic changes and cardiovascular toxicity. Accordingly, a significant proportion of PCa mortality is attributed to cardiovascular diseases. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) improve glycemic control and reduce cardiovascular events in diabetes, but evidence in men with PCa receiving ADT is limited. We aimed to assess survival and cardiovascular outcomes in men with type II diabetes (T2DM) on ADT who received GLP-1RA. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Hungarian National Health Insurance Fund (NEAK) database. Men with PCa initiating ADT between 2018-2024 were identified and classified to exposure groups: (1) T2DM with GLP-1RA use; (2) T2DM with metformin but no GLP-1RA use; (3) T2DM with no metformin and GLP-1RA therapy (4) no diabetes and no GLP-1RA therapy. The primary outcome was the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (non-fatal and fatal acute myocardial infarction and stroke); secondary outcomes included individual cardiovascular events, overall survival (OS), time to next treatment (TNT). RESULTS: A total of 13,944 men with prostate cancer initiating ADT (of which 2758 with T2DM) between 2018–2024 were included in the analysis. Of these, 135 had type 2 diabetes treated with iGLP-1RA, 1,582 were treated with metformin, 1,041 received other antidiabetic medications (non-incretin, non-metformin), and 10,708 had no diabetes. The median age (IQR) was 70 years (66–75) for incretin users, 73 (68–77) for metformin users, 74 (69–78) for non-incretin non-metformin users, and 73 (68–78) for non-diabetic men. Baseline cardioascular characteristics were balanced across biabetic study groups and markedly better for non-diabetic men. Median time to next treatment or death was 0.7 years (IQR 0.1–1.6) in incretin users, 0.8 years (0.2–1.8) in metformin, 0.9 years (0.2–1.9) in non-incretin non-metformin, and 1.1 years (0.5–2.1) years among non-diabetic men. Median overall survival was 1.7 years (IQR 0.9–2.7) among incretin users, 1.7 (0.8–2.6) in metformin, 1.4 (0.7–2.8) in non-incretin non-metformin, and 1.4 (0.6–2.5) years in non-diabetic men. The raw incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events was 32% in incretin users, compared with 52% in non-incretin non-metformin, 43% in metformin, and 35% in non-diabetic men. CONCLUSIONS: Patients with PCa and T2DM receiving ADT are at an elevated risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. These preliminary results support consideration of GLP-1RAs for further prospective validation to mitigate the cardiovascular toxicity associated with ADT use.

title: FEASIBILITY AND OUTCOMES OF SUPINE MINI-PCNL IN CHILDREN USING A DIGITAL DISPOSABLE NEPHROSCOPE WITH VACUUM-ASSISTED SUCTION ACCESS SHEATH: EARLY CLINICAL EXPERIENCE
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Jaisukh Kalathia, Kaushal Patel, Sahil Khant, Santosh Agrawal, Giriraj Vala, Arvind Valiya, Bharti Talreja, Vineet Gauhar
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Supine percutaneous nephrolithotomy (S-PCNL) in children is technically challenging due to smaller renal anatomy, limited working space, and higher risks of bleeding or fluid overload. Safe access and effective instrument manoeuvrability require miniaturized equipment, precise technique, and considerable surgical expertise. Owing to its advantages of maintaining low intrarenal pressure, reducing operative time, and enhancing safety, we prospectively evaluated the feasibility and outcomes of using a vacuum-assisted suction sheath (VASS) in combination with a digital disposable nephroscope in paediatric patients. METHODS: Prospectively maintained records of 963 patients who underwent S-PCNL were analysed following institutional review board approval. Between January 2024 and September 2025, 23 paediatric patients who underwent S-PCNL using a VASS with a mini digital disposable nephroscope were identified. Baseline demographics, radiological findings, stone characteristics, urine cultures, 30-day non-contrast CT (NCCT) stone-free rates (SFR), postoperative infections, transfusion requirements, auxiliary procedures, and hospital stay were evaluated. Feasibility of achieving single puncture access per pelvicalyceal system (PCS), sheath manoeuvrability, and need for additional punctures were documented. Residual fragments (RF) were classified as follows: Grade A—stone-free (no RF), Grade B—single fragment≤4 mm, and Grade C—any fragment >4 mm or multiple fragments. RESULTS: Mean age of the patients was 10.6 years, including 17 males and 6 females. Most cases were Guy’s Stone Score (GSS) Grade II, with a mean stone size of 1.8 ± 0.3 cm; 25% had additional secondary stones. All procedures were performed under general anaesthesia using fluoroscopy-guided single-pass access with a 16/18 Fr sheath in the flank-oblique supine modified lithotomy (FOSML) position. Stone fragmentation was achieved using a digital disposable nephroscope with Holmium:YAG laser, and fragments were evacuated through the VASS. Mean operative time was 38.4 ± 14 minutes, with a mean VASS activation time of 16 ± 8 minutes. Complete clearance through a single tract was achieved in all patients, with no additional punctures required. Zero residual fragments (ZRF) were observed in 20 (87%) patients, and only one required an auxiliary procedure for residual calculi. Mean hospital stay was two days, and no perioperative mortality occurred. The VASS sheath demonstrated excellent manoeuvrability within the PCS, allowing complete access without increased bleeding. CONCLUSIONS: Supine mini-PCNL using a digital disposable nephroscope with a VASS is safe, feasible, and effective in children. It provides high stone-free rates, minimal morbidity, and short hospital stays. These encouraging outcomes support its potential as a preferred approach for paediatric renal stone management.

title: DEEP MACHINE LEARNING ENSEMBLE MODEL FOR EMPHYSEMATOUS PYELONEPHRITIS CLASSIFICATION AND CLINICAL DECISION INTELLIGENCE
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Roshan Yedulla Reddy, Hariharasudhan Sekar, Shreenidhi Sriram, Ganesh Prasad Shivakumar, Vivek Meyyappan, Sriram Krishnamoorthy
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN) is a life-threatening necrotizing renal infection with mortality rates of 10–40%, requiring urgent intervention. The Huang–Tseng CT classification depends on subjective interpretation, often delaying decisions. EPN-CDI was developed as an AI-driven clinical decision support system integrating deep-learning segmentation and ensemble machine learning for automated EPN classification, severity assessment, and treatment recommendations. METHODS: EPN-CDI is an ensemble machine learning system combining automated CT segmentation (nnU-Net), radiomics feature extraction (PyRadiomics), and machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) for outcome prediction. CT DICOM images underwent automated segmentation using nnU-Net v2. Radiomics features were extracted including first-order statistics, texture matrices (GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, GLDM, NGTDM), and morphological descriptors. Clinical parameters included demographics, vital signs, laboratory values (creatinine, eGFR, inflammatory markers, electrolytes), comorbidities, and microbiology. The system predicted: (1) Huang-Tseng classification, (2) ICU/HDU/Ward admission, (3) mortality probability, (4) dialysis requirement, and (5) treatment modality. Modified NEWS2, GREMP score (Gas, Renal impairment, Extended collection, Mental state, Platelets), and EPN-specific severity indices were integrated, generating automated PDF reports with therapeutic guidance. Internal validation included 194 patients with CT-confirmed EPN from a tertiary center. RESULTS: Automated segmentation achieved mean Dice coefficient 0.89 ± 0.03 for gas mapping. Ensemble model performance: classification AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.95; accuracy 89.2%), mortality AUC 0.86, ICU need AUC 0.88—superior to NEWS2 (0.79) and radiologic grading (0.74; p0.05). Treatment recommendation concordance reached AUC 0.90 (sensitivity 89.8%, specificity 92.7%). Independent predictors included gas volume >30% of parenchyma (p=0.012), creatinine >3 mg/dL (p=0.021), and platelets 100×109/L (p=0.009). Full report generation was completed in mean 4.2 ± 1.3 minutes versus 45–60 minutes for traditional evaluation (p0.001), and inter-reader agreement improved (κ=0.84 vs 0.67). CONCLUSIONS: EPN-CDI enables rapid, objective, and accurate EPN classification, risk prediction, and treatment guidance, outperforming existing scores and radiologic grading. Its integration could standardize care, expedite critical decisions, and improve outcomes. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

title: SUCCESSFUL NON-OPERATIVE SALVAGE OF GLANS ISCHEMIA FOLLOWING CHORDEE CORRECTION: A TWO-CASE REPORT
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Pawan Kandhari, Pankaj Joshi, Saurabh Thakkar, Shreyas Bhadranavar, Sanjay Kulkarni
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Glans ischemia is a rare urological emergency, and its occurrence following major penile reconstruction is exceptional. We report two cases of glans ischemia after chordee correction utilising a bovine pericardial graft. METHODS: Two patients developed dusky discoloration and cyanosis of the glans on postoperative day 3 and 6, respectively after undergoing chordee correction with bovine pericardium graft repair. Color Doppler ultrasound confirmed significantly reduced vascular flow, suggesting a delayed thrombotic or inflammatory etiology. A multimodal, non-operative management protocol was immediately initiated, consisting of antiplatelet therapy (Acetylsalicylic acid 75 mg), anticoagulation (Enoxaparin 60 mg), systemic vasodilators (Pentoxifylline 400 mg, Tadalafil 5 mg), and a course of five 90-minute Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT) sessions at 1.6–2.0 ATA. RESULTS: Clinical improvement was noted within 48 hours of initiating therapy. Substantial restoration of glans perfusion was observed after the third HBOT session, leading to complete resolution of ischemia in both patients. In total 5 sessions of HBOT were given for both. At 6-month follow-up, both individuals were asymptomatic, demonstrating normal glans appearance with no residual functional or cosmetic impairment. CONCLUSIONS: Glans ischemia is a rare but critical complication following complex penile surgery. These cases demonstrate that prompt recognition and aggressive, multimodal conservative management, integrating targeted pharmacotherapy with HBOT, can be highly effective in salvaging the glans penis, obviating the need for surgical intervention and yielding excellent long-term outcomes.

title: URETHRAL DIVERTICULA WITHOUT SURGICAL REMOVAL–ARE WE LUCKY OR MISTAKEN?
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Masha Ben Zvi, Sionov Ben Valery, Mohammad Taha, Itay Sagy, Ami Sidi, Alexander Tsivian
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The reported incidence of urethral diverticula ranges between 0.02% and 6%. The natural history of this condition remains poorly understood, and there is no consensus regarding which patients require surgical treatment or the optimal timing of intervention. Currently, most patients diagnosed with urethral diverticula are offered surgery, even if asymptomatic. This study aimed to evaluate the natural history of women with urethral diverticula who were managed without surgical intervention due to various reasons. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients diagnosed with urethral diverticula, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Demographic and clinical data, physical examination findings, imaging results, treatment type, and outcomes were analyzed. In addition, a telephone survey was performed. RESULTS: Of 125 women diagnosed with urethral diverticula, since 2006 31 women (aged 18–58 years; mean 35.8 years) did not undergo surgical treatment at diagnosis and met inclusion criteria. Sixteen symptomatic patients comprised Group 1, and 15 asymptomatic patients comprised Group 2.· In Group 1, four patients underwent puncture and drainage, and eight experienced spontaneous drainage. Six women (37.5%) eventually required surgery, between 1 and 20 years after diagnosis.· In Group 2, one patient had spontaneous drainage of the mass without recurrence, and only one patient (6.6%) underwent surgery. One patient was lost to follow-up. Overall, 22.6% of patients required surgery following an initial conservative approach: 37.5% of symptomatic women and 6.6% of asymptomatic women. CONCLUSIONS: Most asymptomatic patients with urethral diverticula can be safely managed with observation alone. Spontaneous drainage may lead to regression of the mass, further supporting conservative management as a reasonable option. Based on these findings, we suggest that the natural history of this condition more closely resembles that of paraurethral retention cysts rather than true diverticula.

title: STUDY ON FUNCTIONALIZED NANOPARTICLE DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM MODIFIED BY SERTOLI CELL MEMBRANE FOR IMPROVING CYTOXAN-INDUCED TESTICULAR INJURY
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Xiaozhi Zhao, Yisong Ju
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: With the younger age of cancer patients and the improvement of cancer treatment efficacy, fertility preservation in cancer patients has gradually become a new issue during cancer treatment. Cytoxan is a common used alkylating agent in cancer chemotherapy, but it has reproductive toxicity, which often leads to an increase in the level of reactive oxygen species in the tests and subsequent damage. Superoxide dismutase is the key to reducing ROS level; however, clinically, it is difficult to reduce testicular ROS levels through conventional drug delivery methods due to the low efficiency of testicular-targeted delivery and the presence of the blood-testis barrier. This study aims to design and synathesize a material that can be targeted to the tests, reduce testicular ROS levels, and thereby improve cytoxan-induced testicular injury, providing a new method for fertility protection in male cancer patients. METHODS: CAT-SchA@SCM was synthesized using techniques. The testicular accumulation of CAT-SchA@SCM was detected via immunofluorescence. To verify whether CAT-SchA@SCM could cross the blood-testis barrier (BTB), a BTB model was established in vitro using TM-4 cells. Testicular cell lines were treated with 4-hydroperoxycyclophosphamide (4-HC), a metabolite of cytoxan in vivo. A mouse model of cytoxan-induced testicular injury was established by intraperitoneal injection of cytoxan, followed by CAT-SchA@SCM injection for treatment. RESULTS: We designed and synthesized the CAT-SchA@SCM material using techniques including protein self-assembly and ultrasonic emulsification. Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) analyses showed that the nanoparticles had a subspherical shape, along with good uniformity and stability. Probe labeling and immunofluorescence staining results demonstrated that CAT-SchA@SCM could accumulate in testicular tissue. Using an in vitro constructed BTB model, we found that CAT-SchA@SCM was capable of crossing the BTB. Cell line experiments indicated that CAT-SchA@SCM could significantly reduce the reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in TM-4 cells and improve cell viability. Animal experiments showed that CAT-SchA@SCM could restore the testis weight, testis-to-body weight ratio, sperm motility and progressive motility, as well as the number of various testicular cell types in mice after cytoxan induction—suggesting that CAT-SchA@SCM could reverse cytoxan-induced testicular injury. Hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining of tissue sections from major organs revealed that CAT-SchA@SCM had no impact on the morphology of various tissues, indicating its biosafety at the therapeutic concentration. CONCLUSIONS: We designed and prepared CAT-SchA@SCM, a material encapsulated by Sertoli cell membranes and loaded with catalase (CAT) and schisandrin A (SchA). It was confirmed that this material could efficiently accumulate in testicular tissue and cross the BTB. Cell and animal experiments showed that CAT-SchA@SCM could significantly alleviate testicular tissue and cell damage induced by cytoxan and its metabolites. This study provides a new approach for fertility protection in male cancer patients.

title: PREDICTIVE AND PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF BIOPSY GLEASON PATTERN 4 PROPORTION IN LOCALIZED PROSTATE CANCER
session: Global Gateway Posters Day 1 (GG01)
authors: Andrea Rybarikova, Alexandra Furrer, Lena Wolf, Yasmin Heiniger, Fabian Obrecht, Hubert Andreas John, Beat Foerster
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Several policymakers have proposed that patients with intermediate-risk prostate cancer (PC) and a limited amount of Gleason pattern 4 (GP4) disease may be suitable candidates for active surveillance (AS). However, the supporting scientific evidence remains limited, and no consensus has yet been established on this issue. The aim of our study was to assess the predictive and prognostic value of the total extent of GP4 in prostate biopsies on the final pathologic findings after radical prostatectomy (RP) and oncologic outcomes during follow-up. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, we included consecutive patients who underwent combined targeted and systematic prostate biopsies revealing international society of urological pathology (ISUP) grade group 1 to 3 prostate cancer, followed by RP between January 2015 and December 2024. All histologic samples were independently reviewed by a dedicated uropathologist. The amount of GP4 was quantified as the total length (mm) of pattern 4 carcinoma divided by the total length (mm) of carcinoma across all biopsy cores. GP4 thresholds were determined using the Youden and Liu indices. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations with adverse pathological features, while Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate biochemical recurrence-free survival (RFS) and metastasis-free survival (MFS). RESULTS: Among 247 patients included in the analysis, 78 (32%) had ISUP grade group 1, 126 (51%) had grade group 2, and 43 (17%) had grade group 3 disease on biopsy. The median age was 73 years (interquartile range \[IQR\] 68–77). A GP4 cut-off of 10% was identified as being associated with locally advanced disease (standard error 3.4, p=0.003), and a cut-off of 14% was associated with pathological upgrading at RP (standard error 2.7, p<0.001). Overall, 163 patients (66%) had a GP4 extent of less than 10%. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, a GP4 extent <10% was independently associated with lower likelihood of locally advanced disease (odds ratio \[OR\] 0.17, 95% confidence interval \[CI\] 0.08–0.33, p<0.001). During a median follow-up of 46 months, 51 patients (21%) experienced biochemical recurrence, and 9 patients (4%) developed metastases. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, a GP4 extent <10% was independently associated with improved RFS (hazard ratio \[HR\] 0.48, 95% CI 0.25– 0.93, p=0.03) and MFS (HR 0.08, 95% CI 0.02–0.45, p=0.004). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with localized PC, a GP4 extent below 10% on biopsy was strongly associated with more favorable pathological findings and improved oncologic outcomes. These results support the role of quantitative GP4 assessment in refining risk stratification and identifying candidates for AS among selected intermediate-risk patients.

title: BENIGN CYSTECTOMY: THE EFFECT OF SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS AND DISCHARGE DESTINATION ON PATIENT OUTCOMES
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Maxwell L. Sandberg, David Thole, Randall Bissette, Dylan Wolff, Gavin Underwood, Robert Evans, Soroush Rais-bahrami, Alejandro Rodriguez
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The impact of patient socioeconomic status (SES) on patient presentation, preoperative management, and surgical outcomes is often overlooked. Discharge destination (DD) after major surgery is also felt to play into emergency department (ED) and healthcare utilization. Benign cystectomy (BC) for non-oncologic bladder disease is a surgery felt to carry a high morbidity but remains understudied. The purpose of this study was to assess the effect of patient SES and DD after BC on surgical outcomes. METHODS: All BC performed from 2012-2025 at our institution were reviewed. SES was obtained using patient area deprivation index (ADI) scores, with a greater score corresponding to more socioeconomic deprivation (1 through 10). DD was classified as either home, home with nursing assistance (HNA), and skilled nursing facility (SNF). Patient demographics and surgical outcomes were reviewed. Outcomes were compared based on ADI score and DD using independent samples t-test, chi-squared test, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. RESULTS: 183 patients underwent BC. Median ADI score was 5 \Interquartile range (IQR) 4-8; [Table 1a\]. 90 ( Table 1b; 49%) patients were discharged to home, 78 (43%) patients were discharged to HNA, and 15 (8%) patients were discharged to a SNF. No association between ADI and DD was observed (p>0.05). Postoperative complication rate and 90-day readmission rates did not differ by ADI score (p>0.05), but a greater ADI score was associated with a higher mean number of ED visits after BC (p<0.05). Patients discharged to a SNF were more likely to experience a postoperative complication, visit the ED after BC, and have a greater length of stay (p<0.05). Preoperative bladder capacity had no relationship to ADI nor DD (p>0.05). Overall survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis was not different by ADI score (Figure 1a; p>0.05) but was lower in SNF patients (Figure 1b; p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Complication rate was equivalent by SES but patients with a greater ADI score (worse SES) appeared to utilize healthcare resources (ED) more frequently after BC. DD, specifically SNF patients, also were more likely to have a postoperative complication, utilize the ED, and have a longer postoperative stay. These results call for further study on the impact of SES and DD on BC outcomes. | | | --- | | |

title: RACIAL DISPARITIES IN PRE-OPERATIVE UNDERSTANDING OF ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION AND INCONTINENCE AFTER RADICAL PROSTATECTOMY TITLE: RACIAL DISPARITIES IN PRE-OPERATIVE UNDERSTANDING OF ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION AND INCONTINENCE AFTER RADICAL PROSTATECTOMY
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Mary Namugosa-Makumbi, Maxwell Sandberg, Ryan Terlecki
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Radical prostatectomy is a definitive treatment for prostate cancer but frequently leads to stress urinary incontinence (SUI) and erectile dysfunction (ED). Despite guidelines encouraging preoperative counseling, disparities in patient education may impact understanding and outcomes. We aimed to assess whether racial and age disparities exist in patients’ understanding of these complications and whether structured education influences recovery. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 86 patients who underwent prostatectomy between 2016 and 2023 at a tertiary academic center. Patients completed a digital survey via Epic MyChart, assessing their understanding of ED and SUI, awareness of risks, and exposure to pelvic floor instruction. Outcomes were analyzed using descriptive statistics and ANOVA, stratified by race, age, and education exposure. RESULTS: Preoperative SUI education was associated with higher understanding (7.46 vs. 5.61, p=0.0015) and better improvement in leakage (7.97 vs. 6.11, p=0.0018). Pelvic floor instruction improved comprehension and recovery. Racial disparities were evident: Black patients reported lower understanding (5.44) than White (7.24) and Other (7.33) patients. Understanding declined with age, from 6.93 in patients <60 to 5.84 in those≥70. CONCLUSIONS: Structured education improves functional recovery after prostatectomy. However, significant disparities exist by race and age. These findings support the need for standardized and equitable preoperative counseling protocols in urologic oncology.

title: POSTCODE LOTTERY AND LOCALISED PROSTATE CANCER: DOES ADDRESS IMPACT UPON TREATMENT OFFERINGS AND PATIENT CHOICE?
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Deepika Reddy, Ellen Benn, Noor Bhatti, Jonathan Noel
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Once diagnosed with localised prostate cancer patients are faced with a variety of management options ranging from active surveillance to radical therapies including systemic treatment. Multi-disciplinary team meetings and clinics work to standardise decision making between clinicians and patients, by offering nuanced expert opinions upon appropriate management options. We determined if there were differences in MDT decision making, and patient selection of treatment option based upon indices of deprivation; a scoring system based on postcode. METHODS: A prospective review of patients diagnosed with prostate cancer (<rT4N0M0) between Oct 2024-Mar 2025. All patients received PSA, biparametric MRI and transperineal prostate biopsy+/-whole body imaging as appropriate. Primary outcome was to determine if differences in patient treatment choice, per D’Amico risk group, differed according to health and disability decile (HDD). Secondary outcomes included differences in incidence of each risk group per HDD and index of multiple deprivation (IDD), patient treatment choice and treatment offering according to HDD and IDD. RESULTS: 282 patients were diagnosed with localised prostate cancer and reviewed in MDT. 39, 171 and 72 patients were diagnosed with D’Amico low-, intermediate-and high-risk disease respectively. No statistically significant differences in D’Amico classification following diagnosis according to HDD or IDD were noted (p=0.404 and p=0.522 respectively). No statistically significant differences in patient choice, or treatment options offered were observed in this cohort according to HDD or IDD. CONCLUSIONS: Decision making within a multidisciplinary setting demonstrates standardisation of treatments offered and chosen by patients throughout a heterogenous cohort. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: DO MDTS LEVEL TREATMENT DECISION AND PATIENT CHOICE FOR PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH LOCALISED PROSTATE CANCER: AN EVALUATION OF ETHNICITY
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Deepika Reddy, Ellen Benn, Noor Bhatti, Jonathan Noel
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Patients of black descent have a higher incidence of prostate cancer and are often diagnosed with higher grade and later stage disease when compared to patients of Caucasian descent. Understanding of disease progression between the two ethnic groups once diagnosed with similar disease profiles is limited, thus patients should be offered similar treatment options. We evaluated if there were differences in treatment options offered to and chosen by patients with localised prostate cancer. METHODS: We evaluated patients reported in a prospective registry following diagnosis of localised prostate cancer (<rT4N0M0) between Oct 2024-Mar 2025. All patients received PSA, biparametric MRI and transperineal prostate biopsy+/-whole body imaging as appropriate. Primary outcome was to determine differences in treatment options chosen by patients of black and white descent per D’Amico risk group. Secondary outcomes included if treatment options offered per ethnic groups per D’Amico risk group differed. RESULTS: 116 patients of Caucasian and 110 of black descent were diagnosed with localised prostate cancer. 13, 76 & 27 Caucasian descent patients and 18, 63 & 29 Black descent patients had D’Amico low-, intermediate-and high-risk disease respectively (p=0.38). No significant differences in patient choice and treatment offering were noted between ethnicities. CONCLUSIONS: Despite differing incidence of prostate cancer reported in the literature, we did not demonstrate differences between ethnicities in risk stratification following diagnosis of localised prostate cancer. Further, no statistically significant differences were identified in the offering of treatment options and patient treatment choice after consideration of risk stratification. Standardisation may be a result of multidisciplinary review of treatment options and counselling of appropriate options with patients. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: IMPACT OF SOCIOECONOMIC DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH ON TREATMENT TIMELINES IN BLADDER CANCER: AN ANALYSIS OF THE NATIONAL CANCER DATABASE
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Mohamed Javid Raja Iyub, Pushan Prabhakar, Ahil Mahendra, Ahmed Eldefrawy, Murugesan Manoharan
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The impact of demographic and socioeconomic determinants on delays to cancer care for those with bladder cancer is not well studied. Our objective was to analyze the relationship between socioeconomic determinants of health and treatment delay in bladder cancer patients. METHODS: The National Cancer Database was queried for patients with bladder cancer from 2004 to 2021. Treatment delay was defined, based on the literature, as the initiation of neoadjuvant chemotherapy or radical cystectomy more than three months from the time of diagnosis. Demographic and socioeconomic variables were compared between patients with and without treatment delays, and multivariate logistic regression (LR) was done to assess the impact \[odds ratio (OR)\] of different variables on treatment delay. RESULTS: Of the 47,161 patients included in our study, 8,074 (17.12%) experienced treatment delay. Patients older than 70 years and males experienced a greater delay than younger patients and females (p<0.001). Similarly, black individuals \[7.3% (delay) vs 5.4%\ (no delay)\], patients with higher comorbid score (Charlson-Deyo Comorbid score≥3: 5.1% vs 3.9%), median income less than $46,277 (16.7% vs 14.1%), those in last two lower education level quartiles (16.7% vs 14.1% and 25.4% vs 24.2%) and patients utilizing government insurance (69.9% vs 66%) encountered more delays (all p<0.001). LR analysis revealed that older individuals (age > 80: OR 1.235, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 1.115 – 1.368), black patients (OR: 1.346, CI 1.220 – 1.484), and a comorbid score≥3 (OR: 1.309, CI 1.168 – 1.467) had higher odds of treatment delay (all p<0.001). Higher education levels and female patients (OR: 0.799, CI 0.754–0.847) had a lower probability of delay (all p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, 17.2% of bladder cancer patients experienced treatment delay. Patients older than 70 years, males, black individuals, individuals with a median income less than $46,277, patients in the lower two education quartiles, those claiming government insurance, and patients with greater comorbid scores were observed more in the treatment delay group. LR analysis revealed that older age (OR: 1.235), black individuals (OR:1.346), and higher comorbid score (OR: 1.309) had higher odds, and higher education level and female patients (0.799) had lower odds of delayed treatment.

title: NON-METASTATIC BLADDER CANCER DISPARITIES AMONG HISPANICS IN THE UNITED STATES USING THE NATIONAL CANCER DATABASE
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Pablo E. Puente, Matthew S. Del Pino, Julian V. Pacheco, Daniel M. Moreira
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Bladder cancer (BC) features significant racial and ethnic disparities. Hispanic Americans, a diverse population with distinct genetic, socioeconomic, and cultural backgrounds, experience lower BC incidence than non-Hispanic Whites, while presenting with more advanced disease. Prior studies have treated Hispanics as a homogeneous group, potentially masking subgroup-specific disparities. This study evaluates differences in BC stage at diagnosis, treatments, and survival outcomes among Hispanics using the National Cancer Database (NCDB). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 11,336 Hispanics (2004-2020) with urothelial BC. Patients were categorized into six groups based on country of origin: Mexican/Chicano, Puerto Rican, Cuban, South/Central American, Dominican, and Hispanic not otherwise specified. The subgroups were analyzed using Chi-square and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess survival differences. RESULTS: Stage at diagnosis varied significantly, with Cubans having the highest muscle-invasive BC (MIBC) rate (20.9%) and Dominicans the lowest (14.3%). Treatment patterns also differed across groups; among MIBC patients, Cubans had the lowest rate of radical cystectomy (24.2%) and the highest rate of local treatment (73.3%) (p=0.028). Differences in overall survival were seen among Hispanics with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), where Cubans had a 34% higher mortality risk (HR=1.34, p=0.002), while Dominicans and South/Central Americans had lower risks (HR=0.67, p=0.015; HR=0.68, p<0.001, respectively) compared to Mexicans. Among MIBC patients, survival was not significantly different (p=0.16) across groups. CONCLUSIONS: Hispanic subgroup disparities in BC stage at presentation, survival, and treatment highlight the need for targeted interventions. Aggregating Hispanics into a single category may obscure critical differences in BC care. Differences in healthcare access, immigration status, socioeconomic and structural determinants of health likely contribute to these disparities.

title: CUMULATIVE SOCIAL DISADVANTAGE AND RISK OF OVERACTIVE BLADDER: A NATIONAL CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY WITH MACHINE LEARNING AND MEDIATION ANALYSIS
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Weilong Lin, Hai Huang
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a prevalent urological disorder that impairs quality of life and disproportionately affects socially vulnerable populations. The influence of social determinants of health (SDoH) on OAB risk and severity remains underexplored. METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from 31,324 adults in the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2005 to 2018. Eight SDoH indicators were examined, and a cumulative SDoH score was created. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed associations between SDoH and OAB risk. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses explored demographic variation and robustness. Mediation analysis evaluated the indirect role of comorbidities. Multiple machine learning algorithms were applied for prediction, with SHAP analysis for feature interpretation. RESULTS: Six SDoH including unemployment, low income-to-poverty ratio, food insecurity, low education, non-private insurance, and lack of home ownership were independently associated with increased OAB risk. A clear dose-response relationship was observed, with risk rising as adverse SDoH accumulated (P for trend < 0.0001). Subgroups at heightened risk included men, middle-aged adults, and White individuals. Depression, obesity, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and hypertension partially mediated these associations, with depression exerting the strongest effect. Among eight machine learning models, gradient boosting performed best with an AUC of 0.75. SHAP analysis identified age, BMI, and cumulative SDoH as the most influential predictors. A nomogram was developed for individualized risk estimation. CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative social disadvantage significantly contributes to OAB risk and severity, partly through mental and physical health pathways. Addressing SDoH may be vital for effective OAB prevention and management.

title: SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH AND ELECTIVE SURGERY CANCELLATIONS
session: Improving Access and Outcomes Across All Populations I (IP01)
authors: Stephanie Miller, Stephen Leahy, Stephanie Brierly, Gwen Grimsby
