Secondary endpoints: intra- and postoperative complications, length of stay (LOS), residual tumour at re-TURBT, and 24-month oncologic outcomes (recurrence, progression, overall and cancer-specific survival). RESULTS: These are interim analyses after randomization of 82 patients (HoLEBT n=40; RTUb n=42). Final results may be available at the time of presentation, as the last cases are expected to complete in December 2025. Baseline age and tumor size were comparable between arms. Operative time (median \[IQR\]) was 38.4 min \[31.9–45.1\] for HoLEBT vs 42.6 min \[32.3–53.0\] for RTUb (p=0.495). Detrusor muscle was present in 80.0% vs 71.4% of specimens (p=0.44). Bladder perforation occurred in 0/40 vs 8/42 cases (p=0.003), and obturator reflex in 0/40 vs 8/42 (p=0.003). Length of stay was 1.68 vs 1.97 days (p=0.48). Hematuria requiring >2 days of irrigation or readmission occurred in 4/40 vs 9/42 (p=0.132). CONCLUSIONS: In tumors >3 cm, HoLEBT appears feasible and demonstrates a markedly lower rate of perforation and obturator reflex compared with monopolar TURBT, with similar operative time, LOS, and detrusor muscle presence in this interim. This RCT directly addresses the evidence gap for larger bladder tumors and may influence endoscopic management in this subset. Final results, including oncologic endpoints, are anticipated to provide additional guidance on technique selection.

title: EFFICACY OF NADOFARAGENE FIRADENOVEC IN DOUBLY RESISTANT PATIENTS: A REAL WORLD CASE SERIES
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Brandon Ward, Monica Bevilacqua, Wei Shen Tan, David Hesse, Fady Ghali
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: BCG-unresponsive (BCG-U) non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) remains a formidable clinical challenge, with high recurrence and progression risk. Treatment strategies vary significantly, and many patients receive multiple therapies in hopes of avoiding radical cystectomy. Nadofaragene firadenovec (NF), a non-replicating adenoviral vector delivering IFN-α2b, was recently approved for BCG-U NMIBC. This study reports outcomes of NF use in highly pre-treated BCG-U NMIBC following treatment with both BCG and gemcitabine + docetaxel (gem/doc). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with high-risk NMIBC treated with NF who met FDA BCG-U criteria and had prior gem/doc. All declined or were ineligible for cystectomy. Demographic, clinical, and treatment data were collected. Outcomes included complete response (CR) (absence of high-grade recurrence on cystoscopy, urine cytology, or biopsy), cystectomy, and adverse events (AEs). Kaplan-Meier analysis censored patients at recurrence or last follow-up. RESULTS: 18 patients received NF following BCG and gem/doc failure. Median age was 77.4 years (IQR 73.2–81.5); 83% male, 94% White. Patients received a median of 16.5 BCG, 14 gem/doc and 2 (IQR 1-3) NF instillations. 94% of patients declined cystectomy, 11% were deemed medically ineligible. Median time from NMIBC diagnosis to NF was 6.4 years (IQR 4.3-11.1). Of 10 patients (55.6%) with ≥3 months of CR, 7 recurred and 3 maintained CR at last follow-up of 3, 6, and 9 months. On Kaplan–Meier analysis of CR patients, median response was 4.9 months (IQR 3.1–6.5). Two (11%) underwent cystectomy, one had pT2 disease (both N0). AEs occurred in 33%: grade 1–2 in 22%, grade 3 in 6%, and grade 4 in 6%. Events included fever, UTI, unsteadiness, hypertension, and one febrile illness with altered mental status requiring hospitalization. No deaths occurred. CONCLUSIONS: While NF achieved CR in a portion of BCG and gem/doc-refractory NMIBC patients (55.6%), 72% of all patients recurred within 6 months and none achieved 12-month CR. Nearly all declined cystectomy despite surgical candidacy, reflecting real-world patient preference for bladder sparing therapies. These findings suggest that patients who failed both BCG and gem/doc could represent a biologically resistant cohort compared with BCG-U alone, less likely to benefit from NF. Studies elucidating the optimal sequencing of BCG-U agents are needed.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A URINARY EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE MIRNA-PAIR MODEL FOR THE NON-INVASIVE DIAGNOSIS OF UROTHELIAL CARCINOMA
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Yucai Wu, Shiming He, Liqun Zhou, Xuesong Li, Yanqing Gong
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Urothelial carcinoma (UC) is the most common malignancy of the urinary tract. Current diagnostic methods, such as cystoscopy and urine cytology, are either invasive or have limited sensitivity. Urinary extracellular vesicles (EVs) contain stable microRNAs (miRNAs) that may serve as promising non-invasive biomarkers. This study aimed to develop and validate a miRNA-pair-based diagnostic model for UC using EV-derived miRNAs. METHODS: Urine samples were collected from 43 UC patients and 34 patients with non-malignant urinary diseases as the NGS discovery cohort. EVs were isolated using a ZrO2 magnetic bead adsorption method, followed by characterization through transmission electron microscopy (TEM), nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), and Western blotting. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis combined with a genetic algorithm. For PCR validation, an independent cohort comprising 71 UC patients, 42 with non-malignant urinary diseases, and 57 healthy controls was analyzed. A logistic regression model was constructed using the qPCR cohort as a training set. An independent external validation set (51 UC, 72 benign urinary diseases, and 51 other cancers) was used to assess diagnostic performance. RESULTS: 34 discriminative miRNA pairs that showed distinct clustering between cancer and benign samples. Recursive feature elimination with logistic regression identified three optimal miRNA pairs (hsa-miR-21-5p/hsa-miR-27a-3p, hsa-miR-96-5p/hsa-miR-152-3p, hsa-let-7c-5p/hsa-miR-29c-5p) that showed significant differences between UC and control groups (p<0.05). The three-pair miRNA model achieved an AUC of 0.90 in the training cohort and 0.88 in the external validation cohort. The model score significantly differentiated UC patients from benign and healthy controls, as well as from other cancer types. The diagnostic sensitivity and specificity were 93.0% and 74.7% in the training cohort, and 86.3% and 78.0% in the validation cohort, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a novel urinary EV-based miRNA-pair model with high accuracy for non-invasive diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma. The three-pair miRNA signature demonstrated robust performance across multiple cohorts and holds promise for clinical application as a simple, reproducible liquid biopsy tool.

title: MACROPHAGE-ENCAPSULATED ENGINEERED ECN EXPRESSING IL-15&IL-15RΑFUSION PROTEIN ENHANCES THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY IN INTRAVESICAL THERAPY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Rong Yang, Ying Sun, Yuanchun Ma, Xing Yang, Hongqian Guo
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) in bladder cancer is limited by adverse reactions and a high rate of treatment failure. We propose an innovative approach: a recombinant Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) strain engineered to express an IL-15&IL-15Rα fusion protein (EcNIL-15), encapsulated within macrophages endowed with tumor-specific tropism and adhesion capabilities (Macs@EcNIL-15). This system enables targeted intratumoral delivery and sustained release of the IL-15/IL-15Rα complex, promoting specific tumor cell killing. METHODS: The recombinant EcNIL-15 strain expressing the IL-15&IL-15Rα fusion protein was constructed. Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were used to encapsulate EcNIL-15. The release of EcNIL-15 and IL-15&IL-15Rα expression were validated using bladder cancer organoids and an orthotopic bladder cancer model. The therapeutic efficacy and safety of Macs@EcNIL-15 instillation were assessed in orthotopic bladder tumor models. RESULTS: We generated the recombinant EcNIL-15 strain, and confirmed the expression and secretion of the IL-15&IL-15Rα in vitro. The supernatant from EcNIL-15 cultures significantly promoted T-cell proliferation in co-culture with splenocytes. Immunofluorescence assays verified the intratumoral colonization and IL-15&IL-15Rα expression by EcNIL-15. Encapsulation within macrophages significantly enhanced the intratumoral colonization and expansion efficiency of EcNIL-15 in vivo (Tropism). The released EcNIL-15 specifically colonized and proliferated within tumors, effectively preventing bacterial entry into the bloodstream or infection of other organs (Safety). The sustained secretion of IL-15&IL-15Rα induced potent activation and proliferation of T cells and NK cells (Efficacy). The intratumoral colonization of EcNIL-15 persisted for several weeks before gradual immune clearance, allowing for sustained local IL-15&IL-15Rα production and enabling long-term tumor suppression with a single administration. Intravesical Macs@EcNIL-15 resulted in significant tumor regression in the orthotopic model and a marked prolongation of mouse survival. CONCLUSIONS: We have developed a novel intravesical therapy for bladder cancer. Macs@EcNIL-15 enables specific adhesion and infiltration into bladder tumors, and a single instillation facilitates rapid intratumoral colonization by EcNIL-15 and the sustained release of the IL-15&IL-15Rα fusion protein, leading to continuous immune cell activation and direct tumor killing, thereby achieving potent and durable antitumor effects.

title: PREDICTING CANCER-SPECIFIC MORTALITY IN NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER: COMPARATIVE PERFORMANCE OF AUA VS EAU RISK CLASSIFICATIONS
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Mattia Longoni, Pietro Scilipoti, Mario de Angelis, Paolo Zaurito, Giovanni Tremolada, Alfonso Santangelo, Giuseppe Simone, Riccardo Mastroianni, Chiara Lonati, Stefania Zamboni, Nazareno Suardi, Gautier Marcq, Aleksandra Szostek, Jorge Caño Velasco, Alfonso Lafuente Puentedura, José Daniel Subiela, Pedro del Olmo Durán, Aleksander Ślusarczyk, Pierre I. Karakiewicz, Benjamin Pradere, Francesco Soria, Paolo Gontero, Morgan Roupret, Francesco Montorsi, Andrea Salonia, Alberto Briganti, Marco Moschini
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Risk stratification in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) traditionally focuses on recurrence and progression, as in the European Association of Urology (EAU) and American Urological Association (AUA) classifications. Since these events ultimately drive cancer-specific mortality (CSM), assessing their ability to predict CSM may refine patient counseling and follow-up. We compared the accuracy of these models in predicting CSM. METHODS: We relied on 2192 consecutive patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) treated with transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) at seven tertiary-referral European centers (2015-2022). Patients were categorized according to: (1) the 2021 EAU classification into low- (LR), intermediate- (IR), high- (HR), and very high-risk (VHR) groups, based on T stage, WHO 1978/2004 grade, presence of carcinoma in situ (CIS), and additional factors (age >70 years, multifocality, and tumor size ≥3 cm); and (2) the AUA classification, which lacks a VHR group but expands HR category. Kaplan-Meier estimates were used to assess CSM. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) values at 2 and 5 years were calculated to test model discrimination. RESULTS: Median age was 70 years (IQR: 63-77). Overall, 1364 (62%) harbored Ta, 702 (32%) T1, and 118 (5.3%) Tis stage; 328 (15%) had CIS, 1254 (57%) HG disease, and 135 (6.2%) VH. Multifocality was reported in 989 (45%) patients, with median tumor size of 2 cm (IQR: 1-3). According to EAU criteria, 501 (23%) were LR, 989 (45%) IR, 599 (27%) HR, and 126 (5.6%) VHR; according to AUA criteria, 370 (17%) were LR, 1,005 (45%) IR, and 840 (38%) HR. Median follow-up was 49 months (IQR: 30-68). The 2- and 5-year CSM rates were 0.0% and 1.3% for EAU LR vs. 2.3% and 4.5% for IR vs. 7.1% and 14% for HR vs. 6% and 15% for VHR patients; corresponding values for AUA were 0.0%, 4.7%, and 4.8% at 2 years and 0.0%, 9.3%, and 10% at 5 years. The EAU classification demonstrated superior discrimination for CSM (AUC 0.70 vs. 0.58 at 2 years, p=0.028; 0.75 vs. 0.61 at 5 years, p=0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Although developed to predict recurrence and progression, both models provide prognostic insight into CSM. The EAU classification showed superior accuracy compared with the AUA system, supporting its broader prognostic utility in NMIBC.

title: RISK STRATIFICATION OF TA HIGH-GRADE NON–MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER: INSIGHTS FROM A MULTICENTER COHORT STUDY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Paolo Zaurito, Pietro Scilipoti, Mattia Longoni, Aleksander Ślusarczyk, Francesco Soria, Benjamin Pradere, Wojciech Krajewski, David D’andrea, Andrea Mari, Renate Pichler, José Daniel Subiela, Gautier Marcq, Giuseppe Simone, Ekaterina Laukhtina, Javier Aranda, Jorge Caño Velasco, Rodolfo Hurle, Piotr Radziszewski, Shahrokh F. Shariat, Paolo Gontero, Francesco Montorsi, Andrea Salonia, Alberto Briganti, Marco Moschini
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The oncological risk of Ta high-grade (TaHG) non–muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) patients remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the oncological outcomes of TaHG patients treated with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) by applying the 2021 European Association of Urology (EAU) risk stratification and assessing the prognostic value of individual risk factors. METHODS: We identified 529 TaHG patients without carcinoma in situ (CIS) treated with BCG from 16 tertiary centers between 2003 and 2024. As a comparator arm, a total of 151 ‘pure’ intermediate risk (IR) NMIBC patients (with recurrent TaLG and T1LG tumors) treated with BCG were also included. BCG failure was defined as the development of BCG-unresponsive status, BCG relapsing status or identification of muscle invasive bladder cancer during follow-up. TaHG patients were stratified in three groups based on the number of EAU risk factors (i. e. age >70 year, multifocality and tumor size >3 cm; 0, 1, 2-3 risk factors). Cumulative incidence analyses and Cox regression models analyzed the 5-yr risk of HG-recurrence, progression and BCG failure among TaHG patients stratified according to the number of EAU risk factors and compared their risk with those of ‘pure’ IR-NMIBC patients. RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 40 months (IQR: 37-42), 114 (22%) TaHG patients experienced a HG-recurrence, 49 (9%) patients had progression and 107 (20%) had BCG failure. No differences in rates of HG-recurrence, progression and BCG failure were detected among TaHG patients within risk groups based on the number of EAU risk factors. Patients with IR-NMIBC (recurrent TaLG and T1LG) had a significant lower risk of 5-yr HG-recurrence (14%) compared to IR-TaHG (25%, p=0.038) and high-risk (HR)-TaHG (31%, p=0.003) ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191276.85430.b0.12#F1)). Similarly, IR-NMIBC patients had a significant lower risk of 5-yr progression (6%) compared to IR-TaHG (13%) and HR-TaHG (15%) (all p<0.05). Patients with IR-TaHG (adjusted OR: 2.07) and HR-TaHG (adjusted OR: 2.45) had a significant higher risk of BCG failure compared to IR-NMIBC (all p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with TaHG NMIBC represent a homogenous population associated with higher risk of HG-recurrence, progression and BCG failure compared to ‘pure’ IR-NMIBC. These findings may support the consideration of all TaHG tumors as high-risk in clinical practice, regardless of individual risk factors.

title: THERAPY-INDUCED TERTIARY LYMPHOID STRUCTURES IN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT REFLECT IMMUNE REPROGRAMMING AFTER INTRAVESICAL BACILLUS CALMETTE-GUERIN FOR NON-MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Daiki Ikarashi, Shigehisa Kitano, Tatsuya Kawamura, Kenta Takahashi, Ayato Ito, Ei Shiomi, Masakazu Abe, Shigekatsu Maekawa, Renpei Kato, Mitsugu Kanehira, Wataru Obara
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) is standard of care for intermediate- and high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). Recently, immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) was indicated for BCG-unresponsible NMIBC. Recent evidence suggests that tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) within the tumor microenvironment (TME) may play a critical role in orchestrating antitumor immune responses. However, the change in the TME including forming TLS before and after BCG remains unclear. In this study, we assessed the association of TME and BCG treatment for NMIBC. METHODS: Our retrospective study included 18 BCG-unresponsible patients with intermediate- and high-risk NMIBC. Tissue samples were obtained through transurethral biopsy or resection before and after the administration of BCG in all patients. Post-BCG samples were collected when intravesical recurrence as BCG-unresponsible. Additionally, tissues from patients with acute bacterial cystitis were analyzed as controls. We assessed the density of several immune cell types (CD4, CD8, Foxp3, Bcl6, CD204, CD20, CD21, CD38) in intra-tumoral and peri-tumoral areas between pre-BCG and post-BCG tissues via multiplex fluorescence immunohistochemical analysis. RESULTS: BCG-unresponsible was classified as BCG-refractory in 3 cases, BCG-resistance in 5 cases and BCG-relapsing in 10 cases. The formation of TLS was observed in 11 cases (61%) in post-BCG tissues, while TLS was not observed in all cases in the pre-BCG tissues and acute bacterial cystitis tissues. Seven cases of TLS non-formation were all BCG relapsing cases. Comparison according to TLS formation revealed a difference in the timing of recurrence. In peri-tumoral areas, the densities of TLS-associated cells, including CD20+ and CD38+ cells, were significantly higher (p=0.029 and p=0.013, respectively), while the densities of CD21+ and Bcl6+ cells also tended to be higher in the TME of post-BCG tissue compared with pre-BCG tissue. In the intra-tumoral area, there was no difference in the change in immune cells between pre-BCG and post-BCG tissues. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that TLS formation in the TME may be associated with early recurrence following BCG treatment, which may benefit from ICIs for BCG-unresponsible NMIBC.

title: BCG THERAPY RESHAPES THE URINARY MICROBIOME AND IMMUNE CELL LANDSCAPE IN NON–MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Yuki Oda, Makito Miyake, Kazuki Miyazaki, Nobutaka Nishimura, Akira Tachibana, Mitsuru Tomizawa, Takuto Shimizu, Kenta Onishi, Shunta Hori, Yosuke Morizawa, Daisuke Gotho, Yasushi Nakai, Tatsuo Yoneda, Nobumichi Tanaka, Kiyohide Fujimoto
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Intravesical BCG is the standard treatment for intermediate- and high-risk NMIBC; however, 30–40% of patients experience recurrence or progression. The bladder immune milieu and urinary microbiota may be associated with its efficacy; however, their longitudinal interplay remains unclear. Here, we aimed to define these temporal interactions and their clinical relevance. METHODS: This single-center prospective study included 23 patients with NMIBC who completed six BCG instillations. Urine was collected at four time points: pre-TURBT, pre-induction BCG, post-induction BCG, and 3 months later. Urinary sediment transcripts (PD-L1, PD-L2, CD33, MSR1/CD204) were quantified using qRT-PCR, and the microbiota was profiled using 16S rRNA V3–V4 sequencing. Alpha and beta diversity and microbe–immune associations were tested using linear mixed-effects models, and progression risk was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazard model. RESULTS: PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression levels increased significantly after BCG induction (P=0.003), and CD33 and MSR1 showed similar upward trends. Alpha and beta -diversity did not change over time. Lower Actinobacteria and enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae were associated with lower PD-L1 and higher MSR1 expression, respectively. These findings align with reduced IFN-γ/STAT1–IRF1-dependent PD-L1 induction and activation of the IL-10–PPARγ/LXR–MSR1 axis under heightened LPS tone. The Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio and relative abundance of Enterobacteriaceae correlated with PD-L1 dynamics. Post-BCG immune and microbiota indices were significantly associated with longer progression-free survival. CONCLUSIONS: BCG induces coordinated temporal remodeling of urinary immune gene expression and the urinary microbiome. Increased PD-L1/PD-L2 and myeloid markers indicate immune reprogramming, whereas changes in the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio reflect mucosal ecology. Urine-based immune–microbiota profiling may serve as a predictor of response to BCG in patients with NMIBC.

title: SINGLE-CENTER PROSPECTIVE STUDY OF TRANSURETHRAL GAS-BLADDER ULTRASONIC SCALPEL BLADDER TUMOR RESECTION: A REPORT ON TECHNICAL FEASIBILITY AND PRELIMINARY EFFICACY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Yang Shujun, Sun Shengkun
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) requires radical cystectomy (RC). A proportion of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) also needs partial cystectomy or RC. However, RC causes numerous postoperative complications that severely reduce quality of life. For patients strongly willing to preserve the bladder, or young patients demanding high quality of life, exploring safe and effective bladder-sparing strategies is critical. This study evaluated the technical feasibility, safety, and preliminary efficacy of a novel surgery—transurethral gas-bladder ultrasonic scalpel bladder tumor resection (STURBT)—based on the self-developed S-scope (a visualized, large-channel, multi-functional platform). METHODS: This single-center, single-arm prospective trial was approved by the No. S2022-303-01 and ChiCTR2200062202. Conducted from 2022 to Dec 2024, it enrolled patients undergoing STURBT. Surgical steps: 1) Transurethral insertion of S-scope under direct vision to establish CO2 gas bladder (pressure: 6-14 mmHg); 2) Inserting ultrasonic scalpel via S-scope’s main channel, circularly incising bladder wall 1 cm from tumor edge to resect tumor and basal tissue en bloc; 3) Bipolar electrocoagulation for hemostasis; 4) Removing specimens en bloc or in pieces with a basket; 5) Irrigating the field with distilled water. Baseline data, surgical parameters, perioperative complications, postoperative pathology (muscle layer acquisition rate), and follow-up recurrence were recorded. RESULTS: 26 patients were enrolled (24 males, 2 females), with median age 61 years (range: 44-77). Median tumor size was 4.5 cm (range: 2-7). Median surgical time was 116 min (range: 25-210), median hemoglobin decrease 8 g/dL (range: 1-28). Median postoperative bladder irrigation duration was 2 days (range: 1-3). Pathological staging: 23 T1 cases, 3 T2 cases; 21 specimens (80.8%) contained muscle layer. Intraoperative/postoperative advantages: multi-instrument/energy platform collaboration, minimal blood loss, no urinary extravasation, no obturator nerve reflex. Median follow-up was 18 months (7-35); 2 patients had recurrence and underwent RC. Complications occurred in 2 cases (7.7%): 1 urethral stricture, 1 subcutaneous emphysema (both Clavien-Dindo I). CONCLUSIONS: STURBT based on S-scope was preliminarily confirmed safe, feasible, and effective in this single-center trial. It solves key limitations of traditional TURBT: en bloc resection (no fragmentation), no fluid irrigation (reduced seeding risk), clear resection margins (facilitating pathological assessment), sufficient resection depth (high muscle layer rate), no obturator nerve reflex.

title: A RANDOMIZED MULTICENTER CROSSOVER STUDY TO EVALUATE PATIENT PREFERENCE AND SATISFACTION WITH URINE-BASED MOLECULAR TESTING VERSUS CYSTOSCOPY FOR SURVEILLANCE OF NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER (NMIBC)
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Lauren A. Mestas, Lanyu Mi, Christopher Ferguson, Timonthy Lyon, Andrew Zganjar, Mireya Renteria, Mark Tyson
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Cystoscopy remains the standard for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) surveillance, but is invasive, costly, and burdensome. The Cxbladder Monitor (CxbM), a urine-based mRNA assay, offers a noninvasive alternative with validated diagnostic accuracy. We conducted a randomized, multicenter, crossover clinical trial to evaluate patient preference, satisfaction, and quality of life comparing CxbM versus cystoscopy during NMIBC surveillance. METHODS: In this trial conducted at Mayo Clinic between November 2023 and September 2025, adults with NMIBC and a minimum of 9 months of recurrence-free survival were randomized 1:1 to two distinct surveillance regimens: Arm A (CxbM at 3 months, cystoscopy at 6 months) or Arm B (reverse order). This cross-over design enabled within-subject comparisons and minimized interindividual variability. The primary endpoint was overall patient preference (Patient Preference Questionnaire, PQ). Secondary endpoints included satisfaction, convenience, time burden, health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-NMIBC24), fear of recurrence (FCRI-SF), and test performance. Comparisons were with Wilcoxon rank sum test for continuous variables and Chi-squared test for categorical variables between the two arms. RESULTS: Of the 107 patients randomized, 97 completed the study protocol; their mean age was 74 years, and 77.4% were male. CxbM was preferred by 74.2% of participants, cystoscopy by 19.4%, and 6.5% had no preference (p<0.001). CxbM was associated with markedly less pain (p<0.001), greater convenience (p<0.001), and no instances of missed work compared to cystoscopy. Five recurrences (5.2%) were detected, all noninvasive with no missed high-grade events. Discordant error rates were comparable between arms (13 (44.8%) vs 11(45.8%), p>0.99). CONCLUSIONS: Patients strongly preferred CxbM over cystoscopy, providing less pain, more convenience, and improved satisfaction while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance, quality of life, and fear of cancer recurrence. Incorporating CxbM into NMIBC surveillance may enhance patient adherence and experience without compromising oncologic safety. Guideline organizations should consider this data when refining evidence-based surveillance recommendations to optimize patient-centered care in NMIBC. | | | --- | | |

title: IMPACT OF CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE ON PROGNOSIS IN PATIENTS WITH HIGH-RISK NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER WHO UNDERWENT ADJUVANT BACILLUS CALMETTE-GUéRIN THERAPY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Naoki Fujita, Takuma Narita, Masaki Momota, Hiroyuki Ito, Kazuaki Yoshikawa, Shingo Hatakeyama
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Immune dysfunction is a well-recognized complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), potentially impairing host defense mechanisms against malignancy. Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) therapy is a cornerstone of adjuvant treatment for high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), relying on robust local immune activation to prevent tumor recurrence and progression. However, the efficacy of BCG may be compromised in individuals with CKD due to impaired immunological responses. We hypothesized that patients with CKD may exhibit suboptimal antitumor immunity following adjuvant BCG therapy, resulting in inferior oncological outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a multi-institutional retrospective study assessing 209 patients with high-risk NMIBC who underwent transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) and subsequent adjuvant induction BCG therapy from December 1998 to April 2019. Patients were divided into two groups: those with preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 60 ml/min/1.73 m2 (non-CKD group), and those with eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73 m2 (CKD group). Multivariable analyses were performed to assess the impact of CKD on intravesical recurrence and muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) progression, adjusting for the competing risk of death using the Fine-Gray competing risk regression model. RESULTS: Median age and follow-up period after TURBT were 72 years and 45 months, respectively. Of 209 patients, 71 (34%) were diagnosed with CKD before TURBT. In the Fine-Gray competing risk regression model, CKD showed significantly higher probabilities of intravesical recurrence and MIBC progression, with an adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio of 1.886 (95% confidence interval \[CI\] 1.069–3.330, P=0.028) and 3.740 (95% CI 1.060–13.20, P=0.040), respectively ( Fig. A and B). Moreover, metastasis-free survival, cancer-specific survival, and overall survival in the CKD group were significantly shorter than those in the non-CKD group (Fig. C-E). CONCLUSIONS: CKD presents a risk factor of poor oncological outcomes in patients with high-risk NMIBC who underwent adjuvant induction BCG therapy after TURBT. These findings suggest that impaired renal function may compromise the efficacy of BCG-mediated antitumor immunity, underscoring the need for tailored surveillance and therapeutic strategies in this vulnerable population.

title: PROGNOSTIC SIGNIFICANCE OF SYMPTOM-DRIVEN RECURRENCE IN HIGH-RISK NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Naoki Fujita, Masaki Momota, Hiroyuki Ito, Kazuaki Yoshikawa, Shingo Hatakeyama
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Because patients with high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) have high recurrence and progression rates, it is recommended that they undergo intensive surveillance after transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT). However, no study has demonstrated that such an intensive surveillance contributes to improving oncological outcomes. Moreover, no study has investigated an association between symptomatic recurrence and poor prognosis in patients with high-risk NMIBC. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 428 patients with primary high-risk NMIBC who underwent TURBT from November 1993 to April 2019. Of the 428 patients, 140 had experienced recurrence at any site and were divided into two groups: patients who had experienced recurrence detected by the surveillance (asymptomatic group) and patients who experienced recurrence detected by a symptom-driven investigation (symptomatic group). Background-adjusted multivariable analyses with the inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) method were performed to evaluate the impact of symptomatic recurrence on cancer-specific survival (CSS) and overall survival (OS) after first recurrence in patients who experienced recurrence. Moreover, multivariable analysis was performed to identify predictive factors of symptomatic recurrence in the entire cohort. RESULTS: Median age and follow-up periods were 72 years and 55 months, respectively. Of the 140 patients who experienced recurrence, 106 (76%) were diagnosed by a symptom-driven investigation (symptomatic group). Muscle invasive bladder cancer progression rate in the symptomatic group was significantly higher than that in the asymptomatic group (23.5% vs. 6.5%, P=0.005). CSS and OS after the first recurrence in the symptomatic group were significantly shorter than those in the asymptomatic group ( Fig. A and B). In the background-adjusted multivariable analyses with the IPTW model, symptomatic recurrence was significantly associated with shorter CSS along with shorter OS after the first recurrence ( Fig. C). In the multivariable analysis, only tumor grade was selected as a significant predictive factor of symptomatic recurrence after TURBT ( Table). CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic recurrence was significantly associated with poor oncological outcomes in patients with primary high-risk NMIBC. Patients with grade 3 tumors may require more intensive surveillance after TURBT.

title: IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT SIGNATURES OF RESPONSE TO CRETOSTIMOGENE GRENADENOREPVEC IN BCG-UNRESPONSIVE NON–MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Taylor A. Goodstein, Connor Stewart, Hongshun Shi, Jianhua Xiong, Meng Zhang, Kenneth Ogan, Jaqueline T. Brown, Valentina Grajales, William Luke, Viraj Master, Patrick Mullane, Jindan Yu, Hadyn Kissick, Shreyas Joshi, Vikram Narayan
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: A novel agent under investigation for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC is cretostimogene grenadenorepvec (creto), an adenoviral dual-mechanistic oncolytic gene therapy. The BOND-003 phase 3 clinical trial demonstrated a 75% CR rate at any time. Our tertiary care academic medical center investigated a cohort of creto-treated patients with variable responses for whom tissue is available to perform multiplex immunofluorescence (MIF), to better understand the tumor microenvironment associated with treatment response. METHODS: Patients who provided informed consent and received creto for whom at least one pre- and one post-treatment FFPE tissue sample were available were included. MIF staining was performed with the Opal Polaris 7-color fluorescence immunohistochemistry kit. Antibodies used were CD8, FoxP3, TCF1, PD1, MHC-II, and CD4. Vectra Polaris Automated Quantitative Pathology Imaging System was used for multispectral imaging. QuPath-0.2.3 was used to quantify whole slide fluorescence intensity within each cell and calculate cellular density. Patients were classified as Responder \[R\] if they had no recurrence during follow-up, Early Non-Responder \[ENR\] if they developed high-grade recurrence < 1 year after starting creto, Late Non-Responder \[LNR\] if they recurred > 1 year after starting treatment, and Progressor \[P\] if they were upstaged to > T1 at any point during follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 15 specimens from six patients were included (1 R, 3 ENRs, 1 LNR, 1 P). There was no difference in post-treatment recruitment of CD8+ or CD4+ cells between responders (R + LNR) vs non-responders (ENR + P). An increased post-treatment ratio of CD8+ to FOXP3+ cells was seen with responders compared to non-responders ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191276.85430.b0.20#F1)). An increased ratio of CD4+/FOXP3+ and CD4+/PD1+ was also seen with responders compared to non-responders. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of MIF performed in patients who received creto, pre- and post-treated tissue demonstrates immunologic hallmarks of response vs non-response that is similar to what has been shown in other studies in bladder cancer. These data indicate that effective anti-tumor immunity in this context depends less on total immune infiltration and more on the equilibrium between effector and regulatory immune subsets.

title: LONGITUDINAL QUALITY OF LIFE AFTER RADICAL CYSTECTOMY: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF OVERALL TRENDS BETWEEN MUSCLE-INVASIVE VERSUS NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Rocco Simone Flammia, Aldo Brassetti, Alfredo Bove, Umberto Anceschi, Gabriele Tuderti, Maria Consiglia Ferriero, Riccardo Mastroianni, Simone D'annunzio, Flavia Proietti, Leonardo Misuraca, Eugenio Bologna, Leslie Claire Licari, Giuseppe Chiacchio, Salvatore Guaglianone, Costantino Leonardo, Marianna Anselmi, Giuseppe Simone
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To compare Quality of life (QoL) trajectory between patients with muscle-invasive (MI) versus non-muscle-invasive (NMI) bladder cancer (BC) treated with radical cystectomy (RC). METHODS: Within our institutional database we identified all patients treated with RC for non-metastatic bladder cancer for whom QoL was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire at baseline and at multiple follow-up points up to 36 months. The overall cohort was stratified between “true” NMIBC (as confirmed by RC pathology, NMIBC-yes) vs those exhibiting MIBC either prior or at RC pathology (NMIBC-No). Spaghetti plots, linear mixed-effects models and interaction tests were used to analyze the overall trajectories and to test for differences between MIBC and NMIBC groups over time. Multivariable adjustments for age-adjusted Charlson comorbidity index, robot-assisted approach and urinary diversion were performed. RESULTS: Descriptive characteristics were reported in Table 1. At baseline, NMIBC patients exhibited lower Fatigue (FA; estimate -6.44, p=0.016) and Constipation (CO; estimate -7.63, p=0.017). However, both MIBC and NMIBC patients demonstrated significant QoL deterioration over time across multiple functional (PF, RF, SF) and symptom (FA, DY, AP, CO) domains compared to their baseline ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191276.85430.b0.21#F1)). Trajectories were largely parallel between groups, although significant interactions indicated less favorable symptom progression for NMIBC for Constipation (CO, estimate +9.80 at 3 mos, p=0.032), Insomnia (SL, Estimate +10.40 at 3 mos, p=0.021) and Diarrhoea (DY, Estimate +11.20 at 36 mos, p<0.001). Conversely, NMIBC patients showed a trajectory advantage only in Social Functioning (SF; Est. +10.45 at 12 mos, p=0.034). CONCLUSIONS: In this study, patients undergoing RC for both MIBC and NMIBC experienced a significant and sustained deterioration in several QoL domains. Contrary to potential expectations, the long-term QoL trajectories were largely parallel between the two groups. These findings suggest that the impact of RC on QoL is substantial, irrespective of the disease stage, and patient counseling should emphasize that long-term QoL changes are common for both cohorts.

title: SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF BCG ONLY, BCG PLUS EMDA-MMC, OR UPFRONT RADICAL CYSTECTOMY IN HIGH-RISK NON-MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCERS (NMIBCS): A MULTICENTRE COLLABORATIVE STUDY FROM TWO INDEPENDENT TERTIARY REFERRAL INSTITUTIONS
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Dalila Carino, Francesco Del Giudice, Valerio Santarelli, Amir Khan, Mohammed Gad, Rajesh Nair, Elsie Mensah, Felice Crocetto, Ettore De Berardinis, Youssef Ibrahim, Benjamin Challacombe, Jan Laszkiewicz, Bernardo Rocco, Giuseppe Basile, Ramesh Thurairaja, Timothy O’brien, Muhammad Shamim Khan, Yasmin Abu-Ghanem, Eila C. Skinner, Benjamin I. Chung
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: High-risk categories of Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer (NMIBC) remain a therapeutic challenge due to the substantial risk of recurrence and progression despite guideline-based intravesical therapy. The choice between conservative bladder preservation and early radical surgery is still debated, especially in those with adverse pathological features. This study compared survival outcomes among alternative treatment strategies within this high-risk setting. METHODS: High- or Very High-risk NMIBCs treated at two tertiary referral centers between 2009 and 2024 were reviewed. All patients underwent TURBT followed by one of three treatment approaches: Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) alone (I), sequential BCG plus electromotive administration of mitomycin C (EMDA-MMC) (II), or upfront radical cystectomy (RC) (III). Demographic, clinical, and pathological data were assessed. Recurrence-free survival (RFS), Progression-free Survival (PFS), and Overall Survival (OS) were estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods. Multivariable Cox regression modeling was applied to identify predictors independently associated with survival imbalances. RESULTS: A total of n=1178 patients were included, n=852 BCG only, n=249 BCG/EMDA-MMC, and n=77 upfront RC. Kaplan–Meier analysis revealed no significant differences in RFS or PFS between the BCG and BCG/EMDA-MMC groups, nor in OS among the three treatment strategies. On multivariable analysis, both recurrence and disease were not influenced by the type on intravesical treatment (HR: 0.95, 95%CI 0.732-1.238, p=0.71 for RFS and HR: 0.80, 95%CI 0.557-1.155, p=0.24 for PFS, respectively for BCG/EMDA-MMC vs. BCG only). Similarly, none of the evaluated therapeutic approaches (BCG/EMDA-MMC vs. BCG only vs. upfront RC) was independently impacting OS (HR: 1.00, 95%CI 0.701-1.424, p=1.00 for BCG/EMDA-MMC vs. BCG only: HR: 1.13, 95%CI 0.591-2.143, p=0.72 for upfront RC vs. BCG only; HR: 0.89, 95%CI 0.47-1.7, p=0.73 for BCG/EMDA-MMC vs. upfront RC). CONCLUSIONS: Survival outcomes were primarily influenced by age, tumor stage, presence of concomitant CIS, and Re-TURBT. Of note, type of treatment modality (i. e., BCG only, sequential BCG/EMDA-MMC, or upfront RC) did not significantly affect RFS, PFS, or OS. These findings suggest that patient and tumor characteristics, rather than treatment modality, may preferably guide individualized management decisions in high-risk NMIBCs.

title: DURATION OF RESPONSE TO UGN-102 BY AGE AT BASELINE ACROSS 3 CLINICAL TRIALS IN PATIENTS WITH LOW-GRADE INTERMEDIATE-RISK BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Ashish M. Kamat, William C. Huang, Neal D. Shore, Michael J. Louie, Nikky Ugwuoke, Brent Burger, Mark Schoenberg, Princeton, Sandip M. Prasad
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: UGN-102, a reverse thermal hydrogel formulation of mitomycin (75 mg), is FDA-approved for the treatment of adult patients with recurrent low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC). Emerging data suggest that while bladder cancer is mostly diagnosed in older adults (≥70 years), young onset bladder cancer (YOBC) has a distinct profile with higher percentage of LG disease. Here we assessed the therapeutic efficacy of UGN-102 in different age groups, across three prospective clinical trials. METHODS: Data were pooled from three studies. OPTIMA II (NCT03558503)1 and ENVISION (NCT05243550)2 were single arm studies and in ATLAS (NCT04688931)3, patients were randomized to receive UGN-102 or transurethral resection. Only the UGN-102 treated patients are included in this analysis. All patients were randomized to receive six once-weekly intravesical instillations of UGN-102. Eligible patients had LG-IR-NMIBC with ≥1 prior episode of NMIBC. Outcomes included complete response (CR) at 3-months, and Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimates of duration of response (DoR) up to 12 months (pooled) and up to 24 months (ENVISION). RESULTS: In total, 338 patients treated with UGN-102 were included in this analysis. The CR rates at 3 months in the pooled data were 78.4% (29/37) and 75.7% (228/301) in patients <55 and ≥55 years, respectively. The CR rates were 73.5% (86/117) and 77.4% (171/221) in patients <65 and ≥65 years, respectively. The KM estimate of DoR was ≥ 75.9% in all pooled age subgroups at 12 months after CR, and ≥70.0% across ENVISION subgroups at 24 months after CR. In ENVISION, the median KM DoR was 29.63 months (95% CI: NE,NE) in patients <65 years; this was not estimable in the other age subgroups due to the low event rate. CONCLUSIONS: UGN-102 demonstrated robust CR rates across all age groups. Most patients remained event-free 12 months after CR in pooled data, and 24 months after CR in ENVISION. These findings support UGN-102 as an effective, durable, and age-independent treatment option for recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. Limitations include the small size of some subgroups. 1\. Chevli KK, et al. J Urol. 2022;207(1):61–9. 2\. Prasad SM, et al. J Urol. 2025;213(2):205–16. 3\. Prasad SM, et al. J Urol. 2023;210(4):619–29. | | | --- | | |

title: PATIENT EXPERIENCES AND PREFERENCES FOR CHEMOABLATION AND INTRAVESICAL DRUG-RELEASING SYSTEMS IN NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER — A MIXED-METHODS STUDY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Zeeshan Zubair, Samuel Benisti, Kyle A. Richards
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) remains the gold standard for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), yet emerging office-based intravesical therapies offer less invasive alternatives. Patient perspectives on the procedural burden of TURBT and preferences for novel therapies remain poorly characterized. This study examines patient experiences with TURBT and their preferences when presented with alternative intravesical approaches. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, mixed-methods study of 80 NMIBC patients aged >18 years who had undergone at least one TURBT within the past two years. Patients were stratified by tumor grade (low vs high). Quantitative surveys assessed demographics, treatment history, and preferences among repeat TURBT, chemoablation (UGN-102), and an intravesical drug-releasing system (TAR-200). Semi-structured interviews were conducted via a secure virtual platform using a standardized questionnaire covering TURBT experiences and hypothetical treatment scenarios informed by published efficacy and side-effect data. Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis identified key patient perspectives. RESULTS: Of the 80 eligible patients, 40 completed semi-structured phone interviews (21 low-grade, 19 high-grade; 50% response rate). The mean age was 70 years (range, 46–89), and 75% of the participants were male. Most (70%) described their TURBT experience as positive but cited emotional stress (32%), anesthesia burden (19%), and recovery time (13%) as notable challenges. When presented with alternatives, 50% preferred chemoablation to avoid anesthesia and frequent procedures, while 50% favored TURBT for reassurance of complete removal. In contrast, 94% preferred TURBT over TAR-200, citing doubts about efficacy. Nearly half (48%) stated that information about clinical trials would have influenced their treatment choices. Thematic analysis identified three domains: (1) procedural fatigue, (2) desire for shared decision-making, and (3) openness to less-invasive therapy. CONCLUSIONS: While most patients reported positive TURBT experiences, nearly half would have considered a clinical trial. Patients expressed interest in novel delivery systems for chemoablation, but only half preferred this approach over TURBT when efficacy was equal, underscoring that outcome efficacy outweighs procedural burden.

title: PREDICTORS OF DISEASE RECURRENCE AND PROGRESSION OF NON-MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER FOLLOWING EN BLOC RESECTION OF BLADDER TUMOUR
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Mahmoud Laymon, Christophe Chemasle, Pietro Spatafora, Selçuk Erdem, Mohamed Amine Lakmichi, Roman Recher, Lukas Lusuardi, Angus Chin On Luk, Esat Korgali, Andrea Mari, Chen-Yueh Wen, Claudia Zaccaro, Kenneth Chen, Shanjeev Karuppusamy Murali, Sami Ben Rhouma, Antonio Luigi Pastore, Shahrokh Shariat, Vineet Gauhar, Rossella Nicoletti, Chi Ho Leung, Chris Ho Ming Wong, Jeremy Yuen-Chun Teoh
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To investigate the predictors of oncological outcomes of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) following en bloc resection of bladder tumour (ERBT). METHODS: The Global ERBT Registry (NCT04934540) is a prospective multinational database contributed by 74 institutes from 27 countries. Baseline patient and disease characteristics were recorded. Only patients with histologically confirmed NMIBC were included in this analysis. Primary outcomes were 1-year recurrence rate and 1-year progression rate. Multivariable Cox regression analyses were also performed. RESULTS: A total of 2216 NMIBC patients who received ERBT were included in this analysis. The median age was 69 years. The median tumour size was 1.7 cm, and the median number of tumour was 1. 80% were primary tumours, and 64% had single tumour. 68% of the patients had Ta disease, and the rest (32%) had T1 disease. 46% of them had high-grade disease, 52% had low-grade disease, and 2% had papillary urothelial neoplasm of low malignancy potential. 7.1% of the patients had concomitant carcinoma-in-situ (CIS). Detrusor muscle sampling rate was 77%, and clear resection margin was achieved in 85% of them. Overall, the 1-year recurrence rate was 16% and the 1-year progression rate was 1.3%. Upon multivariable analyses, recurrent (HR 2.12, 95% 1.52-2.94), multiple (HR 1.39, 95% 1.03-1.89), and high-grade tumours (HR 1.44, 95% 1.03-2.02) were associated with disease recurrence; T1 disease (HR 11.1, 95% 1.35-90.3), and presence of CIS (HR 3.99, 95% 1.31-12.1) were associated with disease progression. CONCLUSIONS: In NMIBC patients who received ERBT, recurrent, multiple and high-grade tumours were associated with disease recurrence; T1 disease and presence of CIS were associated with disease progression.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A NON-MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER (NMIBC) GENOMIC SCORE (NGS) THAT OUTPERFORMS CLINICAL PARAMETERS TO PREDICT EARLY BCG FAILURE
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Mark Farha, Jacob Lang, Gal Wald, Runzhuo Ma, Noah Freydenlund, Vincent D'Andrea, Ali Ghasemzadeh, Eugene Pietzak
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Although BCG is the standard of care for high-grade (HG)-NMIBC, half of patients recur and 25% progress. Given emerging intravesical therapies, better biomarkers are needed to identify patients at risk for BCG failure. METHODS: We included HG-NMIBC patients treated at Memorial Sloan Kettering (MSKCC) who developed early BCG failure \[HG recurrence within 6 months of complete induction (n=24)\] or long-term response \[no recurrence 5+ years after complete induction (n=40)\]. All underwent targeted exome sequencing with MSK-IMPACT. Three machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine) were employed for genomic feature selection using a stratified 60:40 train-test split and 5-fold cross validation. Random forest achieved the highest test AUC and was selected for feature identification. A normalized NMIBC Genomic Score (NGS) from 0 to 100 was developed using variable importance weights, with patients stratified into risk groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression adjusting for AUA risk, demographics, and CIS were performed. Time-dependent ROC analysis at 12 months evaluated discriminatory performance. RESULTS: The groups had similar clinicopathologic characteristics. Random forest variable importance weights were: Mutation Count (100.0), TP53 (38.6), PIK3CA (28.7), TERT (23.2), KDM6A (17.9), FAT1 (17.4), and ERCC2 (15.1). Only TP53 was associated with early failure. Patients were stratified into intermediate/high NGS (n=42) and low NGS (n=22) groups. Those with low NGS demonstrated superior HG recurrence-free survival (HG-RFS) compared to intermediate/high NGS (median not reached, p=0.025). On multivariable Cox regression, low NGS remained protective (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.11–0.96, p=0.04). ROC analysis at 12 months showed that adding genomic variables to AUA risk resulted in a 22% relative improvement in AUC (AUA Risk AUC: 0.545, Combined: 0.666). CONCLUSIONS: This preliminary evaluation of the novel NGS, derived from the clinically implemented MSK-IMPACT assay, demonstrates independent association with early BCG failure in HG-NMIBC, suggesting utility for risk stratification beyond clinical parameters. Prospective validation in a larger cohort will determine whether this biomarker could identify patients who will benefit from alternative therapies or early cystectomy.

title: SAFETY AND TECHNICAL FEASIBILITY OUTCOMES OF EN BLOC RESECTION OF BLADDER TUMOUR: FIRST ANALYSIS FROM THE GLOBAL ERBT REGISTRY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Vasileios Sakalis, Andrea Gallioli, Xu Chen, Cosmin-Victor Ene, Francesco Soria, Anil Shrestha, Norberto Bernardo, Henry Lazarowicz, Daniel Yong, Marco Moschini, Jorge Cano Velasco, Marek Babjuk, Agus Rizal Hamid, Juan Gomez Rivas, Giorgi Khvadagiani, Francesco Claps, Paolo Gontero, Thomas Herrmann, Rossella Nicoletti, Chi Ho Leung, Chris Ho Ming Wong, Jeremy Yuen-chun Teoh
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To report the safety and technical feasibility outcomes of en bloc resection of bladder tumour (ERBT) utilising data from the Global ERBT Registry. METHODS: The Global ERBT Registry (NCT04934540) is a prospective multinational database contributed by 74 institutes from 27 countries. Baseline patient and disease characteristics were recorded. Peri-operative outcomes including the technical success rate of ERBT, operative time, single-dose intravesical chemotherapy instillation rate, hospital stay, and 30-day complications were recorded. Final pathology results including presence of detrusor muscle and resection margin status were recorded. RESULTS: A total of 2630 patients were included in this analysis. The median age was 69 years. The median tumour size was 1.7 cm and the median number of tumour was 1. 80% were primary tumours, and 65% had single tumour. The majority of the patients had right lateral wall (31%), left lateral wall (31%) and posterior wall (19%) tumours. The technical success rate of ERBT was 97%, and the median operative time was 30 min. Single-dose intravesical chemotherapy was instilled in 40% of the patients; mitomycin C was the commonest instillation agent (74%). The median hospital stay was 2 days. All-grade 30-day complications occurred in 7.6% patients. Among them, 1.5% were Clavien-Dindo grade 3 or above complications, and the most common were haematuria (0.8%) and bladder perforation (0.4%). 91% of the patients had urothelial carcinoma, and among them, 96% were non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). Among those with NMIBC, clear resection margin was achieved in 85% of them. The detrusor muscle sampling rate was 77%. CONCLUSIONS: The Global ERBT registry demonstrated that ERBT was safe, technically feasible and highly generalisable in the real-world setting. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: AI-INFORMED QUANTITATIVE MITOSIS INDEX PREDICTS BCG MAINTENANCE THERAPY BENEFIT IN HIGH-RISK NON–MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Naoto Tokuyama, Sebastian Medina, Sahar A. Nasser, Kamal Hammouda, Tilak Pathak, Xavier Farré, Tuomas Mirtti, Holly Harper, Gregory T. Mac Lennan, Shreyas S. Joshi, Vikram M. Narayan, Viraj M. Master, Anant M. Madabhushi
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) maintenance therapy is a standard of care for high-risk non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer (HR-NMIBC), yet patient benefit varies widely. A practical biomarker identifying patients most likely to benefit could optimize treatment selection. This study evaluated whether AI-informed quantitative mitosis Index, a key histologic indicator of tumor proliferation, predicts BCG maintenance therapy benefit from routine H&E images. METHODS: Transurethral resection specimens from 341 BCG-naïve NMIBC cases were collected from two independent institutions (University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center \[UHCMC\], n=185; Emory University \[EU\], n=156). Mitotic figures were automatically detected using a YOLO-based deep learning model trained on multi-institutional, multi-cancer datasets. The upper tertile of mitotic activity in the UHCMC cohort was used to define the high-risk group, and the same threshold was applied to the EU cohort. All patients in the EU cohort received BCG induction therapy, and the additive benefit of BCG maintenance was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models with interaction terms. The primary endpoint was 24-month high-grade recurrence-free survival (hgRFS). RESULTS: The validation cohort included only HR-NMIBC patients. Of 156 validation cases, 108 (69%) received BCG maintenance, and 22.4% experienced high-grade recurrence (hgR) within 2 years (median hgRFS: 7.7 months). In a multivariable Cox analysis, a significant interaction was observed between mitotic risk classification and maintenance therapy (interaction p=0.039). Stratification by mitotic activity revealed differential BCG maintenance therapy benefits, with mitosis-low patients showing modest but not statistically significant risk reduction (HR=0.54, 95% CI 0.25-1.16, p=0.115), while mitosis-high patients experienced substantial benefit (HR=0.115, 95% CI 0.03-0.41, p=0.0009). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative mitotic assessment on routine H&E slides could serve as an objective biomarker to stratify patients and identify those who benefit from BCG maintenance therapy over induction in high-risk NMIBC, warranting further validation in larger, independent cohorts, particularly in the era of current BCG shortage.

title: REDUCED VERSUS FULL DOSE BCG MAINTENANCE IN NMIBC PATIENTS TREATED WITH FULL DOSE INDUCTION: A MATCHED ANALYSIS
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Michael A. O'Donnell, Yair Lotan, Katherine Lajkosz, Jethro C. C. Kwong, Sarah Attia, Willian Ito, Ian M. Mcelree, Avesh Chadee, Girish S. Kulkarni, Alexandre R. Zlotta
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Due to the ongoing shortage of bacillus Calmette- Guérin (BCG) and considering its immunological mechanism, a reduced BCG dose during maintenance—while administering a full dose at induction—has been proposed for managing non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 989 patients from four academic institutions between 2004 and 2023. Among these, 625 patients received full dose BCG during both induction and maintenance, whereas 364 received a full induction dose followed by a reduced maintenance dose (one-third or less). The primary outcome was time to progression (muscle-invasive, nodal, or metastatic disease). Secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), and recurrence-free survival (RFS). Survival probabilities were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Differences based on treatment were analyzed using propensity score matching (PSM) with logistic regression and 1:1 matching with replacement. Cox regression models evaluated covariates' association with outcomes. RESULTS: After matching, 606 intermediate and high-risk NMIBC patients were included: 303 in the full-dose group and 303 in the reduced-dose group. The median (IQR) age was 70. 7 (63.3-77.1) years; 77% were male, 38% had T1HG NMIBC, and 79% had high-grade disease. Baseline clinical and pathological features were similar between groups. The median (IQR) follow-up was 5.9 (3. 2-10. 0) years for the full dose maintenance group and 5.6 (3.0-8.2) years for the reduced dose group. The estimated five-year cumulative incidence of tumor progression was 14% (95% CI 10%-19%) for the full dose group versus 10% (95% CI 7%-14%) for the reduced dose group (p=0.144). Multivariable Cox regression, adjusting for age, sex, treatment year, and carcinoma in situ, showed no significant difference in the primary outcome between the full and reduced BCG maintenance doses (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.44-1.11; P=0.13). No significant differences were found for CSS and OS; however, RFS was improved with the reduced dose (hazard ratio, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.43-0.67; p<0. 001). CONCLUSIONS: This cohort-matched study found no difference in progression, CSS, or OS between reduced and full BCG doses for maintenance in NMIBC patients who completed full BCG induction. These results support the need for a randomized clinical trial comparing full versus reduced maintenance BCG in patients after full BCG induction, especially given the shortage of BCG.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A MACHINE LEARNING-DRIVEN, NANOSCALE IMAGING PLATFORM FOR NON-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER DIAGNOSIS IN A PROSPECTIVE, CROSS-SECTIONAL, CASE-CONTROLLED STUDY
session: Bladder Cancer: Non-invasive I (IP02)
authors: Amir Monemian, Jean Pham, Son Pham, Zhiying Xie, Nadia Makarova, Louis Liou, Emily Y. Huang, Nnamdi Onochie, Matthew Mossanen
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Bladder cancer (BC) has a high recurrence rate, driving frequent surveillance cystoscopies with increasing cost, discomfort, and procedural risk. A reliable noninvasive rule-out test could reduce negative cystoscopy. We assessed whether a clinic-to-central-lab nanoscale urine imaging pipeline ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191276.85430.b0.30#F1)) can run reproducibly in routine practice, and we defined operational metrics, specimen adequacy criteria, and technical issues to guide multicenter validation. METHODS: In a prospective, cross-sectional, case-controlled study, we enrolled 95 surveillance patients with prior BC; 38 had recurrence confirmed by histology, 54 had no recurrence confirmed by negative cystoscopy, and 3 lacked a final diagnosis. Urothelial cell surfaces were scanned with a nanoscale cantilever to quantify biophysical properties (e. g., adhesion). Surface features underwent a standardized data cleaning pipeline. A finalized gradient-boosting model produced a binary patient-level output (“cancer signature detected” vs “not detected”) with thresholds prespecified for a highly sensitive use case. Performance was compared against cystoscopy/histology. RESULTS: Clinic collection with same-day courier to a central Cellens laboratory yielded an end-to-end turnaround of 2–3 days for evaluable specimens. Of 95 enrolled, 76 patients (80%) were evaluable (27 recurrence, 49 non-recurrence); 19 were non-evaluable due to inadequate urothelial cellularity (n=8), insufficient medical records (n=5), or covered with other particles (n=6). Preliminary patient-level performance on the 76-patient analysis set showed an AUC of 88.1 (95% CI: 79.1-97.0). All of the 27 positive recurrence on both low grade and high-grade patients were detected, which means that patients with negative results can be safely managed without cystoscopy. CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrated that a nanoscale urothelial cell imaging method using Atomic Force Microscopy with Machine Learning is operationally feasible with a predictable 2–3 day turnaround and 80% evaluability in routine urology practice. As samples can be collected from home, this test potentially offers patients a surveillance option outside of the clinic. By identifying those who truly need cystoscopy, this test will help provide greater access to care to patients and improve their quality of lives.

title: INCIDENTAL PROSTATE CANCER DETECTION FOLLOWING ROBOT-ASSISTED SIMPLE PROSTATECTOMY VERSUS HOLMIUM LASER ENUCLEATION OF THE PROSTATE IN MEN WITH LARGE BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA: RESULTS FROM A HIGH-VOLUME EUROPEAN REFERRAL CENTRE
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Attilio Barretta, Angelo Mottaran, Sara Tamburini, Pietro Piazza, Edoardo Beatrici, Nicolas Carl, Francesco Prata, Mario De Angelis, Natali Rodriguez Penaranda, Francesco Pepillo, Alessio Guidotti, Vincenzo Cavarra, Claudio Brancelli, Rocco Papalia, Edward Lambert, Ruben De Groote, Geert De Naeyer, D'Hondt Frederiek, Riccardo Schiavina, Alexandre Mottrie
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Robot-assisted simple prostatectomy (RASP) and holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) are established surgical options for men with large-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). An often underestimated endpoint in this setting is the detection of incidental prostate cancer (iPCa), which may be influenced by differences in specimen retrieval and pathological assessment. METHODS: We analysed data of 468 patients with symptomatic BPH due to large (>100 ml) prostate glands who underwent RASP (n=206, 44%) and HoLEP (n=262, 56%) at tertiary referral centre. Preoperative characteristics included age, body mass index (BMI), prostate volume, prostate-specific antigen (PSA), and PSA density (PSAD). Patients with elevated PSA or abnormal digital rectal examination underwent preoperative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging and targeted and/or systematic biopsy to exclude clinically significant prostate cancer prior to surgery. Postoperative parameters included PSA, specimen weight, and pathological evaluation. The primary endpoint was the rate of incidental prostate cancer (iPCa) on final pathology. RESULTS: Median age and BMI were comparable between the two groups (all p>0.5), as shown in Table 1. Median prostate volume was larger in RASP (180 ml, IQR 130–220) compared with HoLEP (120 ml, IQR 110–140; p0.001). Median preoperative PSA was 6.9 ng/mL (IQR 4.8–9.2) in RASP and 6.8 ng/mL (IQR 4.7–9.0) in HoLEP (p=0.7), resulting in lower PSAD for RASP (0.038 ng/mL2, IQR 0.028–0.052) compared with HoLEP (0.057 ng/mL2, IQR 0.041–0.071; p0.001). Median postoperative PSA was 1.35 ng/mL (IQR 0.9–1.9) in RASP and 1.28 ng/mL (IQR 0.8–1.7) in HoLEP (p=0.4). Median specimen weight was 115 g (IQR 90–145) for RASP and 105 g (IQR 85–130) for HoLEP (p=0.6). iPCa was identified in 9.0% of RASP and 3.4% of HoLEP specimens (p=0.018). All tumours were ISUP Grade Group 1. CONCLUSIONS: RASP was associated with a significantly higher rate of iPCa detection compared with HoLEP, despite comparable baseline characteristics, lower PSAD, and similar specimen weight. This difference likely reflects intact specimen retrieval in RASP, providing a potential diagnostic advantage in men with large BPH. | | | --- | | |

title: QUALITY OF LIFE AND EARLY OUTCOMES FOLLOWING EXTERNAL BEAM RADIOTHERAPY AFTER HOLMIUM LASER ENUCLEATION (HOLEP): A PROPENSITY-MATCHED COHORT STUDY
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Zachary Muench, Emily Serrell, Madison T. Taychert, Margaret Knoedler, Glenn Allen, Daniel Gralnek, Christopher Manakas, Ali Antar, Matthew D. Grimes
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Prostate cancer is incidentally identified (IPCA) in 5–12% of men after holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia. The optimal management of these patients remains uncertain. While most are monitored with active surveillance, those with higher-grade disease or evidence of progression may require definitive treatment with external beam radiotherapy (EBRT). Limited data describe the safety, toxicity, and urinary quality-of-life outcomes of EBRT delivered after HoLEP. Therefore, we aim to directly compare patient reported urinary quality of life (QOL), surgical complications, and functional outcomes in patients receiving EBRT after HoLEP compared with propensity score matched non-EBRT HoLEP patients. METHODS: We included men who underwent HoLEP between 2020-2024 with IPCA. Radiation oncology databases were used to identify patients who received EBRT after HoLEP. Propensity score based on age and grade group was used to generate a matched cohort of patients who did not receive EBRT. Comprehensive clinical data were collected and groups compared with respect to preoperative characteristics, perioperative complications, radiation toxicity, and International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) responses. RESULTS: There were 38 patients in the EBRT group and 98 in the non-EBRT group. Patients receiving EBRT had higher preoperative PSA (27.6 vs 7.3 ng/mL, p=0.04), lower IPSS QOL (3.63 vs 4.44, p=0.03), and were more likely to have an indwelling catheter (37.0% vs 5.1%, p<0.001) compared to non-EBRT patients ( Table). Average postoperative IPSS QOL (2.34 vs 2.37, p=0.92) and total IPSS (6.92 vs 8.16, p=0.36) scores were similar between groups at a median follow-up of 27 months. In the EBRT group, mean IPSS QOL improved from 3.63 pre-HoLEP to 2.34 post-HoLEP and remained stable post-EBRT (2.20). RTOG acute GU toxicity was mild to moderate in most EBRT patients (grade 0–2 in 97.2%), with a single grade 3 event and no grade 4 toxicity. Perioperative surgical complications and patient reported pad use for incontinence were similar in the EBRT and non-EBRT cohorts ( Table). CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving EBRT after HoLEP experienced low rates of high-grade toxicity and sustained urinary QOL improvement comparable to HoLEP-only patients. Further study is warranted to define optimal timing, fractionation, and long-term outcomes of post-HoLEP radiotherapy. | | | --- | | |

title: COMPARING SHORT TERM PERIOPERATIVE OUTCOMES FOR TRANSURETHRAL RESECTION OF THE PROSTATE, PHOTOSELECTIVE VAPORIZATION, AND HOLMIUM LASER ENUCLEATION TREATMENTS OF BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Jonathan Huynh, Michael Gallagher, Nir Tomer, Ignacio Gondolesi, Michael Palese
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To compare 30-day perioperative outcomes among patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP), photoselective vaporization (PVP), or holmium laser enucleation (HoLEP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). METHODS: ACS-NSQIP data from 2015–2020 were reviewed to identify patients who underwent TURP, PVP, or HoLEP. The primary outcome was a composite “suboptimal” 30-day outcome (any major complication or reoperation); the secondary outcome was 30-day hospital readmission. Multivariable logistic regression compared outcomes by procedure type, adjusting for age group (<65, 65–74, ≥75 years), race, ASA class, case urgency, inpatient status, and comorbidities available in the ACS-NSQIP database. Interaction terms assessed whether procedure effects differed by age group. RESULTS: We identified 63,643 patients (mean age 70; 67.8% TURP, 25.8% PVP, 6.4% HoLEP). Overall, 11.7% experienced a 30-day suboptimal outcome and 16% were readmitted within 30 days. On adjusted analysis, HoLEP was associated with significantly lower odds of a suboptimal outcome compared to TURP (odds ratio ~0.7–0.8 in patients ≥65, p<0.01), indicating ~20–30% fewer complications, whereas PVP had no significant difference versus TURP. This improvement became more significant for older age groups. PVP was associated with higher odds of 30-day readmission versus TURP (OR ~1.2, p<0.001), while HoLEP’s readmission risk was similar to TURP. As expected, higher-risk clinical factors (urgent case, inpatient admission, elevated ASA, serious comorbidities) were independently associated with increased complications (all p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this national cohort, HoLEP demonstrated the lowest perioperative morbidity among BPH surgeries, especially in older patients, without increasing readmissions. PVP and TURP had comparable complication profiles, but PVP patients were more likely to be readmitted. These data support the safety and favorable outcomes of HoLEP for BPH and may guide patient counseling and surgical selection, while highlighting the need to reduce readmissions after PVP.

title: RISK OF CLIMACTURIA AFTER LASER ENUCLEATION OF THE PROSTATE FOR BENIGN PROSTATIC OBSTRUCTION
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Ilaria E. Zais, Nicolò Schifano, Sara Baldini, Matteo Coschignano, Alessio Villano, Matteo Broggini, Giuseppe Gianesini, Paolo Capogrosso, Federico Dehò
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Anatomical endoscopic laser enucleation of the prostate (AEEP) is considered a first-line surgical treatment for benign prostatic obstruction (BPO) and is associated with a high rate of retrograde ejaculation, with possible negative impact on orgasmic function and transitory urinary incontinence (UI). Climacturia is defined as orgasm-associated UI, extensively reported after radical prostatectomy in association with UI. We aimed to investigate the prevalence and risk of climacturia in patients treated with AEEP for BPO. METHODS: We analyzed data recorded prospectively from 202 consecutive patients treated at a single center with holmium or thulium laser AEEP for BPO. Preoperative and perioperative clinical and functional data, including International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and Sexual Encounter Profile (SEP) 2-3 questionnaire were collected. All patients were reassessed at regular follow-up visits after surgery. The prevalence of postoperative climacturia was assessed with a dedicated questionnaire. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate the risk of UI. A landmark analysis was used to assess preoperative predictors of climacturia within 3 months after surgery. RESULTS: Overall, 75 (37%) and 127 (63%) patients were treated with HoLEP and ThuLEP, respectively. Median (IQR) age was 71 (65, 75) years with a body mass index of 22.4 (20.6, 25.8). Patients had a high median prostate volume \[94 (65, 113) ml\] with a median PSA of 3.3 (1.4, 6.9) ng/mL and an IPSS of 20 (11, 25). A total of 118 (58%) patients were sexually active with normal erection according to SEP 2-3 questions. At 3 months after surgery, estimated urinary continence recovery was 93% (95% CI: 80%, 99%). Climacturia was reported by 16% (N=33) of cases, with 46% (N=92) of patients reporting being sexually active after surgery. At logistic regression analysis, prostate volume (PV) emerged as the only preoperative predictor of climacturia (OR: 1.01; 95% CI: 1.00, 1.02; p=0.01). The adjusted risk of climacturia for a patient with a PV of 40 cc was 9% (95% CI: 2–15%) compared to 22% (95% CI: 14– 30%) for one with a PV of 100 cc ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191280.81177.3f.04#F1)). Of note, all patients recovered from climacturia at 12 months post-treatment. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study reporting the risk of climacturia after AEEP. Patients should be counseled regarding the risk of transient climacturia after surgery, which appears higher for patients with larger prostate volumes.

title: PROSTATIC URETHRAL LIFT IN YOUNG MEN SEEKING EJACULATORY AND FERTILITY PRESERVATION: SEMEN PARAMETERS UP TO 18 MONTHS FOLLOW-UP
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Nicola D'Altilia, Lorenzo Mazzotta, Edoardo Tocci, Gian Maria Busetto, Bettocchi Carlo, Secco Silvia, Giuseppe Carrieri, Pasquale Annese
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive surgical therapies (MIST) aim to relieve LUTS due to BPH while preserving sexual and ejaculatory function. We prospectively assessed semen parameters up to 18 months after prostatic urethral lift (PUL/UroLift) in men under 50 prioritizing fertility and contextualized these findings against other MIST. METHODS: In this single-center cohort (n=20), semen analyses (WHO 6th edition) were performed at baseline, 6, and 18 months after UroLift. Functional outcomes were prospectively collected through uroflowmetry with post-void residual (PVR) measurement, and subjective outcomes through the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) questionnaire. Ethical Committee at the University Hospital ‘Ospedali Riuniti’, Foggia, Italy—Protocol 155/CE/2017 authorization number 618 of 18 December 2017. RESULTS: Semen parameters remained stable (median total sperm count 29.5→31.0→30.5 million/mL; p=0.88). Ejaculate volume and pH were unchanged. Motility, vitality, and morphology remained within reference thresholds. LUTS improved durably (Qmax +67%, PVR −50%, IPSS −60%). Complications occurred in 15% (1 had prostatitis treated with antibiotic therapy, 1 patient required a bladder catheter for 7 days due to acute urinary retention), re‑treatment in 10% (1 for LUTS e 1 for calcification of device). This series provides the first evidence in the literature of paternity achieved after PUL, observed in two patients. Baseline, peri-operative, and safety data are summarized in Table 1. Semen parameters at baseline, 6, and 18 months are reported in Table 2. Functional outcomes are presented in Table 3. Ejaculation preservation and semen-analysis evidence across contemporary MIST are outlined in Table 4. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected young men, PUL preserved semen quality and ejaculation through 18 months while providing durable symptom relief. Ejaculation‑sparing MIST should be central to counseling of fertility‑conscious patients.

title: SEXUAL FUNCTION OUTCOMES OF THE 5-YEAR TREATMENT WITH REZUM COMPARED TO DOXAZOSIN, FINASTERIDE AND COMBINATION DRUG THERAPY FOR MEN WITH BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA: COHORT DATA FROM THE MEDICAL THERAPY OF PROSTATIC SYMPTOMS (MTOPS) TRIAL
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Timothy M. Han, Bronwyn Long, Amandip Cheema, Cara Joyce, Marina Feffer, Nicholas Gonzalez, Kevin T. Mcvary
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Alpha blockers and 5-ARIs are a mainstay of LUTS/BPH treatment; however, there can be associated sexual function deterioration with these agents. Water vapor thermal therapy (WVTT, Rezum), a minimally invasive procedure for LUTS/BPH, serves as an efficacious treatment while preserving sexual function. We compared sexual function over 5 years after continuous daily treatment with pharmaceutical agents in the NIH-Medical Therapy of Prostatic Symptoms (MTOPS) study versus a single WVTT procedure (Rezum RCT) in subjects with matched criteria for LUTS severity and prostate size. METHODS: We used baseline sexual function data from cohorts of the MTOPS study (n=1157) randomized to doxazosin, finasteride, combination therapy, and placebo, and sexually active men at baseline (n=86) who received WVTT. MTOPS participants completed the Brief Male Sexual Function Inventory, while Rezum RCT participants completed the IIEF-15 and Male Sexual Health Questionnaire. Average percentage changes from baseline were compared using a linear mixed repeated measures model with fixed effects for treatment and follow-up visits ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191280.81177.3f.06#F1)). RESULTS: Men experienced significant worsening of sexual desire, erectile and ejaculatory function, and overall sexual satisfaction with finasteride and combination drug therapy. Men on doxazosin similarly had a significant decline in sexual desire, erectile and ejaculatory function, but overall sexual satisfaction was preserved. WVTT patients experienced a significant increase in sexual desire and erectile function at 1-year follow-up and a significant increase in overall sexual satisfaction over 5 years. There was a significant decrease in ejaculatory function of approximately -10% (vs. -20% combination therapy) from baseline levels from 3-5 years of follow-up with WVTT. CONCLUSIONS: WVTT may offer more favorable outcomes for sexual function compared to pharmacologic treatments, which are consistently associated with declines across multiple domains.

title: COMPARATIVE RISK OF ERECTILE AND EJACULATORY DYSFUNCTION FOLLOWING UROLIFT VS. OPTILUME IN MEN UNDERGOING MINIMALLY INVASIVE BPH THERAPY: A PROPENSITY-MATCHED COHORT STUDY OF 12-MONTH OUTCOMES
session: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Surgical Therapy & New Technology I (IP03)
authors: Muhammed A. Moukhtar Hammad, Bradley Roth, Elia Abou Chawareb, Eliad Amini, Mohammed Mahdi, Akhil Das, Faysal A. Yafi
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive surgical therapies (MISTs) have become increasingly popular for management of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Two popular therapies include Optilume, a urethral dilation balloon coated with paclitaxel, and UroLift, an implant that mechanically widens the lumen of the prostatic urethra. However, data on sexual side effects and outcomes of these treatments is scarce. This study aimed to compare the 12-month outcomes of erectile dysfunction (ED) and ejaculatory dysfunction (EJD) following these procedures. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX research network. Men with BPH undergoing UroLift or Optilume were identified, while those with prior ED or EJD were excluded using CPT and ICD codes. The UroLift and Optilume cohorts included 8630 and 1214 patients, respectively. Propensity score matching based on age, race, BMI, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, testicular hypofunction yielded 1169 matched patients per group.
