We aimed to provide a more robust analysis of functional recovery after prolonged warm ischemia (WI), including quantification of short- and long-term effects. METHODS: 568 PN patients at our center (2011-2020) with prolonged ischemia (>30minutes) with necessary data were evaluated. Recovery from ischemia (Recischemia) was defined as ipsilateral GFR preserved normalized by parenchymal volume preserved, and would be 100% if all nephrons recovered completely from ischemia. The impact of prolonged ischemia on Recischemia, spectrum-score (analogous to AKI), and percent annual decline of ipsilateral GFR and parenchymal volume were assessed. RESULTS: Median tumor size and R. E. N. A. L were 4.3 cm and 8, respectively. The prolonged ischemia cohorts included patients managed with hypothermia (n=268) and WI (n=300). Median ischemia times for the hypothermia and WI cohorts were 42 and 35 minutes, respectively. Median Recischemia for cold versus WI was 96% and 85%, respectively (Table 1, (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.07#F1), p<0.01). Recischemia fell ≈9% for each additional 10 min of prolonged WI beyond 30 minutes. Increased spectrum score was seen with prolonged ischemia, whether cold or warm. GFR at 3 years was generally stable at 95% and 97% preserved, respectively, in both the cold and warm cohorts, and substantial atrophy was not seen ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.07#F1)). On multivariable analysis, prolonged WI and increased spectrum score were associated with reduced Recischemia (both p<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Our results confirm the significant negative impact of prolonged warm ischemia on functional recovery during clamped PN, and hypothermia proved to be protective. Early ipsilateral renal dysfunction was mostly dependent on ischemia time, whether cold or warm. Long-term function and parenchymal volume generally remained stable despite exposure to prolonged ischemia. Prolonged warm ischemia should be avoided in patients with solitary kidneys and/or moderate-severe preexisting CKD. NA.

title: IMPACT OF PROLONGED WARM ISCHEMIA DURING CLAMPED PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY: COMPARISON BETWEEN JAPANESE AND AMERICAN COHORTS
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Takashi Ikeda, Kieran Lewis, Akira Kazama, Carlos Munoz-Lopez, Jayant Siva, Eran Maina, Angelica Bartholomew, Anne Wong, Steven C. Campbell, Toshio Takagi
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Introduction: Recent research suggests that functional recovery begins to decline after ≈30 minutes of warm-ischemia-time (WIT) following clamped partial-nephrectomy (PN). However, the extent of this decline and populations at risk remain unclear. Our objective was to identify factors associated with functional decline following prolonged WIT in Japanese and American patients. METHODS: Methods: A multi-institutional retrospective-review of PN patients managed with prolonged WIT(>30minutes) at Tokyo Women’s and Cleveland Clinic(2010-2024). Inclusion required pre and post-operative serum-creatinine and cross-sectional imaging. Ipsilateral split-renal- function(SRF) was assessed using parenchymal-volume-analysis(PVA). Recovery from ischemia(RecIschemia) was defined: ipsilateral GFR preserved normalized by percent- parenchymal-volume-preserved(PPVP). Multivariable analysis identified factors associated with RecIschemia, PPVP, and %global GFR preservation. RESULTS: Results: 300 U. S./171 Japanese patients met inclusion criteria. U. S. patients had increased comorbidities, including obesity, hypertension, and cardiovascular-disease. A significant and similar decline in global GFR for every additional 10 minutes of WIT was seen in both the Japanese and U. S. patients (3.1% vs. 4.0%, respectively, p=0.41). Independent predictors of decline in global GFR were PPVP in both cohorts and longer WIT only for U. S. patients. R. E. N. A. L. and tumor-size were primary drivers of decline in PPVP, and WIT and HTN were drivers of decline in RecIschemia, but only in U. S. patients. CONCLUSIONS: Conclusion: Japanese and U. S. patients undergoing PN with prolonged WIT experienced similar decline in global GFR, albeit driven by different factors potentially reflecting differences in patient populations and/or surgical technique. Our data suggest that avoiding prolonged WIT may be important in patients with solitary kidneys and/or severe CKD, although further studies will be needed.

title: 3D PERFUSION ZONE MODELS ALLOW FOR MORE ACCURATE AND MORE FREQUENT SELECTIVE ARTERIAL CLAMPING DURING ROBOT-ASSISTED PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY: INTERIM RESULTS OF THE MULTICENTRIC RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED PODRACING TRIAL
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Joris Vangeneugden, Saar Vermijs, Pieter De Backer, Peter De Kuyper, Camille Berquin, Nicolaas Lumen, Frederic Baekelandt, Christophe Ghysel, Yannic Raskin, Bernard Bynens, Kenzo Mestdagh, Pieter De Visschere, Charlotte Debbaut, Karel Decaestecker, Charles Van Praet
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Although the superiority of selective clamping (SC) over main-artery clamping (MAC) in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) remains controversial, SC may offer benefits in certain cases. Improved prediction of kidney perfusion could enhance the precision of SC and thereby promote better preservation of healthy renal tissue. PODRACING (Planning Operative strategy using a Digital Renal Artery ClampING tool) is a multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating the benefits of 3D perfusion zone (3DPZ) models in RAPN. The trial is registered on ClinicalTrials. gov (NCT06536439) and was approved by the Belgian Federal Agency for Medicines and Health Products (CIV-23-11-044854). Herein, we present our pre-planned interim analysis of the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoint regarding clamping strategy. METHODS: Patients undergoing RAPN were randomized 1:1 to either an experimental group (CT scan \+ 3DPZ) or control group (CT scan only), stratified by PADUA complexity score, hospital, and whether SC was deemed feasible or not. The primary endpoint, performing as planned a SC strategy, was analyzed in a subgroup of patients where SC was deemed feasible. The key secondary endpoint, clamping strategy performed (SC vs MAC), was studied in the total population. Both endpoints were analyzed using a Chi-Squared (X2) test. RESULTS: In total, 107 patients underwent RAPN in 4 participating Belgian centers from July 2024 until October 2025. 27/107 cases were classified as PADUA high-risk (≥10), all other cases were PADUA 9 or lower. In 103/107 cases, SC was deemed feasible. SC was planned in 87/107 cases and performed in 73/107 cases. In 65/73 cases, SC was performed as planned. The use of a 3DPZ model was significantly associated with performing more accurate (p<0.00001) ( Table 1) and more frequent (p=0.000076) SC. CONCLUSIONS: PODRACING is the first RCT exploring the benefits of 3DPZ models in RAPN. The interim analysis of our ongoing trial shows that the use of 3DPZ models is strongly correlated with performing more accurate and more frequent SC during RAPN, and thus preserving healthier kidney tissue by less extensive ischemia. More secondary and exploratory endpoints –including renal function, surgical time and quality of life– are currently being studied. | | | --- | | |

title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL IMAGING FOR PERIOPERATIVE PLANNING IN PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY: A META-ANALYSIS OF 3,485 PATIENTS
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Luis A. Esparza-Miranda, Alejandro Calvillo-Ramirez, Andrea C. Beltran-De La Fuente, Ana Paulina Casas-Huesca, Archan Khandekar, Cheryl T. Lee
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Partial nephrectomy (PN) remains the gold standard for localized renal masses. Optimal outcomes depend on meticulous preoperative planning and precise intraoperative navigation, which traditionally rely on two-dimensional (2D) imaging that may not fully capture renal anatomy or spatial relationships. Three-dimensional (3D) visualization modalities, including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and 3D-printed models, offer enhanced anatomical understanding and more accurate surgical planning. This meta-analysis evaluated the impact of 3D imaging on perioperative, oncological, and functional outcomes in patients undergoing PN. METHODS: A systematic search of four databases was conducted through July 2025. Eligible studies compared 3D visualization with standard 2D imaging in adults with renal masses undergoing PN. Outcomes included warm ischemia time (WIT), operative time (OT), estimated blood loss (EBL), positive surgical margins (PSM), major complications (Clavien–Dindo≥III), postoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), length of stay (LOS), and intraoperative complications. Data were pooled using mean differences (MD) or odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Subgroup analyses were performed by surgical approach. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (2 RCTs, 6 prospective, 15 retrospective) with 3,485 patients met inclusion criteria. Baseline characteristics were comparable, 3D imaging significantly reduced PSM rates (OR=0.56, p=0.001), decreased EBL (MD=–25.07 ml, p=0.01), lowered major complication rates (OR=0.60, p=0.02), improved postoperative eGFR (MD=2.0, p=0.02), and shortened hospital stay (MD=–0.64 days, p=0.03). Subgroup analyses revealed consistent trends favoring 3D visualization across surgical approaches. The laparoscopic subgroup showed the greatest benefit, with significant reductions in EBL, WIT, OT and PSM, while in robotic procedures, 3D visualization significantly improved postoperative eGFR. CONCLUSIONS: The use of 3D imaging was associated with improved surgical and functional outcomes, including positive surgical margins, fewer postoperative complications, reduced blood loss, shorter hospital stay, and better renal function preservation. Future randomized studies are warranted to assess cost-effectiveness and long-term functional outcomes.

title: SEEING IS DECIDING: VIRTUAL 3D MODELS IMPROVE DECISIONAL QUALITY IN RENAL MASS COUNSELING
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Stacy E. Piva, Asha Ayub, Lorna Kwan, Joseph D. Shirk
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Treatment decisions for small renal masses (SRMs) remain variable despite comparable oncologic outcomes across options, suggesting that patient comprehension during counseling influences treatment selection. Virtual 3D models provide an interactive visual aid to improve understanding of anatomy and treatment trade-offs. We evaluated whether incorporating patient-specific 3D kidney models during consultation improves decisional quality compared to a historical control cohort. METHODS: We conducted a prospective pilot study of 20 patients counseled for SRMs using interactive virtual 3D models generated from CT/MRI via a cloud-based segmentation platform, compared with a historical control cohort (n=73) from Shirk et al., 2018. After consultation, patients completed validated surveys: Decisional Conflict Scale (DCS; total and subscales), kidney cancer knowledge assessment (9-item), and Service Satisfaction Scale for Cancer Care (SSS-CC). Surveys were administered immediately post-consultation. Group comparisons used Wilcoxon rank-sum and chi-square tests. RESULTS: Among 93 patients (20 3D vs 73 controls), groups were similar in age, sex, and race. Patients counseled with 3D models had lower decisional conflict on the Informed subscale (median 0.0 \[IQR 0–8.3\] vs 16.7 \[0–33.3\]; p=0.014). No differences were seen in total DCS, other subscales, or satisfaction. High knowledge scores were more common in the 3D group (80% vs 63%; p=0.15). Post-consultation treatment choice differed: patients receiving 3D models more often selected active surveillance (40% vs 11%; p=0.005) ( Table 1). CONCLUSIONS: Virtual 3D models reduced decisional conflict in the informed subscale and influenced treatment choice toward active surveillance, even when measured immediately post-consult. These findings suggest that visualizing tumor anatomy enhances comprehension and promotes preference-concordant decision-making. Continued accrual will refine these estimates and assess durability of effects across a larger cohort.

title: APPLICATION OF REAL-TIME DIGITAL TWIN NAVIGATION AND WARNING SYSTEM BASED ON DEEP LEARNING AND AUGMENTED REALITY TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM (AI+AR) IN ROBOT-ASSISTED AND LAPAROSCOPIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY (NCT07020169)
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Shaobo Zhang, Chenkui Miao, Pengfei Shao, Jie Li
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive (robot-assisted and laparoscopic) partial nephrectomy is the mainstream surgical approach for treating T1a and some T1b stage renal tumors. Urologists aim for tumor control, low complication rates, and renal function preservation in this procedure. Complete tumor resection at an appropriate distance from the tumor capsule ensures tumor control and renal function preservation. Identifying important vessels (arteries, veins, and collecting system) during resection is crucial for reducing intraoperative and postoperative complications. Additionally, for endophytic tumors, their hidden location makes intraoperative identification difficult. This project aims to use artificial intelligence (AI) deep learning to construct a three-dimensional vascular model of the kidney and, through augmented reality (AR) technology, establish a real-time, field-of-view-following digital twin navigation and warning system in minimally invasive partial nephrectomy to plan the resection range in real time and warn of potential damage to important vessels. METHODS: The clinical trial registration number of this project is NCT07020169. Patients with T1a and some T1b stage single renal tumors (with normal contralateral renal function) scheduled for minimally invasive partial nephrectomy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from March 2024 to the present were included. Patients with anatomically or functionally solitary kidneys and angiomyolipomas were excluded. All patients underwent 64-slice enhanced CT (pixel size 0.47-0.74 mm/pixel, slice thickness 0.5 mm) before surgery. CT DICOM data were imported into a self-developed AI convolutional neural network segmentation algorithm (Meta Grayscale Adaptive, MGA) to automatically segment and construct a three-dimensional model including the kidney, tumor, and vessels (arteries, veins, renal pelvis and calyces). Real-time digital twins were constructed using vector point marking and real-time camera pose transformation algorithms and superimposed onto the robot-assisted or laparoscopic surgical field for navigation and warning. Three experienced urologic surgeons performed minimally invasive partial nephrectomy using the real-time digital twin navigation and warning system. Patient and tumor basic information, perioperative data were recorded, and the intraoperative digital twin matching degree was evaluated using the Dice score, and the doctor's acceptance was evaluated using the Likert scale. RESULTS: All 112 patients (67 robot-assisted and 45 laparoscopic) successfully completed the surgery without conversion to open or radical resection. The average tumor diameter was 3.1 cm, with a median RENAL score of 7 points, including 14 cases of completely endophytic tumors. The average operation time was 98 minutes, and the average warm ischemia time was 22 minutes. After analyzing 11,200 frames of images, the average Dice score for the kidney contour was 0.86, and for the tumor was 0.82. The average Likert score for robot-assisted surgery was 8.6 points, and for laparoscopic surgery was 8.1 points. Only one patient had postoperative bleeding requiring interventional treatment. CONCLUSIONS: The digital twin navigation and warning system based on AI+AR is safe and reliable in minimally invasive partial nephrectomy. This system has high matching accuracy and robustness, which helps in tumor boundary identification and reduces the risk of surgical complications.

title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL IMAGE-GUIDED ROBOT-ASSISTED PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY FOR TUMORS IN HORSESHOE KIDNEYS: A EUROPEAN MULTICENTRE CASE SERIES (YAU RCC – UROCCR)
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Gaëlle Margue, Federico Rubat Baleuri, Joris Vangeneugden, Jean-Christophe Bernhard, Charles Van Praet, Karel Decaestecker, Antonio Andrea Grosso, Andrea Minervini, Nazareno Suardi, Umberto Carbonara, Pasquale Ditonno, Eduard Roussel, Francesco Porpiglia, Riccardo Campi, Daniele Amparore
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Renal tumors arising in horseshoe kidneys (HSKs) pose major surgical challenges due to complex vascular anatomy, limited mobility, and proximity to critical structures. Three-dimensional (3D) modeling can improve anatomical understanding and support tailored ischemia strategies. This European multicentre study reports outcomes of 3D image-guided robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) for tumors in HSKs. METHODS: Patients with HSK tumors treated with RAPN using patient-specific 3D reconstructions were included. Virtual models from multiphase CT scans detailed renal vasculature, collecting system, and tumor–parenchyma interface. Reconstructions supported preoperative planning and intraoperative cognitive guidance displayed on the robotic console. Clinical, anatomical, perioperative, functional, and oncological outcomes were retrospectively analyzed across European tertiary centres. RESULTS: Twenty-four patients were included (83% male; median age 65 y; tumor size 5.4 cm). Tumor complexity was high (median RENAL 9, PADUA 10), with a median of three renal arteries (range 1–7). A clampless approach was used in 12 (50%), including five with tumor-specific segmental artery ligation. Ten (42%) underwent total and two (8%) selective clamping (median ischemia 23 min). Median operative time was 240 min, blood loss 500 ml. Two (8.3%) had Clavien ≥ III complications; no conversions occurred. Median eGFR variation at last follow-up (21 mo) was –5.0 ml/min/1.73 m2. Two (8.3%) had positive margins, with no recurrences. Trifecta was achieved in 50%. CONCLUSIONS: 3D-assisted RAPN combining preoperative planning and intraoperative guidance enables precise vascular assessment and individualized ischemia management, improving safety in HSK tumor surgery. These findings support integrating 3D reconstruction into the management of complex renal fusion anomalies.

title: SUTURELESS PURELY OFF-CLAMP ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY: EVIDENCE FROM A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED NON-INFERIORITY TRIAL
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Aldo Brassetti, Rocco Simone Flammia, Umberto Anceschi, Eugenio Bologna, Alfredo Maria Bove, Lorenzo Capecchi, Giuseppe Chiacchio, Giuseppe Cosma, Simone D'Annunzio, Mariaconsiglia Ferriero, Salvatore Guaglianone, Sabrina Luculano, Costantino Leonardo, Leslie Claire Licari, Riccardo Mastroianni, Leonardo Misuraca, Flavia Proietti, Giuseppe Simone
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: to describe the novel sutureless (SL) purely off-clamp robotic partial nephrectomy (ocRPN) and compare its results with renorrhaphy (RR). METHODS: a continuous series of patients with cT1-2N0M0 renal tumors, randomly assigned to SL or RR ocRPN, within a single-center, single surgeon randomized controlled trial (GR-2021-12373396). A standard three-arm transperitoneal ocRPN was performed; hemostasis relied on monopolar coagulation of the resection bed. RR was used in controls. Surgical, functional, and oncologic outcomes were collected. Trifecta achievement at discharge tested the non-inferiority hypothesis. Descriptive statistics analyzed the data; recurrence-free survival (RFS) probabilities were compared between groups with the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: among 247 enrolled patients, baseline characteristics were balanced across groups ( Tab. 1). Median operative time was 65 vs 70 minutes in the SL and RR groups (p=0.77). Trifecta was achieved in 93% and 95% of cases, respectively (p=0.43), confirming non-inferiority ( Tab. 2). Blood transfusions (2% vs 0%) and Acute Kidney Injury (2% each) were rare. Nine urinary fistulae occurred overall (3 perioperative, 6 within 90 days), all successfully managed with temporary stenting; rates were higher in the SL group, but not statistically significant. Renal function, assessed by creatinine and scintigraphy, was comparable CONCLUSIONS: SL-ocRPN is safe and effective, representing a feasible alternative to RR-ocRPN in selected cT1-2 renal tumors. Longer follow-up will assess long-term efficacy; further research should clarify which patients benefit more from one technique. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: A SUTURELESS SOLUTION: PROSPECTIVE COMPARATIVE STUDY BETWEEN A NOVEL HAEMOSTATIC PATCH AND RENORRHAPHY IN OFF-CLAMP ROBOT-ASSISTED PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY (RAPN)
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Loris Cacciatore, Antonio Minore, Raso Gianluigi, Contessa Pierangelo, Esperto Francesco, Rocco Papalia, Antonio Rosario Iannello
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Renorrhaphy during off-clamp robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) is technically challenging and may potentially impair renal function in the immediate postoperative period. This study evaluates the use of a novel haemostatic patch as an alternative to conventional renorrhaphy in off clamp RAPN. METHODS: From January 2023 to September 2025, we prospectively collected data on patients who underwent off-clamp RAPN at our institution, dividing them into two groups: those who received a patch (Veriset™ Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) on the tumor bed (PG), and those who underwent conventional single-layer renorrhaphy (RG). We compared the two cohorts based on age, body mass index (BMI), tumor laterality and R. E. N. A. L. nephrometry score (NS). Continuous variables were summarized using mean/SD and median/IQR depending on the normal distribution. Paired eGFR (preoperative, postoperative, and 30-day) was analyzed within groups using paired t-test or Wilcoxon test. Between-group differences in ΔHb, eGFR at different time points, console time, enucleation time, and haemostasis time were assessed using independent-sample t-test or Mann-Whitney test. Correlations between ΔHb and clinical/time variables were calculated within each group (Pearson/Spearman). A significance level was set at p<0.05. RESULTS: Table 1 shows the characteristics of the two groups. 24 patients underwent a sutureless approach while 32 underwent a renorraphy approach. Although the PG and the RG differ in age, BMI and tumor laterality (all p<0.05), the mean NS was not statistically significant (p=0.197). In detail, PG had demonstrated significantly reduced console time (p<0.001) and haemostasis time (p=0.013), compared to RG. Additionally, the PG had a higher postoperative day 1 eGFR compared to the RG (p=0.0031). Enucleation time, postoperative ΔHb, Clavien-Dindo complications, length of stay, renal function at 30 days were similar between the two groups. A single patient in the RG required a blood transfusion, while no readmissions for complications occurred. CONCLUSIONS: According to our first experience the application of a haemostatic patch in off-clamp RAPN provided decreased console and hemostasis times, as well as a quicker recovery of renal function compared to traditional renorrhaphy, demonstrating non-inferiority in terms of efficacy and safety. | | | --- | | |

title: COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF DELAYED BLEEDING (DB) FOLLOWING PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY (PN)
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Eran N. Maina, Kieran Lewis, Jayant Siva, Angelica Bartholomew, Carlos Munoz-Lopez, Akira Kazama, Charles Martin, Steven C. Campbell
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: DB is an uncommon but potentially serious complication of PN, with a reported incidence of 1-2%. Management options include selective arterial angioembolization (SAE), radical nephrectomy (RN), or conservative management (CM). Our objective was to rigorously identify and characterize the presentation, management, and outcomes of DB in a large cohort of PN patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all patients who underwent PN at our institution (2009-2024). Patients with clinical characteristics suggesting hemorrhage and/or post-operative abdominal imaging within 1 month of surgery were screened for possible DB. Patient characteristics and outcomes were collected, and a control group of non-bleed PN patients was included for comparison. RESULTS: 4677 patients underwent PN; 108 (2.3%) experienced DB, and data were also available for 4285 controls (no DB). Median RENAL for patients with DB was only 6 (IQR 5-9)( Table 1). Median time to bleed after PN was 9 days, and the most common presenting symptoms were flank pain (55%) and hematuria (45%). SAE was performed in 64 (59%) patients with a success rate of 92%; 5 (7.8%) required RN. CM was initially pursued in 41 (38%) patients, and 9 (22%) required delayed SAE. Overall, 31 patients (29%) required ICU admission, and the median transfusion requirement was 2 units (IQR 0-3). Three post-DB patients (2.7%) required long-term dialysis. There was no mortality associated with DB. There was no difference in ipsilateral GFR preserved between SAE and CM management ( Table 2), but median global GFR was reduced in DB patients (80%) compared to controls (85%, p=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, DB after PN was more common than previously reported, likely because past studies have generally excluded CM patients. Fifty percent of DB patients had RENAL≤6, suggesting that even less complex PN cases can be at risk. SAE was successful in >90% of cases and did not further impact functional preservation beyond that observed with CM. CM can also be considered for the management of DB after PN in select patients. Although DB carries substantial risk, encouraging outcomes can be experienced in the great majority of cases. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: PERIOPERATIVE COMPLICATIONS OF LOW ANTERIOR ACCESS SINGLE PORT RETROPERITONEAL ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY VERSUS MULTI PORT ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Nicolas A. Soputro, Anthony Tundo, Anastasia Mavridis, Jacob O'Hara, Alissa Elanjian, Graham Kupsaw, Jack Considine, Jewel Bamby, Ruben Sauer Calvo, Gianna Jimenez, Dattatraya Patil, Mehr Nasir-Moin, Sean Horan, Kennedy E. Okhawere, Gabriela Nieto-Blanco, Sarah Duncan, Shamsunnahar Imtiaz, Abdulrahman Al-Bayati, Lin Wang, Karim Daher, Rui M. Bernardino, Ithaar Derweesh, Srinivas Vourganti, Akshay Bhandari, Reza Mehrazin, Adam Lorentz, Jennifer Linehan, Firas Abdollah
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate and compare the incidence of perioperative complications between Single Port (SP) Low Anterior Access (LAA) Retroperitoneal Robotic Partial Nephrectomy (RAPN) and Multi-Port (MP) RAPN. METHODS: A retrospective review was completed on the prospectively maintained, IRB-approved database of the SP Advanced Research Consortium (SPARC) to identify 458 consecutive patients who underwent LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN between 2022 and 2025. This cohort was compared with MP-RAPN cases performed between 2010 and 2025. Baseline clinicodemographic, intraoperative, and postoperative outcomes were collected, with inferential statistics as presented. Postoperative complications were reported according to the Clavien-Dindo classifications, with major complications defined as those of grade 33a. A multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the independent predictors of major complications based on age, BMI, comorbidity burden, baseline renal function, tumor complexity, and the robotic surgical approach. RESULTS: A total of 9984 patients were included in our analysis. Compared to MP-RAPN, the SP group was older (median age, 62 vs. 61 years, p=0.037), had a higher BMI (median, 28.8 vs. 27.1 kg/m2, p<0.001), greater comorbidity burden (median CCI, 3 vs. 3, p=0.011), and overall lower tumor complexity (median RENAL score, 6 vs. 7, p<0.001). Intraoperative complications occurred in 2% of the SP-RAPN and 2.9% of the MP-RAPN (p=0.105), while postoperative complications were reported in 12.9% and 12.6% following the SP and MP procedures, respectively (p=0.905). Major complications were similarly low between the two robotic approaches (3.5% vs. 3.1%, p=0.722). On multivariate analysis, the SP approach was not revealed as an independent predictor of major complications (OR 1.730, 95%CI 0.917 – 3.003, p=0.068). However, higher CCI (OR 1.125, 95% CI 1.023 – 1.226, p=0.009), lower preoperative renal function (OR 0.992, 95% CI 1.028 – 1.226, p=0.045), and a higher RENAL score (OR 1.260, 95% CI 1.160 – 1.340, p<0.001) emerged as independent predictors of major postoperative complications. CONCLUSIONS: This multi-institutional comparative study demonstrates that the novel LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN is associated with low perioperative morbidity comparable to MP-RAPN. The favorable complication profile supports its safe integration into the minimally invasive surgical armamentarium for renal tumors.

title: INCIDENCE OF INCISIONAL HERNIA AND ABDOMINAL WALL BULGE FOLLOWING LOW ANTERIOR ACCESS SINGLE PORT ROBOTIC RETROPERITONEAL PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY: A REPORT FROM THE SINGLE PORT ADVANCED RESEARCH CONSORTIUM (SPARC)
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Nicolas A. Soputro, Alissa Elanjian, Jacob O'Hara, Graham Kupsaw, Anastasia Mavridis, Ruben Sauer Calvo, Jewel Bamby, Gianna Jimenez, Arianna Biasatti, Dattatraya Patil, Anthony Tundo, Jack Considine, Mehr Nasir-Moin, Sean Horan, Kennedy E. Okhawere, Gabriela Nieto-Blanco, Sarah Duncan, Abdulrahman Al-Bayati, Karim Daher, Lin Wang, Shamsunnahar Imtiaz, Samarpit Rai, Adam Lorentz, Jennifer Linehan, Ithaar Derweesh, Srinivas Vourganti, Firas Abdollah, Craig Rogers
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the incidence of incisional hernia and postoperative bulge following Low Anterior Access (LAA) Single Port (SP) Robotic Retroperitoneal Partial Nephrectomy (RAPN) METHODS: A retrospective review was performed on the prospectively maintained, IRB-approved multi-institutional database of the Single Port Advanced Research Consortium (SPARC) to identify 458 consecutive patients who underwent LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN between 2023 and 2025. Postoperative bulge was defined as any protrusion secondary to weakness of the anterior abdominal wall muscle in the absence of any radiological evidence of incisional hernia. Baseline clinicodemographic, perioperative outcomes, and follow-up information were collected, with descriptive statistics as presented. RESULTS: All procedures were completed successfully via a 3-4 cm incision without any evidence of intraoperative complications. At a median follow-up of 12 months (IQR 5.7-20), two patients (0.4%) developed incisional hernia, both of which contained fat and were managed conservatively. Postoperative bulge was reported in six (1.3%) patients, with none requiring additional intervention. When considering some of the risk factors for incisional hernia, the median BMI of our cohort was 29 kg/m2 (IQR 25.1 – 33.2), with 198 (43.2%) reporting active or prior smoking history and 227 (49.6%) reporting prior abdominal surgery. Of the latter, 47 (20.7%) had a history of anterior abdominal wall hernia repair. CONCLUSIONS: LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN can be safely performed with a relatively low risk of postoperative incisional hernia and anterior abdominal wall bulge at a medium-term follow-up.

title: ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY IN LARGE RENAL MASS: COMPARISON OF SURGICAL OUTCOMES BETWEEN PATIENTS WITH CT1 AND ≥ CT2 RENAL TUMORS
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Nicolas A. Soputro, Alexandra Aponte, Rui M. Bernardino, Abdulrahman Al-Bayati, Lin Wang, Karim Daher, Christopher J. Weight, Robert J. Stein, Riccardo Autorino, Jihad Kaouk
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To compare the perioperative, oncological, and renal function outcomes of robotic partial nephrectomy (RAPN) between patients with cT1 and ≥cT2 renal masses. METHODS: A retrospective review was performed on the IRB-approved multi-institutional database of our single institution to identify all consecutive patients who underwent RAPN between 2015 – 2024. Patients were categorized based on their respective tumor size into those greater (≥cT2) or less than 7 cm (cT1). Baseline clinicodemographic, perioperative, and postoperative oncological and renal function outcomes were collected, with inferential statistics as presented. Trifecta outcomes were defined as warm ischemia time (WIT) <25 minutes, negative surgical margins, and absence of postoperative complications. Pentafecta required the achievement of trifecta outcomes, with the addition of >90% renal function preservation and no kidney disease progression at 12 months. RESULTS: Among 2001 patients, 343 (17.1%) cases were identified as ≥cT2. Of these, 57 (16.6%) and 286 (83.4%) had cT2 and cT3 diseases, respectively. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, although hilar tumors were more prevalent in the ≥cT2 cohort (34.6% vs. 10.2%, p<0.001). Compared with cT1 tumors, ≥cT2 cases demonstrated longer operative time (median, 212 vs. 180 minutes, p<0.001), longer WIT (median, 26 vs. 20 minutes, p<0.001), greater intraoperative blood loss (median, 200 vs. 150 ml, p<0.001), and a higher incidence of major complications (8.5% vs. 3.8%, p<0.001). Positive surgical margin rates remained similar between the groups (8% vs. 5.9%, p=0.146). Trifecta was achieved in 42.3% of the ≥cT2 and 64.7% of the cT1 patients (p<0.001). At 12 months, freedom from kidney disease progression was comparable (80% vs. 81.2%, p=0.615), translating to pentafecta attainment in 19.3% and 31.6% of the respective cohorts (p=0.003). After a median follow-up of 27 months, recurrence rates remained similarly low (3.6% vs. 2%, p=0.089). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the surgical efficacy of RAPN for large (≥cT2) renal masses, providing similar oncological and renal function outcomes to patients with cT1 tumors, albeit with the increased surgical complexity and morbidity risk. | | | --- | | |

title: POSITIVE SURGICAL MARGINS AFTER PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY: STILL A REAL CONCERN OR A FADING THREAT?
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Alessandro Bertini, Chiara Re, Lucia Salerno, Giacomo Musso, Francesco Cei, Giuseppe Rosiello, Attilio Barretta, Federico Belladelli, Ciro Piccolo, Natasha Disabato, Aurora Campugiani, Martina Montesano, Gaetano Ficarra, Nazario Tenace, Maurizio Colecchia, Maurilio Ponzoni, Antonio Cigliola, Andrea Necchi, Alberto Briganti, Roberto Bertini, Andrea Salonia, Francesco Montorsi, Alessandro Larcher, Umberto Capitanio
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The prognostic significance of positive surgical margins (PSM) after partial nephrectomy (PN) remains controversial, as most evidence originates from historical cohorts treated with older surgical techniques, limiting its relevance in the era of minimally invasive and robotic approaches. We aimed to reassess their prognostic value in terms of relapse-free survival (RFS), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) within a large and contemporary cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,471 patients who underwent PN between 2000 and 2023 at a tertiary referral center. Patients were stratified according to margin status (PSM vs. negative surgical margins, NSM). Kaplan-Meier analyses estimated RFS, PFS, and OS, while uni- and multivariable Cox regression models tested the association between PSM and local relapse, progression, and all-cause mortality, after adjusting for key covariates including age, smoking habits, comorbidities, tumor stage, and histology. RESULTS: Of 1,471 included patients, 83 (5.6%) had PSM on final pathology. The majority underwent open PN (66%), followed by robot-assisted (24%) and laparoscopic (10%) procedures. Apart from a higher proportion of females in the PSM group (42% vs. 30%, p=0.02), no relevant clinical or pathological differences were observed between groups. At 8-year follow-up, RFS, PFS, and OS were 74% vs. 95% (p=0.001), 88% vs. 92% (p=0.67), and 86% vs. 91% (p=0.19) for PSM vs. NSM, respectively. On MVA, PSM independently predicted a higher risk of local relapse (HR 4.26, p<0.001), but were not associated with disease progression (HR 1.34, p=0.6) or all-cause mortality (HR 2.03, p=0.08). Remarkably, when the analysis was restricted to patients who underwent laparoscopic or robot-assisted PN (n=494), PSM were not significantly associated with local relapse (HR 2.45, p=0.3). CONCLUSIONS: In this large, contemporary series of patients treated with PN, PSM were linked to an increased risk of local recurrence, yet did not significantly affect disease progression or overall survival. These findings suggest that, although PSM should not be underestimated, their long-term prognostic relevance appears limited in the current surgical era—supporting a tailored, surveillance-based approach rather than overtreatment in selected patients.

title: LONG-TERM ONCOLOGICAL AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES OF ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY BEYOND 10 YEARS
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Nicolas A. Soputro, Abdulrahman Al-Bayati, Karim Daher, Lin Wang, Rui M. Bernardino, Samarpit Rai, Rashed Ghandour, Christopher J. Weight, Riccardo Autorino, Jihad Kaouk
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the long-term oncological and renal function outcomes of robotic partial nephrectomy (RAPN) in patients with at least ten years of follow-up. METHODS: A retrospective review was completed on the IRB-approved database to identify 2,023 consecutive patients who underwent RAPN between 2015 and 2025. Only patients with at least ten years of follow-up were included. Exclusion criteria were procedures on solitary or horseshoe kidneys, renal transplant recipients, and cases associated with familial syndromes, such as Birt-Hogg-Dubé, Tuberous Sclerosis, and Von-Hippel-Lindau. RESULTS: A total of 260 patients were analyzed, with a median follow-up of 135.6 months (IQR 123 – 147.1 months). The overall survival and recurrence-free survival in our cohort were 90.4% and 97.7%, respectively. At ten years, 65.6% remained free of clinically significant kidney disease progression, with a median renal function preservation of 83.8% (IQR 70.4% – 98.6%). On multivariate analyses, independent predictors of all-cause mortality included advanced age (OR 1.156; 95% CI 1.082 – 1.250, p<0.001), lower preoperative hemoglobin (OR 0.624; 95% CI 0.405 – 0.920, p=0.023), and a higher complexity tumor according to the RENAL score (OR 1.603; 95% CI 1.183 – 2.246, p=0.004). In addition, the predictors of kidney disease progression at ten years were higher comorbidity burden per the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (OR 1.620; 95% CI 1.115 – 2.570, p=0.022), lower preoperative renal function (OR 0.949; 95% CI 0.917 – 0.977, p<0.001), and reduced GFR preservation at one year post-surgery (OR 0.206; 95% CI 0.043 – 0.549, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: RAPN confers relatively favorable long-term oncological and renal function preservation in patients who survive beyond ten years. However, overall survival and risk of kidney disease progression remain influenced by various clinicodemographic and perioperative factors, including age, comorbidity burden, renal function, and tumor complexity.

title: PARENCHYMAL VOLUME AND FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY AFTER CLAMPED PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY (PN): POTENTIAL DISCREPANCIES
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Eran Maina, Kieran Lewis, Akira Kazama, Carlos Munoz-Lopez, Nityam Rathi, Jayant Siva, Zaeem Lone, Angelica Bartholomew, Rebecca Campbell, Jihad Kaouk, Samuel Haywood, Christopher Weight, Nima Almassi, Jianbo Li, Steven Campbell
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Split renal function (SRF) measurements have enabled evaluation of functional outcomes specific to the kidney exposed to ischemia after PN. Parenchymal volume analysis (PVA) using semiautomated 3D imaging software appears superior to traditional nuclear renal scans (NRS) for assessing SRF. Our objective was to evaluate how ischemia during PN impacts the accuracy of PVA for estimating functional outcomes. METHODS: Retrospective study of all PN (2010-22) at our institution with available pre/postoperative NRS and cross-sectional imaging. Differences between NRS and PVA-derived ipsilateral SRF estimates were evaluated in warm/cold ischemia subgroups. The relationship between ischemia time and PVA/NRS discordance was evaluated with linear and segmented-regression analysis. Correction for PVA overestimation was applied to a previously published cohort of PN patients with prolonged ischemia. RESULTS: Among 437 PN, 246 (56%) and 191 (44%) were managed with warm/cold ischemia, with median ischemia times of 21/28 min, respectively. Preoperative PVA and NRS-based ipsilateral SRF estimates were nearly identical(r=0.94). Post-PN, median PVA-based estimates of ipsilateral SRF were significantly higher than NRS-derived estimates after warm-ischemia(WI)(44% vs. 42%, p=0.001), which was not observed with hypothermia. Segmented regression revealed increasing PVA/NRS discordance at >25 min WI (p=0.04). No relationship was observed between ischemia time and PVA/NRS discordance for hypothermia or limited WI. Correcting for PVA overestimation in an independent cohort demonstrated that functional decline associated with prolonged WI was 2-3-fold greater than estimated by PVA alone. CONCLUSIONS: With prolonged WI, there is discordance between parenchymal volume and function that progressively increases beyond 25 min. Applying this correction to an independent cohort of prolonged WI patients showed a 9% fall in recovery for every 10 min beyond 25 min, 2-fold greater than previously reported for PVA-based estimates. Avoidance of prolonged WI should be considered in patients with solitary kidneys and/or significant pre-existing CKD.

title: FAILURE-TO-RESCUE AND AGE: LESSONS FROM PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY PATIENTS
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Alaa Balaghi, Nadim W. Alame, Mohammad Ali Mazloum, Nader Nawfal, Wael Farchoukh, Albert El Hajj
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Failure-to-rescue (FTR) is a common quality metric used in general surgery, but its exploration in the urology field is not well studied. It is defined as death following one or more major post-operative complications. In patients undergoing partial nephrectomy, associated with slightly more acute complications versus radical nephrectomy, assessing FTR via ACS-NSQIP database may prove to be crucial. METHODS: Using the appropriate CPT codes, patients that underwent partial nephrectomy between the years of 2019-2022 were selected. We decided to assess changes in the FTR rate based on age group percentiles of the patient population, <52 years (25th percentile, 52-69 (25th-75th percentile), and >69 years (75th percentile). FTR was measured as death following development of any Clavien Dindo Grade 3+ complication 30 days post-operatively. Univariate logistic regression followed by adjustment for baseline characteristics was done by multivariate binary logistic regression. RESULTS: 13,301 patients were found that underwent partial nephrectomy on the NSQIP database. The mortality rate in this population was 0.2% while FTR overall in this population was 5.96%, with it steadily increasing with age: 2.50% (<52 years), 3.64% (52-69 years), and 11.29% (>69 years). The most common complication Grade that occurred in patients that survived partial nephrectomy was Clavien Dindo Grade 2 (76.3%) while patients that died mainly developed Clavien Dindo Grade 4 (95.7%). After adjustment with multivariate binary logistic regression, older age groups were associated with higher odds of FTR in comparison to the young age group (<52): 1.501 (52-69, p-value=0.630) and 7.140 (>69, p-value=0.014). CONCLUSIONS: Partial nephrectomy is a surgery known to have acute post-operative complications that require their own immediate attention. Monitoring proves crucial in these patients, especially the older age groups, as they could lead to significantly higher mortality rates. Moreover, evaluating failure-to-rescue rates these patients at an institutional level may further provide a quality assessment metric to provide the best care for their patients. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: SURGERY ON THE EDGE: REAL-WORLD OUTCOMES OF PARTIAL AND RADICAL NEPHRECTOMY IN PATIENTS WITH STAGE 4 CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Pietro Scilipoti, Francesco Trevisani, Bettiga Arianna, Mattia Longoni, Alessandro Bertini, Chiara Re, Lucia Salerno, Giacomo Musso, Francesco Cei, Giuseppe Rosiello, Federico Belladelli, Ciro Piccolo, Sabrina Bettini, Daniela Canibus, Natasha Disabato, Aurora Campugiani, Gaetano Ficarra, Alberto Briganti, Giorgio Gandaglia, Roberto Bertini, Andrea Salonia, Francesco Montorsi, Alessandro Larcher, Umberto Capitanio
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Patients with stage 4 chronic kidney disease (CKD4) have a substantial risk of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Management of localized renal tumors is controversial, as both radical (RN) and partial nephrectomy (PN) may precipitate renal decline, yet evidence on postoperative functional and oncological outcomes in this high-risk group is limited. We aimed to characterize renal function trajectories, ESRD risk, and perioperative morbidity among CKD4 patients undergoing renal surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 4,019 consecutive patients who underwent PN or RN (1987-2023) at a tertiary center. CKD4 was defined as baseline eGFR 15-29 ml/min/1.73m2. Outcomes included postoperative renal function decline (ΔeGFR=pre - postoperative eGFR) and progression to ESRD (eGFR15 ml/min/1.73m2) at last follow-up. ESRD was modelled as a competing-risk event with death as competing endpoint. 90-day postop complications were recorded. Multivariable linear regression (MVA) assessed predictors of ΔeGFR. Fine–Gray competing-risk regression identified predictors of ESRD. Logistic regression compared complication rates between PN and RN. RESULTS: 67 CKD4 patients met inclusion criteria; 37 (55%) underwent RN. RN patients had larger tumours (7 vs 4.7 cm, p=0.002), with otherwise comparable baseline characteristics. At a median follow-up of 20 months, 15% progressed to ESRD. Median postoperative ΔeGFR was 1 ml/min/1.73m2 (IQR –2.3, 6.2), with no difference between PN and RN (p>0.9). On MVA, RN predicted greater short-term functional decline (p=0.007). The 60-month cumulative incidence of ESRD was similar in PN and RN (22% vs 20%, HR 0.65, p=0.4). Younger age was associated with lower ESRD risk (HR 0.94, p0.001). Overall, 57% had postop complications, with no difference between PN and RN (60% vs 54%, OR 0.78, p=0.6). Bleeding/hematoma occurred more often after PN (40% vs 16%), whereas acute kidney injury was more frequent after RN (30% vs 17%). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CKD4 undergoing renal surgery, RN led to greater short-term renal function decline but did not increase long-term ESRD risk compared with PN. Overall complication rates were high but comparable between approaches. These data provide contemporary real-world benchmarks for counselling CKD4 patients with localized renal tumours and call for individualized surgical strategies in this rare, high-risk population.

title: FROM GLYCEMIC CONTROL TO RENAL OUTCOMES: DO GLP-1 AGONISTS SLOW KIDNEY FUNCTION DECLINE AFTER RADICAL NEPHRECTOMY?
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Amar Kassim, Noor Banihashem Ahmad, Sri S. Manivasagam, Jay D. Raman
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Radical nephrectomy (RN) results in immediate reduction in renal function and accelerates age-related decline. While glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have shown reno-protective effects in patients with diabetes, their impact on renal function after RN remains unexplored. The present study aims to evaluate the association between GLP-1 RA use and renal function outcomes following RN using a multi-institutional dataset. METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2005–2024). Adult patients (≥18 years) undergoing RN were stratified by GLP-1 RA use. Outcomes included change in eGFR, acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and dialysis dependence defined by ICD-10 codes at 1, 2, and 5 years. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess event-free survival and risk. RESULTS: After matching, 3,840 patients per cohort were analyzed. Mean eGFR was consistently higher in the GLP-1 RA group at 1 year (49.5 vs. 44.4 ml/min/1.73m2, p=0.01), 2 years (49.2 vs. 43.9, p=0.005), and 5 years (49.2 vs. 43.4, p=0.001). GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with significantly lower AKI rates at 1 year (6.3% vs. 12.3%, RR 1.95), 2 years (8.8% vs. 16%, RR 1.82), and 5 years (12.6% vs. 20.8%, RR 1.65; p for all 0.001). CKD incidence was lower in GLP-1 RA cohort at 1 year (15.8% vs. 26.2%, RR 1.66), 2 years (20.3% vs. 30.1%, RR 1.49), and 5 years (24.1% vs. 37%, RR 1.53; p for all 0.001). Dialysis dependence was markedly lower in GLP-1 RA cohort at 2 years (0.8% vs. 5.7%, RR 7.07) and 5 years (1.7% vs. 8.1%, RR 4.86; p0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed improved event-free survival for AKI and dialysis dependence (p0.05), but not for CKD (p=0.11) ( Figures 1 and 2). Cox modeling revealed GLP-1 RA use was independently associated with reduced risk of AKI (HR 0.58, p0.0001) and dialysis dependence (HR 0.37, p0.0001), but not CKD (HR 0.92, p=0.51). CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly better preservation of renal function and fewer renal complications and after radical nephrectomy for RCC. These findings highlight the reno-protective potential of GLP-1 RAs post-nephrectomy and support prospective evaluation.

title: LONG-TERM RENAL FUNCTION AFTER RADICAL NEPHRECTOMY AND IVC THROMBECTOMY: A MULTICENTER ANALYSIS
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Ethan Wan, Vaneeza Mukhtar, Alireza Dehghanmanshadi, Emily Biben, Kartik Patel, Kennedy Kuykendall, Andrew M. Fang, James E. Ferguson, Ahmet M. Aydin, Charles Peyton
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Radial nephrectomy with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombectomy is a complex operation presumably associated with surgically induced acute kidney injury (AKI). However, specific risk factors associated with AKI and long-term renal insufficiency (LTRI) for IVC tumor thrombectomy patients are not well described. We evaluated incidence of and clinicopathological factors associated with LTRI in surgically treated patients after radical nephrectomy and IVC tumor thrombus. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter review of patients undergoing radical nephrectomy with IVC tumor thrombectomy between 2015 and 2025. Patient demographics, preoperative, and postoperative variables were collected. LTRI was defined as a ≥1 chronic kidney disease stage decline from baseline at most recent follow-up. Temporary AKI was defined as a 1.5x increase in baseline creatinine at discharge after surgery. Univariate logistic regressions were performed. Variables with clinical relevance were included in a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of LTRI. Rates of AKI and LTRI were compared between tumor thrombi levels 0-2 vs. 3-4, and the eGFR change for each patient was plotted. RESULTS: Among 117 patients with complete follow-up data, the AKI rate was 15.5% and the LTRI rate was 50.4% ( Table). Median follow-up length was 530 days. On both univariate and multivariate analyses, older age and pre-existing hypertension were significantly associated with LTRI. Neither AKI nor LTRI rates differed by tumor thrombus level, but eGFR decline long-term was lower in patients with level 3-4 IVC thrombus compared to those with level 0-2 (p=0.03). Many patients who did not develop LTRI experienced an improvement in renal function long-term ( Figure). CONCLUSIONS: Age and hypertension at the time of surgery are independently associated with LTRI. Tumor thrombus level does not predict temporary adverse renal function outcomes, though patients with higher level thrombi appear to have less eGFR decline long-term. Presumably, this may be related to removing bulky tumor thrombus from the IVC and improving contra-lateral kidney outflow. | | | --- | | |

title: WHEN THE THROMBUS RISES: INFERIOR VENA CAVA INVOLVEMENT IMPAIRS PREOPERATIVE RENAL FUNCTION IN RENAL CELL CARCINOMA
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Giacomo Musso, Francesco Trevisani, Francesco Cei, Chiara Re, Pietro Scilipoti, Mattia Longoni, Alessandro Bertini, Lucia Salerno, Ciro Piccolo, Natasha Disabato, Federico Belladelli, Martina Montesano, Gaetano Ficarra, Aurora Campugiani, Giuseppe Rosiello, Roberto Bertini, Rayan Matloob, Giorgio Gandaglia, Alberto Briganti, Andrea Salonia, Francesco Montorsi, Ithaar H. Derweesh, Alessandro Larcher, Umberto Capitanio
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In renal cell carcinoma (RCC), a venous tumor thrombus (VTT) extending into the inferior vena cava (IVC) may impair both ipsi-and contralateral renal venous outflow, predisposing to renal dysfunction. We compared survival outcomes between renal vein (RV) and IVC VTT and assessed whether caval extension is independently associated with preoperative chronic kidney disease (preopCKD). METHODS: From a prospectively maintained database, we retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing nephrectomy with VTT, dichotomized as RV or IVC (T3b/T3c) involvement. Overall (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were analyzed using restricted mean survival time (RMST) up to =60 months. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between VTT extension and preopCKD (eGFR 60 ml/min/1.73 m2), adjusting for renal-function confounders (diabetes, Charlson Comorbidity Index \[CCI\], smoking, ECOG, age, sex, BMI, tumor size). RESULTS: Among 389 patients, 238 (61%) had RV VTT and 151 (39%) IVC VTT (111 T3b, 40 T3c). Median follow-up was 75 months (IQR 67–84). For OS (τ=60), RMST was 44 months (95% CI 41–47) for RV VTT vs 33 months (95% CI 28–37) for IVC VTT, a ΔRMST of +11months (95% CI +6 to +18; p<0.001). The RMST ratio (RV/IVC)=1.35 (95% CI 1.16–1.57; p<0.001) indicated 35% more event-free survival time for RV VTT. For CSS, RMST was 46 months (95% CI 43–49) vs 38 months (95% CI 34–43), ΔRMST +8 months (95%CI +2 to +13; p=0.006) and RMST ratio 1.21 (95% CI 1.05–1.38; p=0.009). PreopCKD occurred in 59 (25%) RV VTT and 56 (37%) IVC VTT (p=0.01). At multivariable analysis, IVC VTT was independently associated with higher odds of preopCKD (OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.23–3.79; p=0.025), together with higher CCI (OR 1.50; p=0.006), increasing age (OR 1.10; p<0.001), higher BMI (OR 1.09; p=0.041), and larger tumor size (OR 1.10; 95% CI 1.01–1.19; p=0.048). CONCLUSIONS: IVC involvement by VTT is associated with significantly shorter 5-year event-free survival for both OS and CSS and with increased risk of preoperative CKD, reflecting the hemodynamic burden of caval obstruction on bilateral renal drainage. These findings underscore the importance of proactive renoprotective strategies in patients with IVC thrombus extension and warrant validation in larger multicentric cohorts.

title: LONG-TERM OUTCOMES OF SURGICAL AND ENDOVASCULAR INTERVENTIONS FOR SPORADIC RENAL ANGIOMYOLIPOMA
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Rebecca Spivak, Omer Anis
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Renal angiomyolipomas (AMLs) are the most common benign renal tumors, composed of varying proportions of dysmorphic blood vessels, smooth muscle, and fat tissue. Approximately 80% of AMLs occur sporadically, most often in middle-aged women, and are frequently discovered incidentally. Larger tumors (>4 cm) or symptomatic lesions carry increased risks of hemorrhage and renal function decline. Treatment options include partial or total nephrectomy and selective arterial embolization, each with distinct implications for renal preservation and retreatment. However, long-term outcomes, particularly renal function preservation and retreatment rates, remain limited. This study evaluates renal function preservation and retreatment rates after intervention for sporadic AMLs using a large clinical database. METHODS: Adult patients (18–90 years) with sporadic renal AML who underwent nephrectomy (n=2,987) or arterial embolization (n=1,293) were identified from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Patients with tuberous sclerosis or who were deceased were excluded. Outcomes included need for secondary treatment and renal function (serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate \[eGFR\] were assessed from the most recent available measurements prior to initial intervention, within 5 years, and within 10 years). Kaplan-Meier analysis and comparative risk estimates, including risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio, hazard ratio were used to compare retreatment rates between groups. RESULTS: After exclusions, nephrectomy patients were 58% female (mean age 66), and embolization patients were 81% female (mean age 63). Patients undergoing embolization had significantly higher rates of repeat intervention compared to those receiving nephrectomy (13.8% vs. 2.1%, p<0.001). When comparing the embolization and nephrectomy cohorts, the nephrectomy group had a significantly lower GFR compared to the embolization group within 5 and 10 years and no significant difference in creatinine levels. CONCLUSIONS: Selective arterial embolization is associated with better renal function but a higher likelihood of repeat intervention, whereas nephrectomy provides more durable tumor control at the cost of reduced renal reserve. These findings highlight the clinical trade-off between renal preservation and definitive disease control when selecting therapy for sporadic AML. Embolization may be preferred for patients for whom renal preservation is a priority, particularly younger individuals, those with bilateral disease, or pre-existing renal impairment, while nephrectomy is best reserved for large symptomatic tumors, failed embolization, or suspected malignancy. Prospective studies incorporating tumor characteristics and symptom burden are needed to guide long-term management strategies.

title: SINGLE PORT ROBOTIC NEPHROURETERECTOMY: A MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL EXPERIENCE FROM THE SINGLE PORT ADVANCED RESEARCH CONSORTIUM (SPARC)
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Nicolas A. Soputro, Alireza Deghanmanshadi, Jack Considine, Federico Lavagno, Melissa Moran, Ernest Kaufmann, Ruben Sauer-Calvo, Roberto Contieri, Redi Gishto, Alec Zhu, Jeffrey W. Nix, Srinivas Vourganti, Reza Mehrazin, Saum Ghodoussipour, Simona Ingrassano, Paolo Gontero, Firas Abdollah, Craig Rogers, Ryan J. Nelson, Sisto Perdona, Agostino Mattei, Christian Fankhauser, Simone Crivellaro, Jihad Kaouk, Sammy Elsamra, Soroush Rais-Bahrami, Riccardo Autorino
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To investigate the safety and efficacy of robotic nephroureterectomy (RNU) performed using the purpose-built Single Port (SP) robotic platform. METHODS: A retrospective review was completed on the IRB-approved multi-institutional database of the Single Port Advanced Research Consortium (SPARC) to identify all consecutive patients who underwent SP-RNU between 2018 and 2025. Baseline clinicodemographic, intraoperative, and postoperative outcomes were collected, with descriptive statistics as presented. RESULTS: A total of 125 patients were included, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 62 – 77) and a median BMI of 26.8 kg/m2 (IQR 23.2 – 30.8). All cases were completed successfully within a median operative time of 223 minutes (IQR 185 – 271) and a median intraoperative blood loss of 80 ml (IQR 50 – 150). Supine position was preferred in 51.6% and most cases were completed via a retroperitoneal approach (80.5%). An additional port was utilized in 48% of the procedures. On histopathology, urothelial carcinoma was identified in 83.1%, with positive surgical margins reported in 7.1%. Postoperatively, the median length of stay was 2 days (IQR 1 – 3), with major complications observed in 12.8%. At a median follow-up of 6 months (IQR 2 – 11), 25.4% of the cohort received neoadjuvant therapy, and recurrence was observed in 21.9%. CONCLUSIONS: RNU can be safely and effectively completed using the SP robotic platform, featuring satisfactory perioperative and oncological outcomes. Nevertheless, longer follow-up data remain necessary to ensure the adequacy of the technique and optimal patient selection amidst the growing repertoire of minimally invasive surgical modalities. | | | --- | | |

title: ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY FOR COMPLEX VERSUS NON-COMPLEX RENAL TUMORS: A SINGLE-SURGEON DECADE-LONG EXPERIENCE ANALYZING FUNCTIONAL AND ONCOLOGIC OUTCOMES, RECURRENCE, PREDICTORS OF COMPLICATIONS, AND TRIFECTA/PENTAFECTA ACHIEVEMENT
session: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I (IP05)
authors: Yuvaraja B. Thyavihally, Akash Shah, Rahul Zalse, Abhinav Pednekar, Achint Bajpai, Usha Vaswani, Maithili Kunte, Mohd Salman Aquib
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) is increasingly used to treat complex renal tumors. This study compared functional and oncological outcomes of RAPN in complex (RENAL score ≥7) versus non-complex tumors (RENAL score <7). Secondary aim was to identify predictors of postoperative complications in both groups. METHODS: A prospectively maintained uro-oncology database was reviewed for all RAPN procedures performed between January 2012 and July 2024 at Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, Mumbai. A total of 635 patients were categorized into complex (n=358) and non-complex tumors (n=277) using the RENAL Nephrometry Score (radius, exophytic/endophytic, nearness to sinus/collecting system, anterior/posterior, polar location). Demographics, tumor complexity, perioperative and pathological data were analyzed. Trifecta was defined as negative margins, no postoperative complications, and warm ischemia time (WIT) <25 min. Pentafecta additionally required >90% estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) preservation and no chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage up-migration at 1 year. Predictors of outcomes and complications were evaluated by logistic regression. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 67 months. Complex tumors showed higher clinical T stage (p=0.007), RENAL scores (p=0.002), and longer WIT (p<0.0001). Trifecta and pentafecta were significantly more frequently achieved in non-complex tumors. However, recurrence rates were similar (p=0.999). No perioperative mortality occurred. One-year eGFR preservation did not differ (p=0.706). Complex tumors demonstrated marginally higher Clavien-Dindo ≥3 complications, but without statistical significance (p=0.511). On multivariate analysis, multifocality predicted major complications in complex tumors, while prolonged WIT was the major predictor in non-complex tumors. Higher pre-operative eGFR and shorter WIT predicted better trifecta and pentafecta outcomes in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: RAPN is safe and effective for complex renal tumors with comparable functional preservation, major complication rates, and recurrence to non-complex tumors. Though trifecta/pentafecta achievement is lower in complex cases due to tumor anatomy and longer ischemia, modern robotic platforms facilitate precise excision and reconstruction, enabling successful management of challenging renal masses.

title: ROBOTIC-ASSISTED ULTRASOUND-GUIDED PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMY: INITIAL CLINICAL EXPERIENCE FROM A CONSECUTIVE SERIES OF TEN CASES
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Andrew Amenyogbe, Karen L. Stern, Mitch Humphreys, Jackson Cabo
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Safe and precise renal access remains the most critical and technically demanding step of percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL). Fluoroscopy-guided access emits ionizing radiation and offers limited soft-tissue discrimination, whereas ultrasound guidance eliminates radiation but requires advanced hand-eye coordination. The Focalist system (Mendeara Inc.) is a robotic-assisted handheld ultrasound platform that orients the needle and provides real-time needle-tip tracking and on-screen trajectory planning. We present the first consecutive clinical series worldwide evaluating feasibility, workflow integration, and perioperative outcomes using this system for PCNL access. METHODS: A prospective observational study included ten consecutive renal units undergoing ultrasound-guided PCNL with the Focalist system between August and September 2025. Procedures were performed by an endourologist or trainee. Primary endpoints were successful collecting-system access and first-attempt success. Secondary outcomes included time metrics, radiation exposure, papillary targeting, complications, and surgeon-reported usability (5-point Likert scale). RESULTS: Robot-assisted ultrasound-guided access was successful in 8/10 renal units (80%) with first-attempt success in 6/10 (60%) and papillary access in 7/8 (87.5%) successful cases. Mean time from target acquisition to needle at target was 270 ± 324 s; needle insertion time averaged 14 ± 19 s. Mean fluoroscopy time was 15.5 ± 23.7 s (mean air kerma 5.5 ± 11.3 mGy). No device-related complications occurred. Usability scores were high (ease of setup 5.0, ease of use 4.1, confidence in placement 4.6), with smooth workflow integration across attending, fellow, and resident operators. CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted ultrasound-guided renal access using the Focalist system was feasible, safe, and rapidly adoptable across experience levels, achieving high access success with minimal fluoroscopy and no complications. Real-time needle tracking and ergonomic probe stabilization supported efficient targeting, while limited ultrasound field of view contributed to two failures. This low-capital, bedside robotic adjunct may lower barriers to urologist-performed ultrasound-guided PCNL. Larger comparative studies are warranted to validate performance, learning curves, and cost-effectiveness. | | | --- | | |

title: SOLVING CHALLENGES OF FLEXIBLE URETEROSCOPES TOWARD THE SOCIAL IMPLEMENTATION OF URETEROSCOPE-ASSISTED ROBOTS-AI-BASED SOFTWARE AS MEDICAL DEVICE DEVELOPMENT RESEARCH
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Satoshi Kobayashi, Keiji Tsukino, Mikifumi Kora, Nakagawa Shohei, Tokiyoshi Tanegashima, Shigehiro Tsukahara, Takashi Matsumoto, Masaki Shiota, Masatoshi Eto
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Robotic ureteroscopy (rURS) is emerging in Western countries as a potential paradigm shift from flexible ureteroscopy (fURS). Despite its utility, fURS imposes ergonomic strain on surgeons due to structural limitations. This study aimed to quantitatively compare the motion characteristics between expert and novice surgeons during flexible ureteroscopy (fURS) using an AI-based pose estimation application. By analyzing joint trajectories, speeds, and angular variations, ergonomic stability and surgical proficiency were evaluated. METHODS: Five participants (experts: n=3, novices: n=2) performed standardized fURS tasks on a 3D-printed kidney phantom. The AI-based system (MediaPipe Pose) estimated three-dimensional joint coordinates and calculated movement distances (cm), velocities (cm/s), and angular variations. Statistical comparisons between groups were performed using t-tests and Wilcoxon tests. RESULTS: Experts demonstrated significantly smaller joint movements than novices, as shown in (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191292.44613.d7.02#F1). The right wrist movement distance was markedly shorter in experts (471 cm) than in novices (3558 cm, p=0.0227), as were right elbow movements (277 cm vs. 2653 cm, p=0.0355). Angular variation of the shoulder was also significantly smaller in experts (32 cm vs. 90 cm, p=0.0102). In terms of motion velocity, novices showed higher speeds at the elbow (14.0 cm/s vs. 4.8 cm/s, p=0.0323) and wrist (19.2 cm/s vs. 8.0 cm/s, p=0.0488). Operation time was shorter in experts (65 s vs. 186 s, p=0.0603). CONCLUSIONS: The AI-based Pose Estimation Application successfully distinguished between expert and novice operators. Experts maintained stable postures with limited and controlled joint movements, whereas novices exhibited greater motion variability and longer procedure times. These findings demonstrate the potential of AI-driven motion analysis as a reliable tool for evaluating surgical proficiency and providing real-time feedback during robotic or endoscopic training.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED PREDICTION OF POSTOPERATIVE SEPSIS IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING SUCTION MINI-PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMY: A MULTICENTER ANALYSIS FROM THE GLOBAL STUMPS REGISTRY
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Tzevat Tefik, Rifat Burak Ergul, M. Firat Ozervarli, Daniele Castellani, Ee Jean Lim, Steffi Kar Kei Yuen, Carlotta Nedbal, Thomas R. W. Herrmann, Bhaskar K. Somani, Vineet Gauhar
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Suction mini-PCNL has advanced stone removal with lower infection rates. This study leveraged an artificial intelligence model to accurately predict postoperative sepsis following suction mini-PCNL. METHODS: We analyzed data from the STUMPS registry, a prospective, multicenter cohort of adult patients undergoing suction mini-PCNL across 30 centers between March-November 2024. Baseline patient characteristics, stone features, operative details and perioperative labs were recorded. Postoperative sepsis within 30 days was defined using qSOFA criteria. A supervised machine learning model (XGBoost) was developed to predict sepsis using patient, stone, and procedural variables. Data were split into training (80%) and test (20%) sets, with categorical variables one-hot encoded. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and confusion matrices. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP values to identify key predictors of postoperative sepsis. RESULTS: A total of 2,172 patients were included, with 87 developing postoperative sepsis. Age and preoperative GFR were similar between groups, while patients with sepsis had higher BMI and preoperative hemoglobin. Stones were slightly larger in the sepsis group. Operative factors differed markedly: lithotripsy time, number of tracts, and total operative time were higher in sepsis patients. Sheath size and peri-/postoperative labs did not differ significantly. The XGBoost model predicted postoperative sepsis with excellent accuracy (AUC 0.946). At the optimal cutoff, sensitivity was 0.88, specificity 0.99, overall accuracy 98.4%, and Cohen's κ=0.802. Positive and negative predictive values were 0.75 and 0.995, respectively. SHAP analysis identified lithotripsy time, high Guy's stone score, stitch-based tract closure, sheath size, and exit type (exit tubeles with stent) as the strongest contributors to sepsis risk. Prolonged procedures, complex stones, and certain closure techniques increased risk, while pre-operative WBC/HGB, GFR and procedural nuances also contributed. CONCLUSIONS: Operative complexity, stone burden, and patient physiological status are key predictors of postoperative sepsis after suction mini- PCNL. Machine learning models can reliably identify high-risk patients, supporting early risk stratification and targeted preventive strategies. | | | --- | | |

title: COMPARING EXTRACORPOREAL SHOCK WAVE LITHOTRIPSY AND URETEROSCOPIC LITHOTRIPSY FOR THE MANAGEMENGT OF LOWER URETERIC STONES: A RANDOMIZED TRIAL
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Shiv Charan Navriya, Jaydeep Jain, Gautam R. Chaudhary, Mahendra Singh, Deepak P. Bhirud, Arjun S. Sandhu
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Acute colic due to lower ureteric calculi is a significant cause of morbidity, necessitating prompt and effective management. Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL) and Ureteroscopic Lithotripsy (URSL) are widely employed treatment modalities. Comparative data on their outcomes, particularly in acute settings, remain sparse. This study aim to evaluate and compare the efficacy, patient satisfaction, and cost-effectiveness of ESWL and URSL in managing lower ureteric stones presenting with acute colic. METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted at AIIMS, Jodhpur, involving 164 patients presenting with acute colic due to lower ureteric stones. Patients were randomized equally into two groups: ESWL (Group A, n=82) and URSL (Group B, n=82). Primary outcomes included stone-free rates (SFR) at 1 week, 8 weeks, and 3 months. Secondary outcomes encompassed pain intensity, analgesic requirements, complications, quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), loss of working days, and treatment costs. RESULTS: URSL demonstrated significantly higher SFR at all time points compared to ESWL (95% vs. 55.83% at 3 months, p<0.0001). Group A exhibited fewer complications (43.33% vs. 25%, p=0.006) and shorter recovery times, reflected in fewer working days lost (5.08 ± 1.08 vs. 8 ± 0.64 days, p<0.0001). While ESWL was less expensive (mean: Rs 4386.67 ± 1827.76 vs. Rs 5049.17 ± 2067.26, p=0.009), URSL yielded higher patient satisfaction scores (4.07 ± 0.66 vs. 3.78 ± 0.71, p=0.002). CONCLUSIONS: For lower ureteric calculi, URSL offers superior stone clearance and patient satisfaction, particularly for larger or more complex stones, while ESWL remains a viable, less invasive, and cost-effective option for smaller stones. These findings highlight the importance of tailoring treatment decisions based on patient and stone-specific factors.

title: REDUCED LIKELIHOOD OF POST-OPERATIVE URINARY TRACT INFECTION WITH SINGLE-USE URETEROSCOPE WITH REAL-TIME INFRARENAL PRESSURE MONITORING VS. ALL OTHER SINGLE-USE URETEROSCOPES FOR PATIENTS WITH KIDNEY STONES
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Naeem Bhojani, Kathryn Morris, Jenifer White, Sirikan Rojanasarot, Emma D. Tran, Manoj Monga
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Ureteroscopy (URS) carries inherent risks including intrarenal pressure (IRP) elevation and can lead to complications such as urinary tract infection (UTI). This study compared post-operative UTI associated with the LithoVue™ Elite Single-Use Digital Flexible Ureteroscope (LVE) with pressure monitoring vs. all other single-use ureteroscopes as comparative effectiveness evidence for LVE with pressure monitoring is needed. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health record (EHR) data from Truveta. Patients undergoing URS with laser lithotripsy between January 1, 2023-June 1, 2025 and with ≥30 days follow-up after the index URS procedure were included. The prevalence of post-operative UTI 30 days from the index URS encounter was evaluated and compared for patients treated with LVE with pressure monitoring vs. all other single-use ureteroscopes. Propensity score matching was used to control for differences in baseline characteristics. RESULTS: 208 patients treated with LVE with pressure monitoring (mean age 61.4; 48.1% female; 85.1% White) were matched to 416 patients treated with other single-use ureteroscopes without pressure monitoring (mean age 61.8; 48.4% female; 85.1% White). Compared to patients treated with other single-use ureteroscopes, lower proportions of patients treated with LVE with pressure monitoring had post-operative UTI 30-days post-index (5.2% vs. 10.8%; p=0.033). Multivariable analyses confirmed significantly higher likelihood of 30-day UTI with other single-use ureteroscopes (odds ratio 2.41 \[95% confidence\ interval 1.21-5.27\]; p=0.020). Given the prevalence of URS and the high incidence of post-operative UTI with URS, use of LVE with pressure monitoring could have a transformative impact on URS patient care. CONCLUSIONS: LVE with pressure monitoring was associated with reduced 30-day post-URS UTI. These findings support clinical improvement associated with LVE and suggest that IRP monitoring may contribute to better patient outcomes. Use of LVE with pressure monitoring may be a strategy to improve patient quality of care and to help healthcare decision makers manage the expanding burden of patients with kidney stones.

title: ROBOTIC FLEXIBLE URETERORENOSCOPIC LITHOTRIPSY WITH THE ZAMENIX SYSTEM: A PRELIMINARY CLINICAL STUDY
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Seungsoo Lee, Dan Bee Lee, Won Hoon Song, Jae Min Chung, Jong Kil Nam, Sung-Woo Park, Sang Don Lee
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: This study presents our initial clinical experience with robotic flexible ureterorenoscopic stone removal using the Zamenix™ robotic system, a newly developed platform designed to enhance precision and ergonomics in endourological stone surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 18 consecutive patients who underwent robotic flexible ureterorenoscopic stone removal with the Zamenix™ system between August and December 2024\. Demographic data (age, sex, and body mass index \[BMI\]) and stone characteristics (size, location, and composition) were collected. Operative parameters, perioperative complications, and stone-free rates were analyzed. RESULTS: The cohort included 18 patients with a mean age of 52.3 ± 15.2 years (range 25–78), and 55.6% (n=10) were male. The mean BMI was 27.3 ± 5.1 kg/m2 (range 17.0–43.0). The mean stone volume was 1450.2 ± 1093.1 mm3 (range 93.2–4046.8). Stone laterality was right in 38.9%, left in 22.2%, and bilateral in 38.9% of cases. The mean operative time was 107.2 ± 26.3 minutes (range 65–175). The overall stone-free rate was 88.9%, with complete stone clearance in 38.9% of patients. Subclinical residual fragments were identified in 50.0%, and stone-free failure occurred in 11.1%. Stone composition was predominantly calcium oxalate (66.7%), followed by struvite (22.2%), cystine (5.6%), and uric acid (5.6%). Postoperative complications were limited to one case of fever and one case of steinstrasse, both managed conservatively. CONCLUSIONS: Robotic flexible ureterorenoscopic lithotripsy using the Zamenix™ system appears to be a safe and effective option for renal stone management. The system offers ergonomic and technical advantages; however, its relatively long setup time compared with conventional ureteroscopy remains a limitation to be improved in future iterations. | | | --- | | |

title: SURGEON-REPORTED PERFORMANCE OUTCOMES OF A NOVEL 6.3-FRENCH SINGLE-USE FLEXIBLE URETEROSCOPE
session: Stone Disease: Surgical Therapy (Including ESWL) I (IP06)
authors: Kevin Koo, Garrett Ungerer, Kunal Jain, Matthew Gettman, Aaron Potretzke, Kevin Wymer
