The creation of the Integrated Responsibility Centre (CRI) for Urology in 2020 marked full operational integration—enabling shared surgical planning, robotic programs, and comprehensive oncologic collaboration across sites. CONCLUSIONS: The century-long trajectory of Lisbon’s urology—from Desterro’s early cystoscopies to CHULC’s robotic surgery and multidisciplinary oncologic care—reflects a progressive model of institutional modernization. This evolution demonstrates how visionary leadership, academic cooperation, and technological adoption transformed fragmented services into a cohesive, university-affiliated center of excellence. The history of CHULC’s Urology Service stands as a paradigm for European hospital integration in urology, linking heritage to innovation within a unified academic structure.

title: FROM CANDIRU TO KETAMINE CYSTITIS: A HISTORICAL ANALYSIS OF UROLOGICAL URBAN LEGENDS AND MYTHS
session: History of Urology Forum (HF02)
authors: Kevin Parham, Hannah Moreland, Lorie Fleck
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Throughout history, urology has generated some of medicine’s most persistent legends—from the Amazonian “penis fish” to paraffin penile injections and viral social-media “party tricks.” These stories reflect changing public attitudes toward sexuality, cleanliness, and medical authority. We sought to catalog and contextualize major urologic urban legends across time and culture, tracing how scientific discovery debunked or reframed each myth. METHODS: A narrative historical review was performed using PubMed, JSTOR, and gray-literature sources (1800–2025). Legends were included if they met ≥ 1 criterion: (1) recurrent appearance in public media or folklore, (2) urologic relevance, (3) documentation or debunking in peer-reviewed literature. Each entry was characterized by its date of origin, medium of dissemination, geographic spread, and subsequent scientific clarification. RESULTS: Twenty-one discrete urologic legends were identified. Early myths (e. g., paraffin or Vaseline injections for penile enlargement, “urine is sterile”) arose in the late 19th century amid limited laboratory methods. Mid-20th-century beliefs such as “beer dissolves kidney stones” and “cranberry cures all UTIs” were propagated by consumer media. Late-century and digital-era legends—including the Candiru “penis fish,” “Blue Waffle,” and the “human wine decanter”—spread virally through television and the Internet. Some, like ketamine-induced cystitis and SGLT2-related Fournier’s gangrene, originated as sensationalized truths later verified in clinical reports. Collectively, these myths trace the evolving interplay among scientific literacy, taboos surrounding sexuality and excretion, and mass communication. CONCLUSIONS: Urology’s blend of intimacy, stigma, and curiosity has made it a fertile ground for mythmaking. Mapping these legends chronologically highlights both the hazards of misinformation and the enduring fascination with the genitourinary system. Historical awareness of such narratives can enhance modern patient education and strengthen trust in evidence-based urologic care.

title: LIQUID BIOPSY USING NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING TO PREDICT LYMPH NODE METASTASES IN PENILE SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Limirio M. Fonseca, Katia R. M. Leite, Sabrina T. R. Faria, Joao Paulo L. Silva, Claudio B. Murta, Guilherme Padovani, José Pontes, Jr, William C. Nahas
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Lymph node status is the most important prognostic factor in penile squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Inguinal lymphadenectomy remains the gold standard for staging but is associated with significant morbidity. Current non-invasive methods show poor sensitivity for micro metastases. Liquid biopsy through circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis and next-generation sequencing (NGS) offers a minimally invasive alternative for molecular risk stratification. This study aimed to evaluate whether ctDNA levels and mutational profiles correlate with pathological lymph node involvement (pN). METHODS: A single-center observational study included 21 patients with penile SCC who underwent partial or total penectomy and inguinal lymphadenectomy between 2015–2023. Preoperative plasma samples were collected for ctDNA extraction (Qiagen QIAamp). Sequencing was performed on the DNBSEQ™ platform using a 40-gene hybrid-capture panel including _TP53, NF1, TJP2, ALK_, and _FGFR_ family genes. Variant calling was conducted using the DRAGEN pipeline (hg38). Variables analyzed included ctDNA concentration, number of variants, histopathologic features, and HPV status. Associations with pN were evaluated using Mann-Whitney and Fisher’s exact tests. RESULTS: Median age was 63 years (range 32–82); 13 patients (61.9%) were pN+. Mean ctDNA concentration was higher in pN+ versus pN− (1.10 vs 0.72 ng/µL; p=0.328). The mean number of variants was significantly greater in pN+ than in pN− (20.6 vs 17.0; p=0.045). Microvascular invasion correlated with nodal metastasis (p=0.024), whereas perineural invasion, histologic grade, and HPV status showed no significant association. The most frequent variants were _NF1_, _TJP2_, _TP_ 53, and _ALK_ (95–100% of cases). CONCLUSIONS: Liquid biopsy with NGS demonstrated that higher ctDNA mutational burden correlates with lymph node metastases in penile SCC. Although ctDNA concentration alone was not discriminatory, molecular profiling may serve as a biomarker for nodal involvement and help avoid unnecessary lymphadenectomies. This is a pioneering study in penile cancer, supporting further validation in multicenter cohorts and the development of disease-specific genetic panels.

title: SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF THE TUMOR IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT AND HETEROGENEITY LANDSCAPE IN PENILE CANCER
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Peizhe Li, Jianfei Ye, Min Lu, Huiying He, Yimeng Song, Lulin Ma, Shuhua Wei
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Penile cancer is a rare but aggressive malignancy of the male genitourinary system, where lymph node metastasis predicts poor prognosis. The tumor immune microenvironment (TME) plays a critical role in tumor progression and treatment response. This study applied single-cell RNA sequencing to systematically delineate the TME of penile cancer at different disease stages, aiming to uncover molecular mechanisms of tumor progression and immune evasion, and to identify potential immunotherapeutic targets. METHODS: Fresh tumor and adjacent tissues from four penile cancer patients were analyzed, including one non-metastatic and three lymph node–metastatic cases. High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) status was confirmed by in situ hybridization and p16 immunohistochemistry. A total of 36,601 cells were processed using Cell Ranger and Seurat pipelines. Integrated analyses, including bulk RNA sequencing, cell–cell communication, pseudotime trajectory, and functional enrichment, were performed to characterize TME heterogeneity. RESULTS: Nine transcriptionally f cellular clusters were identified, highlighting marked heterogeneity within the tumor immune microenvironment. Interactions among epithelial, fibroblast, and endothelial cells promoted epithelial–mesenchymal transition, angiogenesis, and invasion. Lymph node–metastatic tumors showed increased cell cycle activity and proliferative potential. Non-metastatic tumors exhibited active innate immune responses with dendritic cell activation but also early immunosuppression through regulatory T-cell enrichment. Metastatic tumors were dominated by M2-like macrophages, exhausted and naïve T cells, indicating an immunosuppressive milieu. During progression, the TME shifted from immune activation to suppression, reflecting gradual immune escape and T-cell exhaustion as a hallmark of advanced disease. CONCLUSIONS: This study constructs the first single-cell immune atlas of penile cancer, revealing marked heterogeneity and dynamic remodeling of the TME during disease progression. The findings provide potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for immunotherapy and offer a molecular basis for individualized treatment strategies. Validation in larger patient cohorts is warranted.

title: SURVIVAL OF THE FITTEST: OUTCOMES IN NODE POSITIVE PENILE CANCER PATIENTS WHERE NON-SURGICAL MANAGEMENT IS UTILISED IN PLACE OF RILND
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Victoria Hyett, Catherine McCollum, Cameron Boyle, Rebecca Huey, Ross Vint, Allan Johnston, Michael Fraser, David Hendry, Jonathan Salmond, Matthew Rewhorn
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Approximately one-third of penile squamous cell carcinoma (pSCC) cases present with nodal disease at presentation. Radical inguinal lymph node dissection (RILND) is the standard of care for nodal-positive disease but carries substantial morbidity, with many patients unfit for surgery. This study evaluates outcomes in node positive disease managed non-surgically. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 287 adults with newly diagnosed pSCC from January 2017 to December 2024, across four regional referral centres. Data was obtained from multidisciplinary team (MDT), pathology, and electronic health records. Patient demographics, treatment modalities, and survival outcomes were analysed. RESULTS: 85 patients (29.6%) had nodal disease at presentation (N1=31, N2=13, N3=41). Mean age was 65.6 (range 31–92), with 41.2% presenting with palpable nodes. Nodal status was determined at MDT based on radiological and pathological assessment (core node sampling or sentinel node biopsy). Twelve patients with distant metastases were excluded. Median follow-up was 19.5 months. 56.5% were fit for RILND; of these 18.75% received neoadjuvant systemic anti-cancer therapy (SACT), and 20.8% received adjuvant radiotherapy. 43.5% of patients were unfit for RILND and received SACT plus radiotherapy (10.8%), radiotherapy alone (56.8%), SACT alone (10.8%), or supportive care (21.6%). The Kaplan-Meier curve below demonstrates that the best survival was in patients undergoing surgical node management. Among non-surgical patients, SACT plus radiotherapy offered the most favourable outcomes, followed by radiotherapy alone, while supportive care yielded the poorest survival. Recurrence rates were 31.7% in the surgical cohort and 30% in the non-surgical cohort, though recurrence in the latter is likely underestimated, as 72.2% died from their primary disease before recurrence could be assessed. CONCLUSIONS: RILND remains the optimal treatment for node-positive pSCC, but a significant proportion of patients (43.5%) are unfit for surgery. Although SACT in combination with radiotherapy appears to offer the best survival for these patients, prognosis in this group remains poor. Further research is needed to optimize systemic therapies and improve prognosis in patients unfit for surgical nodal management.

title: REAL-WORLD PATTERNS AND PREDICTORS OF SURGICAL LYMPH-NODE MANAGEMENT IN PENILE CANCER: INSIGHTS FROM THE EPIC COSMOS DATABASE
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Carlo Silvani, Alfonso Santangelo, Alex Stephens, Nicholas Saeedi, Tavan Zadeh, Mohit Butaney, Jack Considine, Sebastiano Nazzani, Andrea Salonia, Alberto Briganti, Francesco Montorsi, Nicola Nicolai, Emanuele Montanari, Craig Rogers, Firas Abdollah
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate management of regional lymph nodes, through sentinel node biopsy or inguinal lymph-node dissection (ILND) — either for staging or therapeutic purposes — is essential for disease control and survival in penile cancer. Current international guidelines recommend surgical nodal evaluation for all patients with ≥ T1b disease; however, adherence in real-world practice remains uncertain. We aimed to assess national patterns of surgical lymph-node management, including both staging and therapeutic dissections, and to identify factors associated with their use in patients with penile cancer. METHODS: Epic COSMOS, an aggregated electronic health record dataset encompassing over 300 million patients from >1,700 hospitals and 40,000 clinics across North America and abroad, was queried for men diagnosed with penile cancer stage ≥ T1b between 2015 and 2025. Patients with distant metastases or 1 year of follow-up were excluded. Surgical lymph-node management included any node biopsy or inguinal lymph-node dissection (ILND) performed within six months of diagnosis, in both clinically node-negative (N0) and node-positive (N+) cases. Demographic, clinical, and socioeconomic characteristics were compared by lymph-node surgical status, and multivariable models were used to assess factors independently associated with surgical management. RESULTS: Among 679 eligible patients, 240 (35%) underwent surgical lymph-node management. Patients who received lymph nodes surgery were younger (median 66 vs 69 years, p=0.011) and more frequently diagnosed in recent years (p<0.001). In multivariable analysis, higher T stage (T2 vs T1b: OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.01–2.57, p=0.047) and later year of diagnosis (OR 1.14 per year, p<0.001) were independently associated with undergoing lymph node surgery, whereas older age predicted lower odds (OR 0.99 per year, p=0.042). BMI, comorbidity, and insurance type were not significant predictors. Geographic variation persisted, with patients from the Southern part of United States less likely to undergo nodes surgery (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37–0.95, p=0.029). CONCLUSIONS: Despite established guidelines, only one in three men with ≥ T1b penile cancer underwent surgical lymph-node management, whether for staging or therapeutic intent. Utilization increased modestly over time but remained suboptimal even in most recent years, underscoring significant undertreatment of potentially curable regional disease and the need for broader adherence to evidence-based surgical practice.

title: COMPARATIVE REAL-WORLD OUTCOMES OF MULTIMODAL TREATMENT STRATEGIES IN PATIENTS WITH LOCALLY ADVANCED N>-STAGE PENILE CANCER: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Yilong Gao, Xiang Li, Yanxiang Shao, Kan Wu, Xu Hu, Yaxiong Tang, Linghao Meng
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Penile cancer is a rare malignancy, with a global incidence of approximately 0.8 cases per 100,000 men. N3-stage locally advanced disease typically presents with fixed inguinal lymph node metastases and poor prognosis. Chemotherapy is commonly used in this setting, and there has been a growing number of studies investigating immunotherapy and targeted therapy for the treatment. However, comparative data on the outcomes of different multimodal regimens remain limited. Our study aims to evaluate the outcomes of different multimodal treatments in patients with locally advanced N3-stage penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 107 patients with locally advanced N3-stage PSCC treated at our center between 2008 and 2024. Patients either received multimodal therapy or surgery alone. Clinical responses were assessed using RECIST 1.1. Treatment-related adverse events (TrAEs) and postoperative complications were graded by CTCAE v5.0 and Clavien-Dindo classification. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared by log-rank test. The approval of study was obtained from the Institutional Review Board of West China Hospital. RESULTS: Among 107 patients that all received surgery, 16 received chemotherapy, 19 received chemotherapy and targeted therapy, 2 received chemotherapy and immunotherapy, 16 received chemotherapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy. 54 underwent surgery alone. Median OS was 14.8 months (95% CI, 12.1-18.1) in the multimodal group, compared with 5.8 months (95% CI, 4.7-7.5) after surgery alone (HR 0.26; 95% CI, 0.17-0.40; p<0.001). Median PFS for patients receiving multimodal therapy was 4.4 months (95% CI, 3.5-6.0), with no statistical significance between different multimodal groups. The overall disease control rate (DCR) and objective response rate (ORR) were 79.2% and 62.3% respectively, with different DCR and ORR in each group. Treatment-related toxicities and postoperative complications were acceptable. CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal treatment significantly improved OS compared with surgery alone in patients with locally advanced N3-stage PSCC. Although no statistical significance in OS was observed among different multimodal treatment groups, the combination of chemotherapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy appeared to yield the most favorable outcomes.

title: PENILE CANCER TREATMENTS AND THEIR PSYCHIATRIC SEQUELAE: A NATIONAL ANALYSIS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Reza Lahiji, William Luke, Elizabeth Chu, Adam Braunschweig, Siddharth Marthi, Maria Grosso Zelaya, Mahdi Mottaghhi, Dattatraya Patil, Valentina Grajales, Vikram M. Narayan, Reza Nabavizadeh, Mohammad Hajiha, Kenneth Ogan, Viraj A. Master, Shreyas S. Joshi
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Penile cancer patients may be particularly vulnerable to depression, anxiety, and social isolation, yet population-level data on mental health outcomes are lacking. We investigated the incidence and predictors of mental health disease (MHD) following penile cancer diagnosis and treatment using nationally representative datasets. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the de-identified MarketScan® Commercial Claims (MCCD) and Medicare Supplemental (MSD) databases (2009–2023). Eligible patients were ≥18 years with a confirmed penile cancer (required of disease-specific treatment within three years of initial diagnosis). Those with pre-existing MHD were excluded. Treatments were categorized as radical (radical penectomy/perineal urethrostomy), partial (partial penectomy), topical (imiquimod/5-FU), or local excision. The primary outcome was new-onset MHD (major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder requiring pharmacologic therapy) within 36 months. Multivariable Cox models identified predictors. RESULTS: Among 1,633 patients (1,044 MCCD; 589 MSD), 151 (14.5%) and 83 (14.1%) developed MHD, respectively. In MCCD, radical penectomy (HR 3.33, 95% CI 1.72-6.47, p<0.001), CCI 2 (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.03-2.96, p=0.040), and CCI 3+ (HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.54-3.91, p<0.001) predicted increased MHD risk, while age in the 3rd quartile was protective (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.75, p=0.001). These variables did not significantly correlate with MHD in the MSD cohort. CONCLUSIONS: Penile cancer patients face high rates of MHD, particularly after radical surgery, in the presence of comorbidities. This relationship appeared to differ between MSD and MCCD cohorts. Survivorship models should integrate timely mental health support and address access disparities.

title: ONCOLOGICAL AND SEXUAL OUTCOMES AFTER GLANS RECONSTRUCTION WITH INVERTED URETHRAL FLAP: RESULTS FROM A SINGLE CENTER STUDY
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Salvatore Sansalone, Massimiliano Foti, Damiano Stracci, Mario Falsaperla, Antonio Minore, Francesco Dibitetto, Asgar Akhundov, Roberto Castellucci, Mauro De Dominicis
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: EAU Guidelines recommend penile preserving approach for T1 and T2 squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the penis with involvement of the glans in selected patients who commit to regular follow up (FU). We report the long-term outcomes of a cohort of patients who underwent glansectomy and pseudo-glans reconstruction with inverted urethral flap (IUF). METHODS: Data of patients who underwent glansectomy and IUF glans reconstruction for T1 and T2 penile SCC in our center between March 2007 and March 2022 were collected and a database was built. Penile MRI in erection was used to assess the invasion of the corpora cavernosa. Glansectomy and urethral dissection were performed according to the usual technique; if frozen sections were negative, the distal part of the urethra was spatulated for 2.5 cm and everted to cover the corporeal heads and form a pseudoglans. Oncological, cosmetic and sexual outcomes, including patients’ satisfaction, recurrence and need for further instrumentation, were recorded at FU. Pre-op and post-op sexual function was evaluated with the IIEF-5 questionnaire. RESULTS: 58 patients were included in this retrospective analysis. Mean age was 62 years (range 36–76). Pathology revealed 23 G2 pT1 (39.7%), 26 G3 pT1 (44.8%), and 9 pT2 (15.5%). Positive margins were found in 6 patients (10.3%), who required further surgery. Local recurrence occurred in 2 patients (3.4%). Among the 37 patients (63.8%) with good pre-operative sexual function, 27 (46.6%) reported good rigidity after surgery and 25 (43.1%) resumed sexual activity. 2 patients (3.4%) reported ventral curvature during erection, and 43 patients (74.1%) were satisfied with the cosmetic outcome. CONCLUSIONS: According to our series, glans reconstruction with IUF is an organ-sparing technique with excellent cosmetic and functional results for selected patients with SCC of the penis.

title: AGE-STRATIFIED ASSOCIATION BETWEEN INFLAMMATORY PENILE DISORDERS AND PENILE CANCER: A TENFOLD INCREASED RISK ACROSS ALL AGE GROUPS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Michael Kozlov, Myles Goliger, Esther Auerbach, Robert Adler, Anthony James, Cindy Lin, Justin Ingram, Andrew Winer, Nicholas T. Karanikolas, Jeffrey P. Weiss
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Inflammatory disorders of the prepuce and glans (IDPG), including phimosis, paraphimosis, balanitis, and balanoposthitis, are proposed risk factors for malignant penile cancer (MPC), a rare but aggressive disease. Additional established risks include human papillomavirus infection, smoking, low socioeconomic status, and lack of circumcision. Chronic inflammation is thought to promote carcinogenesis; however, large-scale studies directly linking IDPG to oncologic outcomes remain limited. To address this gap, we conducted a retrospective cohort study evaluating the association between IDPG and adverse outcomes, including MPC, amputation, nodal metastasis, and mortality. METHODS: The TriNetX Research Network (TNX) contains the aggregated and de-identified healthcare records of over 150 million patients from 107 healthcare institutions. We queried TNX for patients diagnosed with IDPG. Inclusion criteria included at least 1 year of follow up after IDPG diagnosis, and no prior history of MPC. Patients were split into those diagnosed with IDPG (n=81,163) at 35-55, 55-75, and 75+ years old. We identified control patients without IDPG (n=3,842,747) who met inclusion criteria, and performed 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching (PSM) on demographics, comorbidities, and measures of healthcare use. We analyzed 20 year incidence of MPC, penile amputation, radiation, chemotherapy, metastasis, and all-cause mortality. Risk ratios (RR) were calculated within TriNetX on Aug 8th, 2025. RESULTS: IDPG patients showed higher rates of mortality, MPC, amputation, and nodal metastasis. Radiation use was increased only in the 35–55 IDPG- group, while chemotherapy exposure was not significant between groups. Of note, patients who are IDPG+ had a 10-12X higher risk of MPC than the IDPG- group. Median follow-up (days, IQR) was shorter in IDPG patients than controls across all age groups: 35–55 (1648, 1901 vs. 1726, 2017), 55–75 (1606, 1769 vs. 1823, 1986), and 75+ (1145, 1200 vs. 1266, 1320). CONCLUSIONS: IDPGs were linked to higher risks of MPC, mortality, amputation, and nodal metastasis across all age groups, suggesting an independent and clinically significant effect beyond age related comorbidity. These results underscore the importance of early hygiene, timely diagnosis, and targeted management in this high-risk population. | | | --- | | |

title: PROGNOSTIC IMPACT OF RECURRENCE ON SURVIVAL IN SURGICALLY TREATED PENILE CANCER: A 12-YEAR RETROSPECTIVE COHORT (2013–2025)
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Adel Jorge El Rassi, Caio Vinícius Suartz, Alex Resende Allig, Bruno Ricardo Di Domenico, Arthur Degani Ottaiano, Luiz Guilherme Serrão Gimenez, Leopoldo Alves Ribeiro-Filho, Paulo Afonso De Carvalho, Fabio Pescarmona Gallucci, William Nahas, Mauricio Dener Cordeiro
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Penile squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) remains rare yet clinically aggressive, even with organ-sparing techniques and standardized inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND), survival is dictated mainly by post-treatment biology. Reliable outcome estimates are essential to refine risk stratification and guide adjuvant therapy. This study assessed recurrence, metastasis and cancer-specific mortality (CSM) in a surgical cohort, correlating clinicopathologic features and surgical approach with disease-free (DFS) and overall survival (OS). METHODS: Retrospective single-center analysis (2013–2025) of histologically confirmed SCC. Variables included pathologic (pT/pN), lymphovascular/perineural invasion (LVI/PNI), margins, histology, surgery type, ILND, adjuvant therapy, recurrence, metastasis, and vital status. DFS and OS were analyzed by Kaplan–Meier and log-rank tests, predictors by multivariable Cox regression modeling recurrence as a time-dependent covariate. Fine–Gray analysis addressed competing CSM events, and inverse-probability weighting corrected selection bias. RESULTS: Organ-sparing surgery predominated, as ILND nearly universal, reflecting a paradigm of oncologic thoroughness with functional preservation. Recurrence occurred in one-third of cases, being the primary determinant of mortality. In adjusted Cox models, recurrence was the strongest predictor of DFS and OS (HR 4.87; 95% CI 2.81–8.42; p<0.001), persisting after weighting and imputation. Advanced T stage (HR 2.35; p=0.003), positive margins (HR 1.78; p=0.02), LVI (HR 2.14; p=0.008), and PNI (HR 1.96; p=0.01) intensified risk, denoting synergism between aggressiveness and microscopic persistence. Penectomy type lost independent significance (HR 0.91; p=0.64), confirming oncologic equivalence under negative margins and proper nodal control. Competing-risks modeling reaffirmed recurrence as the main driver of CSM (sub-HR 5.22; 95% CI 2.71–10.06; p<0.001), with strong discrimination (Harrell’s C=0.83) and calibration. CONCLUSIONS: Relapse is the pivotal determinant of prognosis in penile SCC, surpassing surgical extent and baseline pathology. With optimized margins and nodal control, organ-sparing surgery remains oncologically sound. Next frontier lies in recurrence prevention through risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, vigilant surveillance and early salvage.

title: PURE TESTICULAR SEMINOMAS THAT RELAPSE WITH NONSEMINOMATOUS ELEMENTS: CLINICAL PATTERNS AND MANAGEMENT
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Pia Kraft, Ahmad Mousa, Ali Amiri, Lynn Anson-Catwright, Isabelle Tan, Philippe Bedard, Di Maria Jang, Rachel M. Glicksmann, Peter Chung, Padraig Warde, Susan Prendeville, Michael A. S. Jewett, Robert James Hamilton
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: A subset of testicular seminomas, though initially pure seminoma and without alpha fetoprotein (AFP) elevation, will relapse with nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCT) elements. This phenomenon, marked by nonseminomatous histology or AFP elevation, is rare but potentially clinically significant, and herein we report on our management and outcomes. METHODS: We included male patients who had pure seminoma at diagnosis with no AFP elevation and who developed subsequent relapse with either histologically confirmed nonseminoma or elevated AFP (>15ng/mL) between 1980-2024. Patient characteristics, disease stage, therapy details, perioperative outcomes, and follow-up data were collected from medical records. RESULTS: Pure seminoma was histologically confirmed in 2116 patients undergoing orchiectomy across all stages. In patients who met our criteria relapse occurred in 305 patients (14%) of which 22 patients (1%) had nonseminomatous elements and/or AFP >15 ng/mL. At diagnosis, laterality of the tumor was equal and rete testis invasion was positive in 55%. Clinical stage was I in 41%, II in 45%, and III in 14% of patients. Table 1 presents details stratified by clinical stage. Active surveillance was performed in 36% of patients, while 64% received treatment after orchiectomy. Primary treatment entailed radiotherapy in 36% and chemotherapy in 64% of patients. Median time to follow-up was 8 years (IQR 5-12). Relapse-free survival was 1 year (IQR 0.6-1.6 years). Most common relapse site was retroperitoneal in 50% of patients. 73% of patients had elevated AFP at relapse, median peak level of AFP was 30 ng/mL (IQR 20-132). Retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) was performed in 45% of patients of which 80% were post- chemotherapy. Nonseminomatous histology was found in 60% of RPLNDs and no RPLND specimen showed seminoma. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with pure seminoma who experience relapse, awareness of possible nonseminomatous elements is essential. At relapse, evaluating AFP levels and obtaining histological confirmation - particularly when clinical or radiological findings are atypical - is recommended. Although the presence of nonseminomatous components is rare, its recognition is critical, as management differs from that of seminoma relapse. | | | --- | | |

title: PRIMARY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION FOR CLINICAL STAGE II SEMINOMA: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS AGAINST ESTABLISHED PARADIGMS USING THE NATIONAL CANCER DATA BASE
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Josiah Low, John Musser
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: While primary retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for clinical stage II seminoma can reduce chemotherapy and radiation burden, no comparative analyses of this approach currently exist. We utilized a national oncologic data registry to perform the first comparative analysis of outcomes after primary retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for stage II seminoma. METHODS: Using the National Cancer Data Base, we identified patients with stage II germ cell tumors between 2004 to 2022. Cox regression was used for survival analyses. Primary analysis examined overall survival for patients with stage II seminoma. Sensitivity analysis after energy-balancing weighting was performed. Secondary analyses were performed for overall survival in patients who underwent primary retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for stage II germ cell tumor generally and for salvage-chemotherapy-free survival after primary retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for stage II seminoma. RESULTS: Primary analysis included 4,661 patients (median follow-up 6.8 years, IQR 3.6-10.5yr). Overall survival did not differ by primary treatment (versus chemotherapy – HR1.34, 95% CI 0.93-1.93, p=0.12; versus radiation – 1.02, 0.65-1.59, p=0.95). Sensitivity analysis results were similar. Secondary analysis showed increased mortality with nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (HR2.63, 1.07-6.49, p=0.036) and increased salvage chemotherapy with cN2 (HR3.88, 1.87-8.03, p=0.00027) and cN3 (HR6.03, 2.1-17.3, p=0.00083) compared to cN1. CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival after primary retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for stage II seminoma appears comparable to alternatives and possibly improved in favor of seminoma compared to nonseminomatous germ cell tumor. Risk of needing salvage chemotherapy increases with clinical disease extent.

title: PRIMARY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION (RPLND) FOR CLINICAL STAGE IIA/IIB SEMINOMA – UPDATED POPULATION-BASED RESULTS FROM SWEDISH AND NORWEGIAN TESTICULAR CANCER GROUP (SWENOTECA)
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Anna Thor, Bjarte Almås, Gabriella Cohn-Cedermark, Axel Gerdtsson, Anna Grenabo Bergdahl, Ingrid Glimelius, Dag Halvorsen, Andreas Habberstad, Hege Sagstuen Haugnes, Annika Hedlund, Martin Hellström, Anna K. Jansson, Berglind Johannsdottir, Ása Karlsdottir, Anders Kjellman, Carl Wilhelm Langberg, Signe Melsen Larsen, Helene Negaard, Olof Ståhl, Torgrim Tandstad
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Cure rates for metastatic testicular cancer are very high, but this comes at a cost for patients. While most achieve long-term remission, survivors face elevated risks of cardiovascular disease, secondary malignancies, and reduced life expectancy. To reduce the long-term morbidity associated with chemotherapy or radiotherapy for metastatic seminoma, primary RPLND has been explored as a treatment option for patients with low-volume disease. Several prospective and retrospective series have reported on the efficacy and safety of this approach, leading to recommendations in both the AUA and SWENOTECA guidelines. In May 2024, SWENOTECA published the results of the first prospective population-based cohort of 62 metastatic patients treated with primary RPLND. Herein we present data for overall 135 patients treated with primary RPLND for presumed low-volume metastatic seminoma. METHODS: This is a population-based prospective cohort of 135 patients with presumed metastatic seminoma clinical stage (CS) IIA/IIB with a maximum of two suspected malignant lymph nodes with a maximum diameter of 3 cm. Patients were operated with primary RPLND from 2019 to 2025 at five tertiary hospitals in Sweden and Norway. RESULTS: Median age at RPLND was 44 years (IQR: 36-51). Median time of follow-up was 25 months (IQR: 12-39). Overall, 79 patients (59%) were included after relapse in former CS I, of whom 24 (19%) had received prior adjuvant chemotherapy. At time of RPLND, 97 patients (72%) had CS IIA, and 38 patients (28%) had CS IIB. In total, 98% had a prior FDG-PET, of whom 95% had a positive result. Robot-assisted laparoscopic RPLND was performed in 106 patients (79%). 40% were right sided unilateral template, 58% left sided unilateral template, and 2% bilateral RPLND. Median operating time was 158 min (IQR: 116-218), median blood loss 50 ml (IQR:20-100) and intraoperative complications occurred in 4 patients (3%). Post-operative complications Clavien-Dindo ≥ III occurred in 6 patients (4.4%), chylous ascites requiring drainage was the most common event. Median hospital stay was 2 nights (IQR: 2-4). 89% reported preserved ejaculation after RPLND (data available in 101 patients). Metastatic seminoma was confirmed in 131 patients (97%), one patient had a teratoma (0.7%), one patient had a non-seminoma other than teratoma (0.7%), one patient had necrosis/fibrosis and one patient had a glandular infection (pN0 1.5%). Median lymph node yield was 11 (IQR: 7-16), with a median of 1 malignant node (IQR: 1-2), and median largest metastasis diameter 20 mm (IQR:15-25). 58 patients (43%) received post-RPLND adjuvant chemotherapy, most one cycle of BEP. Post-RPLND relapse occurred in 16 patients (12%), 5 of those were outfield. Median time to relapse was 12 months (IQR: 7-18). Progression free survival at 25 months was 90% (95% CI 0.82-0.94) and overall survival was 100%. CONCLUSIONS: This approach to treat selected patients with surgery instead of conventional chemotherapy or radiation, still appears safe and effective. The relapse rate after RPLND remains low. The FDG-PET is a useful tool for selecting seminoma patients for surgery, thereby avoiding higher rates of benign outcomes.

title: OUTCOMES OF PRIMARY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION FOR CLINICAL STAGE IIB TESTICULAR SEMINOMA: A BINATIONAL RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Alireza Ghoreifi, Julian Heidenreich, Muhannad Alsyouf, David Pfister, Pia Paffenholz, Anne Schuckman, Axel Heidenreich, Siamak Daneshmand
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) has been established as a first-line treatment for seminoma with small volume retroperitoneal metastases, aiming to reduce long-term toxicity from chemotherapy and radiotherapy. However, its role in clinical stage IIB disease remains unclear. This study evaluates the outcomes of primary RPLND in stage IIB seminoma. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we included consecutive patients who underwent primary RPLND with curative intent for clinical stage IIB seminoma, defined as a retroperitoneal lymph node size of 2 to 5 cm on preoperative imaging, at two large referral centers in the United States and Germany between 2016 and 2025. Those with insufficient clinical data were excluded. Perioperative and oncological outcomes of the patients were assessed. RESULTS: Forty patients with a median age of 35 years were included. The median preoperative mass size was 2.5 cm (range 2 – 4.5). A midline abdominal approach was used for all surgeries. Median operative time and blood loss were 154 minutes and 100 ml, respectively. A median of 21 nodes was removed, and final pathology revealed pN0, pN1, pN2, pN3 in 2 (5%), 1 (2.5%), 32 (80%), and 5 (12.5%) cases, respectively (Table). Complications within 90 days were observed in seven patients (17.5%), six of which were grade III. None of the patients received adjuvant chemotherapy. With a median follow-up of 27 (IQR 17-39) months, 9 patients (22.5%) experienced recurrence (5 in-field and 4 outfield). Of these, five were pN2 and four pN3; six received chemotherapy and three underwent additional surgery. Median time to recurrence was 10 months. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated 2-year recurrence-free and overall survival rates at 78% and 100%, respectively. Recurrence-free survival was significantly lower in patients with pN3 disease ( Figure). CONCLUSIONS: RPLND can be considered as a first-line treatment for stage IIB testicular seminoma, offering low morbidity and favorable intermediate-term oncological outcomes if performed in specialized centers by expert surgeons. Larger nodal disease is not suitable for surgical management due to the increased recurrence risk. | | | --- | | |

title: POST-CHEMOTHERAPY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION FOR PATIENTS WITH METASTATIC PURE SEMINOMA
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Viranda H. Jayalath, Samuel L. Gold, Nicole Liso, Brandon Williams, Samuel A. Funt, Darren R. Feldman, Joel Sheinfeld, Richard S. Matulewicz
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (pcRPLND) for metastatic testicular seminoma is reserved for highly select cases and can be associated with significant morbidity. We report contemporary outcomes of pcRPLND in patients with metastatic pure seminoma with the goal of better defining patient selection for surgery and exploring gaps in diagnostic staging. METHODS: Patients who underwent pcRPLND after ≥1-line of chemotherapy for metastatic pure seminoma at our institution between 2000-2024 were included. Clinicopathologic, radiographic, perioperative, oncologic, and survival outcomes are reported. RESULTS: 52 patients underwent pcRPLND for metastatic pure seminoma during the study period. Most patients (67%) received ≥2 lines of chemotherapy prior to surgery. Eight patients (15%) harbored residual viable seminoma at pcRPLND, 38% and 6% following first-line and ≥2-lines of chemotherapy, respectively (Figure). None of the patients that received high-dose chemotherapy (TI-CE) had viable disease at surgery. Over a median follow up of 50-months, 5 (10%) patients relapsed after pcRPLND, all of whom had viable residual seminoma at pcRPLND. Of the 8 patients with residual seminoma at pcRPLND, 2 were cured with pcRPLND alone, 3 with pcRPLND plus additional chemotherapy, and 3 died from progressive disease. CONCLUSIONS: The risk of finding viable residual seminoma at pcRPLND varied based on prior chemotherapy received. These data underscore the importance of careful patient selection given the competing risks of morbidity associated with pcRPLND, the high likelihood of cure with high-dose chemotherapy, and the need for better diagnostics to guide surgical decision-making in this setting. | | | --- | | |

title: ROBOTIC VERSUS OPEN POST-CHEMOTHERAPY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION: A PROPENSITY SCORE MATCHED STUDY ACROSS ELEVEN ACADEMIC MEDICAL CENTERS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Julian Chavarriaga, Alireza Ghoreifi, Eshetu G. Atenafu, Ahmad Mousa, Lynn Anson-Cartwright, Sanchit Kaushal, Farshad Sheybaee, Anirban P. Mitra, Ashish Khanna, Amitabh Singh, Sol Moon, Ahmed Saeed Goolam, Ryan Chuang, Jordan Rich, Fady Baky, Mathew Ho, Jacob Roberts, Inderbir Gill, Reza Mehrazin, John Sfakianos, James Porter, Soroush Rais-Bahrami, Aditya Bagrodia, Nariman Ahmadi, Scott Eggener, Sudhir Rawal, John F. Ward
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (PC-RPLND) is crucial in testicular cancer treatment, as one-third of patients have residual masses post-chemotherapy. While the open approach remains the gold standard, it is associated with higher morbidity. Minimally invasive approaches like robotic PC-RPLND aim to reduce morbidity, and increasingly, is being performed at academic centres due to the potential for lower blood loss, shorter length of stay, and accelerated recovery. Our objective was to compare perioperative and survival outcomes of patients undergoing robotic versus open post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (PC-RPLND) for testicular cancer. METHODS: Analyzing data from patients who underwent PC-RPLND at eleven academic centres between 1990-2023, we used propensity score matching (PSM) to create a 1:1 (open-RPLND: robotic-RPLND) matched cohort. The primary endpoint was time to relapse. Secondary endpoints included operative time, length of stay, estimated blood loss, and surgical complications. Relapse free survival rates were calculated using the Kaplan-Meier methodology, and log-rank tests to compare perioperative outcomes between robotic vs. open PC-RPLND. RESULTS: A total of 134 robotic cases were propensity score matched to 134 open cases. At a median follow-up of 2.2 years, estimated relapse-free survival at 3 years was similar between robotic and open PC-RPLND (92.8% vs. 88.5%, p=0.18). Relapse occurred in 5.2% (robotic) vs. 12.3% (open), with most relapses occurring within the first year . Robotic PC-RPLND was associated with lower blood loss, shorter operative time and hospital stay, and fewer complications (16.4% vs. 32.1%), including a 0% rate of ileus compared to 12.7% in the open group. Lymph node yield and rates of viable tumor were comparable between approaches. The main limitation of this study was its retrospective nature. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first multicenter study to compare open versus robotic PC-RPLND using a PSM system. With appropriate patient selection and surgical experience at academic centers specializing in testicular cancer care, robotic PC-RPLND offers low morbidity and improved perioperative outcomes while maintaining the same oncological outcomes, compared to the open approach.

title: ROBOTIC-ASSISTED RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION FOR METASTATIC TESTICULAR MALIGNANCIES – A 9-YEAR COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE OUTCOMES AND LEARNING CURVE
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Henry YC. Pan, Clancy J. Mulholland, Weiwei Shi, Marc A. Furrer, Gal Rinott Mizrahi, Ciara Conduit, Ben Tran, Nathan Lawrentschuk, Benjamin C. Thomas
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Robotic-assisted retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RA-RPLND) is an emerging minimally-invasive alternative for treating and staging metastatic testicular malignancies. Whilst open RPLND remains the standard-of-care, global uptake of RA-RPLND has expanded. We report peri-operative outcomes of RA-RPLNDs by a single, fellowship-trained uro-oncologist over 9 years, with a focus on learning curve trends. METHODS: A prospective database for RA-RPLNDs performed between August 2016-2025 was analysed. Patients with retroperitoneal metastatic testicular tumours undergoing primary or post-chemotherapy resections were included. All cases used a transperitoneal robotic-assisted approach. Patients were stratified into 4 sequential cohorts of 20 cases each. Cohort comparisons used Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn’s post-hoc test. Predictors of outcomes were evaluated with generalised linear models. RESULTS: Of 80 consecutive RA-RPLND patients; 33 (41%) underwent primary and 47 (59%) post-chemotherapy RA-RPLND. Median operative time (OT) was 180 minutes (IQR 150-210), estimated blood loss (EBL) was 100 ml (IQR 50-150) and median hospital length of stay (LOS) was 1 night (1-7). Six high-grade (33) Clavien-Dindo complications were observed, 2 each in cohorts 2-4. Cohort analyses showed significant differences for template performed (p=0.01), OT (p=0.001) and lymph node (LN) yield (p0.001), but no difference in EBL (p=0.074), LOS (p=0.076) or complications (p=0.59). OT increased in later cohorts, with subset analysis showing an increase of 40 and 50 minutes in cohort 2 and 4 respectively (p=0.012, p=0.002), reflecting progressive shift in complexity and paralleled by proportion of bilateral templates and LN yield. On multivariate regression, bilateral template dissection independently predicted OT (p0.001), longer LOS (p0.001), greater EBL (p0.001) and higher LN yield (p=0.026). Cohort 4 showed longer OT (p=0.026) and higher LN yield (p 0.027-0.001), with unchanged EBL and LOS. Integrating peri-operative variables identified complications and open conversion to be independently associated with longer LOS (p=0.039, p0.001), while concomitant procedures prolonged operative time (p=0.033). CONCLUSIONS: This is the largest reported single-surgeon series of RA-RPLND for metastatic testicular cancer. Outcomes were most affected by surgical template and intra-operative factors rather than case sequence. These findings support the feasibility and oncological safety of RA-RPLND in high-volume hands, while underscoring the importance of case selection and formal training in this heterogenous and technically demanding procedure.

title: ROBOTIC PRIMARY AND POST-CHEMOTHERAPY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION FOR TESTICULAR CANCER: SINGLE INSTITUTION EXPERIENCE
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Madelyn A. Flitcroft, Drew Price, Arjun Sivaraman
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Robotic retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to open surgery for testicular cancer, but outcomes in post-chemotherapy patients remain incompletely characterized. We report our institutional experience evaluating peri-operative and early oncologic outcomes of robotic RPLND in both pre- and post-chemotherapy settings. METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of all patients undergoing robotic RPLND for testis cancer between 2015 and 2025 at a single academic institution. Demographic, operative, and pathologic variables were analyzed. Perioperative outcomes were compared between primary RPLND and post-chemotherapy RPLND cohorts. RESULTS: A total of 51 patients underwent robotic RPLND, including 25 post-chemotherapy and 26 primary RPLND cases. Median operative time was 410 minutes (IQR 305–514) for post-chemotherapy and 309 minutes (IQR 240–433) for primary cases. Median estimated blood loss was 200 ml (IQR 100–300) and 125 ml (IQR 75–250), respectively. Clavien I–II complications occurred in 2 post-chemotherapy (8%) and 2 primary RPLND (8%) patients. Clavien III or greater complications did not occur in either group. Conversion to open occurred in 0 post-chemotherapy and 1 primary RPLND case. Median lymph node yield was 31 (IQR 25–55) for post-chemotherapy and 29 (IQR 21–44) for primary RPLNDs. No in-field recurrences were observed in either cohort. CONCLUSIONS: Robotic RPLND is feasible and safe in both primary and post-chemotherapy settings, achieving comparable node yields and low morbidity. Despite longer operative times in post-chemotherapy patients, overall outcomes and early oncologic control were favorable. These findings support the broader adoption of robotic RPLND in post-chemotherapy setting at experienced centers.

title: BEYOND A SIMPLE PROCEDURE: MULTICENTER EVALUATION OF SURGICAL PRACTICES IN RADICAL ORCHIECTOMY FOR TESTICULAR GERM CELL TUMORS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Massimiliano Raffo, Fausto Negri, Sebastiano Nazzani, Carlo Silvani, Elio Mazzone, Sofia Giudici, Paolo Dell’Oglio, Luca Boeri, Federica Passarelli, Ludovico M. Basadonna, Giuseppe Garofano, Marco Paciotti, Giovanni Lughezzani, Andrea Triggiani, Giuseppe Fallara, Matteo Ferro, Alberto Briganti, Andrea Salonia, Marco Bandini
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Radical orchiectomy (RO) is the cornerstone and curative first-line treatment for testicular germ cell tumors (TGCT). Although often considered a straightforward procedure, it plays a crucial role in diagnosis, staging, and oncologic outcomes. Yet, data on surgical technique, perioperative variables, and short-term outcomes remain limited and mostly from single-center studies. A clearer understanding of perioperative practice across institutions is needed to identify variability and improve surgical standards. This study aimed to analyze perioperative and surgical outcomes of patients undergoing RO. METHODS: Data from 305 patients who underwent RO for TGCT between 2020 and 2024 across six academic institutions were retrospectively analyzed. Preoperative variables included Eastern cooperative oncology group (ECOG) performance status, serum tumor markers, hormonal profile, scrotal ultrasound (US), body CT scan, and sperm cryopreservation status. Perioperative parameters such as operative time, testicular prosthesis implantation, and drain placement were also collected. Postoperative recovery and complications were assessed according to the Clavien–Dindo classification, and surgical margin status was reported in relation to pathological tumor (pT) stage. Descriptive statistics were applied. RESULTS: The median (IQR) age was 35 (29-43) years. Most patients had an ECOG performance status of 0 (96.7%), while 5 (1.6%) patients had a status of 1, 2 (0.7%) had 2, and 1 (0.3%) had 3. Preoperatively, all serum tumor markers (LDH, β-hCG and AFP) were assessed in 219 (71.8%) patients, while hormonal profiling (total testosterone, LH, FSH) was performed in 57 (18.7%) patients. Scrotal US was performed in 99.7% of case, while preoperative body CT scan in 83%. Sperm cryopreservation was utilized in 192 (63%) patients. The median operative time was 64 (46-86) minutes. A testicular prosthesis was implanted in 42% of cases, and a surgical drain was placed in 2.3%. Postoperative complications occurred in 7 (2.3%) patients, all Clavien–Dindo grade I. Overall complication rates did not differ between patients with and without drain placement (2.3%% vs 2.1%) or prosthesis implantation (0.8% vs. 3.5%), respectively. Operative time was significantly longer with prosthesis implantation (70 \[50-94\] vs 60 \[44-79\] minutes, p=0.04). Positive surgical margins were reported in 5 (2.6%) patients, corresponding to pT1 in 1.2% cases, pT2 in 0.9%, and pT3 in 40% (p=0.008). CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative patients work-up is usually comprising serum markers, US, and CT scan assessment, but frequently lacks hormonal screening and cryopreservation, although representing two relevant aspects in patients with TGCT. RO is usually associated with few postoperative complications. Margin positivity is relatively rare overall but appear to be more frequent in higher pathological stages.

title: DELAYED ORCHIECTOMY AND RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION PATHOLOGY AFTER CHEMOTHERAPY: CORRELATION AND PROGNOSTIC IMPACT IN ADVANCED GERM CELL TUMORS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Vinay Sagar, Tejas Medapalli, Karm Ghei, Jackson F. Harmon, Austen Clark, Serkan Karakus, Eric Umbreit
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In patients with advanced nonseminomatous germ cell tumors (NSGCT), orchiectomy (OE) is often delayed when urgent chemotherapy is required. The prognostic value of post-chemotherapy OE pathology versus retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) findings remains uncertain. We examined the histopathologic concordance between OE and RPLND specimens and evaluated the prognostic value of each site in relation to relapse-free (RFS) and overall survival (OS). METHODS: Among 807 NSGCT patients treated between 2000 and 2025, 87 who underwent post-chemotherapy OE and/or RPLND were analyzed. Pathology was categorized as necrosis/fibrosis, teratoma, or viable GCT. Combined-pathology risk was defined by the most aggressive histology. RFS and OS were estimated by Kaplan-Meier at 24 and 60 months with log-rank testing. Univariable and multivariable Cox models included RPLND pathology, combined pathology risk, International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group (IGCCCG) risk group, and clinical stage. Serum AFP and β-hCG levels (pre- and post-chemotherapy) were analyzed for associations with pathology and outcomes. RESULTS: Median age was 28.0 years; 83.9% had Stage III disease and 49.4% were IGCCCG poor risk. OE pathology showed no viable tumor in 57.5%, teratoma in 27.6%, and viable GCT in 13.8%; corresponding RPLND results were 35.6%, 39.1%, and 12.6%. Among 76 paired cases, 36.8% were discordant: viable GCT appeared only in OE in 4 patients and only in RPLND in 8, indicating either site may harbor residual malignancy. Pre-chemotherapy AFP/β-hCG elevation occurred in 89.1% of patients and correlated with higher clinical stage and more aggressive histology. Marker elevation persisted in 40% with viable GCT, 8.6% with teratoma, and 13.5% with necrosis., Patients with discordant pathology had twice the rate of persistent marker elevation (17.6% vs 8.7%). Discordance was not associated with OS (p=0.354) or RFS (p=0.433). RPLND pathology was the strongest prognostic factor: patients with viable tumor had 24- and 60-month OS of 77.8% and 51.9%, compared with 96.8% and 92.7% for teratoma and 100.0% and 89.4% for necrosis. In multivariable analysis, RPLND pathology independently predicted OS (HR 8.51, p=0.034) and RFS (HR 2.59, p=0.030), while combined-pathology risk and marker normalization were not significant. CONCLUSIONS: Pathologic discordance between post-chemotherapy OE and RPLND is common, but only RPLND pathology predicts survival. These findings emphasize the dominant prognostic value of RPLND pathology and the continued importance of performing both procedures for complete disease assessment and clearance.

title: THE ROLE OF DELAYED ORCHIECTOMY FOLLOWING CHEMOTHERAPY FOR METASTATIC GERM CELL TUMOURS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Ahmad Mousa, James Hayes, Ali Amiri, Lynn Anson-Cartwright, Eshetu G. Atenafu, Philippe Bedard, Di Maria Jiang, Rachel Glicksman, Peter Chung, Padraig Warde, Martin O'Malley, Susan Prendeville, Robert James Hamilton
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In patients with testicular germ cell tumors (TGCT) presenting with high-volume or site-critical metastases, upfront chemotherapy is often initiated to expedite systemic control, while orchiectomy is deferred. However, limited data exist characterizing testicular pathology in this context or identifying predictors of residual disease. This study aims to describe our institutional experience with post-chemotherapy orchiectomy and to determine clinical and radiologic factors associated with the absence of residual disease. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all patients with metastatic TGCT who underwent post-chemotherapy orchiectomy at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre between 1992 – 2025. Clinical, radiologic, and pathologic features were compared between patients with benign versus viable testicular pathology. Kaplan–Meier analysis was used to estimate relapse-free and cancer-specific survival (RFS and CSS), and logistic regression was used to identify predictors of viable disease. RESULTS: A total of 82 patients underwent post-chemotherapy orchiectomy, with a median follow-up of 3.7 years. Teratoma was identified in 36 cases (44%), viable seminoma identified in only 2 patients (2.4%) - both within teratoma-containing specimens. At 5 years, RFS and CSS were 92.2% and 94.5% for patients with benign pathology, compared to 64.9% and 81.6% for those with viable disease (log-rank p<0.001 and p=0.066, respectively). Specific orchiectomy histology was not significantly associated with CSS (log-rank p=0.2).On univariate analysis, predictors of viable disease included younger age, palpable testicular mass, poor-risk IGCCCG classification, receipt of second-line chemotherapy, adverse post-chemotherapy ultrasound features (vascularity and/or coarse calcifications), and concurrent extragonadal surgery for post-chemotherapy residual masses. Viable testicular pathology was also associated with viable disease at retroperitoneal lymph node dissection. Notably, no viable disease was identified in patients with post-chemotherapy ultrasound demonstrating normal or “burnt-out” findings, or in those with residual testicular masses <1 cm. CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with favorable clinical and radiographic features, the risk of viable TGCT following chemotherapy is low. These findings support the consideration of surveillance or partial orchiectomy in lieu of routine radical orchiectomy in selected patients where testicular preservation is desired. Prospective validation is warranted.

title: CIRCULATING TUMOR DNA PERFORMANCE IN PRIMARY RETROPERITONEAL LYMPH NODE DISSECTION: A STAGE-BASED ANALYSIS
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Parth Thakker, Connor Drake, Amy Tennant, Timothy Masterson, Clint Cary
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Novel biomarkers appear to have use in the surveillance and treatment monitoring of testicular germ cell tumors (GCT). Recently, ctDNA has been demonstrated to detect GCT in both primary and post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND), however the association of ctDNA levels with tumor burden has not yet been determined. Herein, we sought to determine the utility of ctDNA for predicting GCT on P-RPLND by comparing patients’ RPLND histology with their pre-operative ctDNA status in those with clinical stage (CS) 1 and 2 disease. Furthermore, we determined the association between ctDNA levels and clinical stage at RPLND. METHODS: Patients undergoing primary (P-RPLND) from 2023 to 2025 had prospectively collected plasma ctDNA assay (SignateraTM, Natera Inc.) Patients were stratified by CS based on pre-operative CT imaging and serum tumor markers. The association between ctDNA positivity and P-RPLND histology was assessed. Test statistics were calculated for ctDNA to detect active cancer on RPLND. Additionally, the association between ctDNA levels and CS as a surrogate for disease burden was determined using linear regression analysis. RESULTS: 64 patients undergoing P-RPLND had pre-operative ctDNA collection with a median age of 37 (IQR:29-42). Plasma was collected on average, 8 days pre-operatively. 10 (16%) patients underwent P-RPLND for CS 1 and 54 (84%) for CS 2 disease. ctDNA was positive in 47 (73%) patients in the entire cohort. In the CS I group, 7 patients had a (-) ctDNA all of which had a negative P-RPLND. Of the 54 CS 2 patients, 44 (81%) had a (+) ctDNA. No false positives were found in this cohort. The SN, SP, PPV, and NPV in the CS 1 cohort were 100%, 78%, 33%, and 100% and in CS 2 were 88%, 100%, 100%, and 40%, respectively. Additionally, ctDNA level does not appear to correlate to disease volume at this juncture (r2=0, p=0.948). CONCLUSIONS: CtDNA may have use in predicting retroperitoneal histology on P-RPLND. In CS 1 disease a negative test appears to be correlated with an absence of disease. In CS 2 disease, no false positives were found. ctDNA appears to be a binary test for detecting disease in the retroperitoneum. | | | --- | | |

title: PERFORMANCE OF CIRCULATING TUMOR DNA AS A BIOMARKER IN TESTICULAR SEMINOMA AND NON-SEMINOMATOUS GERM CELL TUMOR
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Parth Thakker, Connor Drake, Amy Tennant, Timothy Masterson, Clint Cary
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Serum tumor markers have been the cornerstone in the detection and surveillance of testicular germ cell tumors (GCT). However, the sensitivity of specificity of STM for detecting GCT is poor. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has shown promise in the detection of GCT in both primary and post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND). Herein, we sought to determine the utility of ctDNA for predicting active GCT on P-RPLND by comparing patients’ RPLND histology with their pre-operative ctDNA status in those with seminoma and non-seminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCT). METHODS: Patients undergoing primary (P-RPLND) from 2023 to 2025 had prospectively collected plasma ctDNA assay (SignateraTM, Natera Inc.) Patients were stratified to seminoma or NSGCT based on orchiectomy and serum tumor markers. The association between ctDNA positivity and P-RPLND histology was assessed. Sensitivity (SN), specificity (SP), and positive (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV) were calculated for ctDNA to detect seminoma or NSGCT on RPLND. RESULTS: 64 patients undergoing P-RPLND had pre-operative ctDNA collection. Plasma was collected on average, 8 days pre-operatively. 27 (42%) patients underwent P-RPLND for seminoma and 37 (58%) for NSGCT. ctDNA was positive in 47 (73%) patients in the entire cohort. Of seminoma patients, 16 had CS 2A and 11 had CS 2B disease. 24 (89%) seminoma patients had a (+) ctDNA. All seminoma patients had GCT present on P-RPLND. Of NSGCT patients, 10 had CS 1, 21 had CS 2A and 6 had CS 2B disease. 23 (62%) NSGCT patients had a (+) ctDNA. 2 patients in the NSGCT cohort had (+) ctDNA and negative RPLND. Of these, 1 patient had a persistently elevated ctDNA post-operatively, and had a lung recurrence. The second patient had a continually rising ctDNA test with negative surveillance imaging at 9 months. The SN, SP, PPV, and NPV in the NSGCT cohort were 88%, 85%, 91%, and 79%, respectively for predicting GCT. For the seminoma cohort these were 89%, undefined, 100%, and 0%. The undefined SP and 0% NPV in the seminoma group were due to the lack of patients with negative RPLND. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study evaluating performance of ctDNA in relation to RPLND histology, when stratified by seminoma or NSGCT. These findings suggest that ctDNA may be a useful tool in predicting retroperitoneal histology. Persistently positive ctDNA after RPLND may be indicative of disease outside of the retroperitoneum.

title: TUMOR-INFORMED CIRCULATING TUMOR DNA FOR RELAPSE DETECTION IN CLINICAL STAGE I TESTICULAR CANCER
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Towfik Sebai, Parth U. Thakker, Timothy A. Masterson, Clint Cary, Nabil Adra
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Serum tumor markers (STM) are integral to testicular cancer management but lack sensitivity for early relapse detection. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may enhance surveillance accuracy. To determine the role of ctDNA in the surveillance protocols, we evaluated its performance for the detection of relapse in patients with clinical stage (CS) I disease on surveillance. METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of patients with CS I testicular cancer from 2019 to 2025 who underwent ctDNA testing during surveillance. All tests were performed during surveillance, post-orchiectomy, and at 3 months intervals onwards. Sensitivity (SN), specificity (SP), positive (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were calculated for ctDNA to detect relapse, which was defined as radiographic progression or STM elevation. The relative risk and 95% confidence interval (CI) of relapse in ctDNA-positive versus ctDNA-negative patients was calculated. RESULTS: We included a total of 59 patients with CS I testicular cancer, of whom 30 experienced relapse during surveillance. A total of 80 ctDNA assays were performed, comprising 26 positive and 54 negative results; 36 patients (61%) had nonseminomas, 22 (37%) had seminomas, and 1 (2%) had a Sertoli cell tumor in their orchiectomy specimen. Median follow-up was 11 months (interquartile range 4-20). Of the 26 ctDNA-positive results, 24 (92%) were true positives and 2 (8%) were false positives. One false-positive patient had a repeat ctDNA test 3 months later that returned negative and remained relapse-free after 9 months of follow-up. The other underwent retroperitoneal lymph node dissection, which revealed no positive nodes, and was followed for 1 month before being lost to follow-up. Of the 54 ctDNA-negative results, 50 (93%) were true negatives and 4 (7%) were false negatives. All false negatives were in retroperitoneal relapses and included two pure seminomas (1.7 cm and 3.3 cm), one 4.2 cm pure embryonal carcinoma, and one 4.8 cm pure teratoma. The results corresponded to a SN, SP, PPV, and NPV of 86%, 96%, 92%, and 93%, respectively. The relative risk of relapse in ctDNA-positive versus ctDNA-negative patients was 12.5 (95% CI, 4.8-32.2; p<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Tumor-informed ctDNA demonstrated high PPV and good SN for detecting relapse in patients on surveillance for CS 1 testicular cancer. ctDNA positivity was strongly associated with disease relapse, supporting its potential role as an adjunct biomarker to traditional STM.

title: PROSPECTIVE EVALUATION OF THE PERFORMANCE OF MIR371 TEST UNDER REAL-LIFE CONDITIONS FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF TESTICULAR GERM CELL CANCER
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Carolina D'elia, Giovanni Mazzucato, Margherita Palermo, Christine Mian, Christine Schwienbacher, Armin Pycha, Salvatore M. Palermo, Isabel M. Heidegger, Emanuela Trenti
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Testicular germ cell tumour (GCT) has a cure rate exceeding 90% in clinical stages (CS) I -II and approximately 75% in CS III. Cornerstones of clinical management are surgery, imaging and measurement of the serum tumour markers such as alpha fetoprotein (AFP), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-HCG) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). However, clinical utility of these tumour markers is limited due to their low sensitivity. Recently, miRNA-371a-3p (M371) has has emerged as promising biomarker in the diagnosis of GCT by performing better than conventional markers. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of M371-Test under real-life clinical conditions in comparison with the classical markers AFP, beta-HCG and LDH in patients with suspected GCT. Furthermore, the study aimed to identify a correlation between tumour size and preoperative value of M371. A control group of healthy individuals was also included to verify the reliability and specificity of the results. METHODS: 99 M371 tests were performed from March 2021 to October 2025 and were prospectively included in this study. Of these, 79 tests were conducted in patients with clinical suspicion of GCT (median age: 38 years). In the remaining 20 cases the test was performed in healthy patients, used as control group. Results of M371, AFP, beta -HCG, LDH of the patients with suspicion of GCT were compared with the histology. Results of Mi371, AFP, beta-HCG, LDH of control group were compared to assess their performance in a healthy population. A relative quantification (RQ) cut-off value of >5, according to the manufacturer’s instructions, was used to calculate sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values RESULTS: M371 showed a sensitivity of 91.8% and a specificity of 90.0%, outperforming AFP (20.4%/96.7%), LDH (40.8%/93.3%), and β-hCG (44.9%/100%) in terms of sensitivity. The positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were 93.7% and 87.1%, respectively. When patients were stratified by histological subtype, miR-371 sensitivity was 89.6% for seminomas and 95.0% for non-seminomas; moreover, after excluding teratoma cases, sensitivity reached 100% in the non-seminomatous subgroup. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.93 (95% CI 0.87–0.99; p<0.001). The optimal cut-off value, determined by the Youden index and anchored to the nearest observed value in the dataset, was 5.3, corresponding to a sensitivity of 89.8% and a specificity of 93.3%. Finally, correlation analysis between serum miR-371 concentrations and tumor diameter revealed a moderate positive association (Spearman’s ρ=0.57), indicating that higher miR-371 levels are associated with larger tumor size. CONCLUSIONS: The M371 test demonstrated good diagnostic performance under real-world clinical conditions. It maintained high sensitivity even in patients with small testicular tumors, supporting its potential role as a new standard biomarker for GCT diagnosis.

title: EVALUATION OF MIRNA-371A-3P (MIR371A) ASSAY TO PREDICT FINAL PATHOHISTOLOGY IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING PRIMARY NERVE-SPARING RETROPERITONEAL LYMPHADENECTOMY (NSRPLND) FOR STAGE IIA/B SEMINOMAS AND NON-SEMINOMAS (NSGCT)
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Olivia Steenbock, David Pfister, Julian Heidenreich, Constantin Rieger, Richard Weiten, Axel Heidenreich
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: 20-30% of patients with marker negative clinical stage IIA/B seminomas and nonseminomas might harbor non-malignant histologies. MiR371a is thought to represent a new biomarker with diagnostic and predictive properties. It was the purpose of our study to evaluate the predictive accuracy of this new biomarker to identify the presence or absence of lymph node metastases in clinical stage IIA/B TGCT. METHODS: In a cohort of 91 consecutive patients with marker negative CS IIA/B TGCT (n=45 seminoma, n=46 nonseminoma) serum concentration of miR371 was assessed one day before nsRPLND. Positive or negative findings were correlated with lymph node pathology. Blood specimens were drawn on the day prior to surgery and processed according to the manufacturer’s protocol (mirdetect, Bremerhaven, Germany). In brief, cubital vein blood was placed on ice and processed within 30 minutes for extraction of miR371a. The Maxwell RSC with the Maxwell® RSC MiRNA Plasma and Serum Kits (Promega GmBH, Walldorf, Germany) was used here to extract and purify the miRNA. The extracted miR371a waas transcribed into cDNA using cDNA Solution, Reverse Transcriptase and RNase Inhibitor. Subsequently, this cDNA was amplified. Using qPCR (Real Time-quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction), the miR371a was quantified using Roche Lightcycler 480 II (Roche Diagnostics, Rotkreuz, Switzerland). Using the Lightcycler software, the median Cp (CP=Crossing Points) of the triplicates is calculated and converted into a RQ value (RQ=Relative Frequency), which indicates whether the sample is positive or negative. RESULTS: Histology revealed metastatic GCT in 79/91 (87%) patients. miR371a was positive in 66/71 (93%) patients with metastases. miR371a negative lymph node metastases included teratoma in 2, embryonal carcinoma in 2 and seminoma in 1 patient. Histology revealed no malignancy in 12 patients and all patients showed negative miR371a findings. Sensitivity and specificity for the whole cohort were 95% and 100%, respectively; positive predictive value (PPV) was 91% and negative predictive value (NPV) was 78%. For the seminoma cohort, sensitivity and specificity were 98% and 100%, PPV and NPV were 100% and 98%. For nonseminomas, sensitivity and specificity were 90% and 100%, PPV and NPV were 100% and 50%. CONCLUSIONS: Based on the available data, miR371a represents a highly reliable personalized tumor marker to predict the presence of small volume retroperitoneal lymph node metastases in marker negative TGCT. miR371 has to greatest potential in seminomas were we use miR371 to stratify patients for RPLND versus active surveillace. For nonseminomas miR371 is useful for non-teratomatous tumors and it is not reliable for teratomas and malignant somatic transformation.

title: DYNAMICS OF CIRCULATING MIR-371A-3P LEVELS BEFORE AND AFTER BEP CHEMOTHERAPY IN PATIENTS WITH METASTATIC SEMINOMA AND NON-SEMINOMATOUS GERM CELL TUMOR
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Olivia Steenbock, Felix Seelemeyer, Roberto Pappesch, David Pfister, Axel Heidenreich
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: MiR-371a-3p (miRNA-371) is a promising biomarker for germ cell tumors. Its expression in blood may provide a non-invasive method for monitoring disease activity and treatment response. The aim of this study was to analyze miRNA-371 levels before and after BEP chemotherapy (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) in patients with metastatic seminoma and non-seminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCT). METHODS: A retrospective analysis of miR-371a-3p expression was performed in patients who received systemic PEB chemotherapy between 2022 and 2025. miRNA expression levels were quantified from serum samples using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Crossing point (Cp) values were determined for each sample and converted into relative quantification (RQ) values using the ΔΔCp method. The dynamics of miRNA-371 levels and their correlation with clinical response were evaluated. RQ levels <5 were considered negative, and >10 were considered positive. RESULTS: MiRNA-371 levels were significantly higher before chemotherapy than after treatment (median 138.6 vs 4.19; p=0.0010) in patients with seminoma. In 7 of 11 patients, the levels dropped to undetectable, and in two patients to the indeterminate range. Two patients showed persistently positive miRNA-371 levels after chemotherapy despite radiological regression; they developed early relapse. In patients with intermediate measurements during chemotherapy (e. g. 2 of 3 cycles), a statistical significant (p=0.0078) decrease was also observed, although most values remained positive (median 445.5 vs 11.71). In the NSGCT cohort, data were available from before treatment and the admission day of the third treatment cycle. miR-371a-3p levels declined significantly (n=9, p=0.0156) after two cycles of BEP. However, most patients remained positive. Pre-chemotherapy miRNA-371 levels correlated significantly with initial tumor size (Spearman r=0,8239, p=0.0001), while post-chemotherapy levels showed no correlation with residual tumor size (Spearman r=-0.01425, p=0.9645). CONCLUSIONS: MiRNA-371 levels decrease significantly after BEP chemotherapy in patients with seminoma and non-seminomatous germ cell tumor. Our findings support the role of miRNA-371 as a potential biomarker for monitoring disease activity and treatment response in germ cell tumors.

title: HOW RELIABLE ARE SERUM TUMOR MARKERS IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF SMALL TESTICULAR MASSES? A MULTICENTRIC ANALYSIS FROM THE MILAN TESTIS CANCER ALLIANCE
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Christian Corsini, Massimiliano Raffo, Sebastiano Nazzani, Carlo Silvani, Elio Mazzone, Sofia Giudici, Paolo Dell’Oglio, Luca Boeri, Federica Passarelli, Ludovico M. Basadonna, Giuseppe Garofano, Marco Paciotti, Giovanni Lughezzani, Andrea Triggiani, Giuseppe Fallara, Matteo Ferro, Francesco Montorsi, Andrea Salonia, Marco Bandini
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The diagnostic value of serum tumor markers (STM) (i. e., AFP, hCG, LDH) in men with testicular germ cell cancer is well established in advanced disease, but their role in the assessment of small testicular masses remains uncertain. We aimed to i) explore the relationship between tumor size and both biochemical and ultrasound (US) markers; and, ii) develop a model for discriminating benign from malignant lesions. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 497 men who underwent surgery for testicular masses at six academic centers (2020–2024). Baseline characteristics, US features (vascularity, echogenicity, microcalcifications, dimensions), and preoperative STM were retrospectively collected. Descriptive statistics compared benign and malignant tumors at final pathology. Tumor size–marker relationships were modeled using natural spline regression by histology, and a regression tree identified key predictors of malignancy. RESULTS: Of 497, 66 (13%) patients had benign and 431 (87%) patients malignant lesions. Median tumor size was larger in malignant masses (26 \[16–42\] vs 14 \[7–20\] mm; p<0.001). Serum markers were higher in malignant cases: AFP 2.3 \[1.3–9.9\] vs 1.66 \[0.23–3.5\] ng/mL (p=0.0027), β-hCG 1.4 \[0.19–9\] vs 0.35 \[0.005–2.3\] IU/L (p=0.004), and LDH 187 \[148–262\] vs 134 \[0–184\] U/L (p<0.001). Malignant lesions were more often hypoechoic (90% vs 73%; p<0.001) and hyper-vascularized (58% vs 38%; p=0.001), but did not differ in terms of microcalcifications compared to benign lesions (16% vs 11%; p=0.3). Marker levels correlated weakly with lesion size, particularly in small lesions (<20 mm), where benign masses occasionally showed rising values. Malignant lesions exhibited consistent marker elevation only beyond this threshold (Figure). The regression tree achieved high diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.9), identifying echogenicity and microcalcifications as key discriminants, while vascularity was not predictive of malignancy ( Figure). CONCLUSIONS: In small testicular masses, tumor markers alone are unreliable for predicting malignancy. A “gray zone” exists below 20 mm, where marker trends are inconsistent and benign lesions may mimic malignant profiles. Integrating ultrasound parameters provides improved diagnostic discrimination in this challenging setting.

title: ASSOCIATION OF AREA DEPRIVATION INDEX WITH TESTICULAR CANCER DIAGNOSIS AND OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY NORTH AMERICAN COHORT
session: Penile & Testicular Cancer I (IP13)
authors: Mohit Butaney, Silvia Viganò, Anna Tylecki, Alessandro Bertini, Alessio Finocchiaro, Carlo Silvani, Alfonso Santangelo, Bassel Salka, Shane Tinsley, Alex Stephens, Jack Considine, Akshay Sood, Alberto Briganti, Francesco Montorsi, Emanuele Montanari, Nicola Nicolai, Craig Rogers, Mani Menon, Firas Abdollah
abstract_text: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: While current testicular management has led to impressive 5-year survival rates in patients, the incidence continues to increase and its disproportionate effect on younger patients leads to several long-term effects. Socioeconomic status and race have often been correlated to cancer outcomes but the underlying cause of these disparities is complex and multifactorial making them challenging to understand. The Area of Deprivation Index(ADI) could offer a distinctive and valuable metric for measuring the impact of socioeconomic factors. Our study examined the impact of ADI on Testicular Cancer(TCa) diagnosis and outcomes in a contemporary North American population. METHODS: The Michigan Department of health and Human Services (MDHHS) database was used to obtain data regarding patients with testicular cancer between 2004-2019. ADI was assigned to each patient dependent upon their residential census-block group and ranked as a percentile of deprivation relative to the national level. We stratified the cohort into quartiles based on national ADI-values, where the fourth quartile(75-100) represented the most disadvantageous socio-economic status. The main outcomes were TCa stage at diagnosis, all-cause mortality, and cancer-specific mortality. RESULTS: We analyzed 2,848 patients (94% NHW) with median age of 34 years (IQR 27-43). Among those, 10.3%, 29.7%, 32.9%, and 27.1% were in the first, second, third and fourth ADI-quartile respectively.
